courses.title: Basic Electronics
topics: Semiconductor physics: energy bands, carriers, n and p material
Diodes: bias, V-I curve, Zener, rectifiers, filters, regulated supplies, clippers, clampers, multipliers, datasheets
BJT: operation, CE/CB/CC, load line, biasing, thermal stability, switching
Digital circuits: gates, diode gates, logic families RTL/DTL/TTL/CMOS
RLC circuits series and parallel
Signals: continuous/discrete, even/odd, periodic, power/energy
courses.description: From the physics of silicon to working amplifier and logic circuits, with every circuit built, measured and simulated rather than only drawn. Taught to the depth of a first-year engineering circuits course, with every circuit simulated and measured.
modelledOn: Sedra and Smith, Microelectronic Circuits
Agarwal and Lang, Foundations of Analog and Digital Electronic Circuits
Boylestad and Nashelsky, Electronic Devices and Circuit Theory
outcomes: Analyse DC and AC circuits with Kirchhoff's laws, node and mesh analysis, Thevenin and Norton equivalents.
Explain how carriers move in doped silicon and derive the diode and transistor V-I behaviour from it.
Design rectifiers, regulators, clippers and clampers and predict their waveforms.
Bias a BJT amplifier for stable operation and compute its gain, input and output resistance.
Analyse RLC circuits in the time and frequency domains and read resonance and bandwidth from a plot.
Classify signals and relate the continuous and discrete views of them to later signal processing courses.

syllabus.title: Circuit fundamentals and lab practice
topics: Charge, current, voltage, power and energy; passive sign convention
Resistors, Ohm's law, series and parallel combinations, voltage and current dividers
Kirchhoff's current and voltage laws; node-voltage and mesh-current analysis
Superposition, Thevenin and Norton equivalents, maximum power transfer
Using a breadboard, multimeter, oscilloscope and bench supply; reading a datasheet
Dependent sources and the ideal operational amplifier as a circuit element

syllabus.title: Semiconductor physics
topics: Energy bands in conductors, insulators and semiconductors; band gap of silicon and germanium
Intrinsic carriers, electrons and holes; temperature dependence
Doping: donors and acceptors, n-type and p-type material, majority and minority carriers
Drift and diffusion currents; mobility and conductivity
The p-n junction at equilibrium: depletion region, built-in potential

syllabus.title: Diodes and diode circuits
topics: Forward and reverse bias; the diode equation and the V-I curve; ideal, constant-drop and piecewise models
Zener breakdown and avalanche; Zener regulators and line/load regulation
Half-wave, full-wave centre-tap and bridge rectifiers; ripple and capacitor filters
Regulated DC supplies: transformer, rectifier, filter, regulator (78xx and LM317)
Clippers, clampers and voltage multipliers; LED and photodiode circuits
Reading a diode datasheet: PIV, forward drop, maximum current, recovery time

syllabus.title: Bipolar junction transistors
topics: NPN and PNP structure and operation; active, saturation and cut-off regions; alpha and beta
Common-emitter, common-base and common-collector configurations and their characteristics
DC load line and Q-point; fixed, emitter and voltage-divider biasing; bias stability and thermal runaway
Small-signal model (hybrid-pi) and the gain, input and output resistance of a CE amplifier
The transistor as a switch: driving an LED, a relay and a small DC motor
Introduction to MOSFETs: enhancement-mode NMOS and PMOS, threshold voltage, regions of operation

syllabus.title: Operational amplifiers
topics: Ideal op-amp rules; inverting, non-inverting, summing and difference amplifiers
Integrators, differentiators and active filters
Comparators, Schmitt triggers and simple oscillators
Real op-amp limits: offset, slew rate, gain-bandwidth product

syllabus.title: Digital circuits and logic families
topics: Voltage levels, noise margins and the transfer characteristic of an inverter
Diode logic AND and OR gates and why they cannot be cascaded
RTL, DTL and TTL gate construction; totem-pole output; fan-out and propagation delay
CMOS inverter, NAND and NOR; static and dynamic power
Interfacing logic families and level shifting; open-collector and tri-state outputs

syllabus.title: Capacitors, inductors and RLC circuits
topics: Capacitor and inductor V-I relations; energy storage; RC and RL transients and time constants
Sinusoidal steady state: phasors, impedance and admittance
Series and parallel RLC circuits: resonance frequency, quality factor, bandwidth
Frequency response and Bode plots; low-pass, high-pass and band-pass filters
Second-order transients: underdamped, critically damped and overdamped responses

syllabus.title: Signals
topics: Continuous-time and discrete-time signals; sampling as the bridge between them
Even and odd decomposition; periodic and aperiodic signals
Energy and power signals; RMS value of common waveforms
Standard signals: impulse, step, ramp, exponential and sinusoid
Reading a signal on an oscilloscope: amplitude, period, frequency, phase, DC offset

courses.title: Biochemistry and Cell Biology for Computing
topics: Amino acids, proteins and levels of structure
Enzyme kinetics and curve fitting
Metabolic pathways and energy flow
Membranes, transport and cell signalling
Cell cycle, division and cancer basics
Gene expression and its regulation at the cell level
Laboratory techniques and the data they produce
courses.description: The chemistry and cell biology a computing student needs before bioinformatics: proteins, enzymes, metabolism, membranes, the cell cycle and gene regulation. In the lab students fit enzyme kinetics, simulate pathways and signalling, and interpret the data that wet-lab techniques produce.
modelledOn: Nelson and Cox, Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry
Alberts et al., Molecular Biology of the Cell
Berg, Tymoczko and Stryer, Biochemistry
outcomes: Describe the structure of amino acids and proteins and explain how sequence determines folding and function.
Fit Michaelis-Menten and inhibition models to enzyme data and interpret the kinetic parameters.
Trace carbon and energy through glycolysis, the citric acid cycle and oxidative phosphorylation, and model a small pathway as a system of equations.
Explain membrane transport, cell signalling, the cell cycle and the origins of cancer in terms of molecular mechanisms.
Model gene regulation with simple dynamical and Boolean networks and interpret the output of common laboratory assays.

syllabus.title: Chemistry of life
topics: Atoms, covalent and non-covalent bonds; water as solvent and hydrogen bonding
Acids, bases, pH and buffers; the Henderson-Hasselbalch equation
Functional groups and the four classes of biomolecule: carbohydrates, lipids, proteins, nucleic acids
Thermodynamics of reactions: free energy, enthalpy, entropy and equilibrium constants
Coupled reactions and the role of ATP as an energy currency

syllabus.title: Amino acids, proteins and structure
topics: The 20 amino acids: side-chain classes, charge, pKa and isoelectric point
The peptide bond, backbone angles and the Ramachandran plot
Levels of structure: primary, secondary (alpha helix, beta sheet), tertiary and quaternary
Protein folding, the hydrophobic effect, chaperones and misfolding diseases
Haemoglobin and myoglobin: oxygen binding, cooperativity and sickle cell disease
Protein databases and formats: UniProt entries and PDB files as data

syllabus.title: Enzymes and kinetics
topics: How enzymes lower activation energy; active sites, cofactors and specificity
Michaelis-Menten kinetics: derivation, Km, Vmax and kcat
Linearised plots versus non-linear least-squares curve fitting
Competitive, uncompetitive and non-competitive inhibition; drug action
Allosteric enzymes, the Hill equation and feedback regulation
Enzyme assays: progress curves, initial rates, replicates and error bars

syllabus.title: Metabolism and energy flow
topics: Catabolism and anabolism; the major pathways as a network
Glycolysis: ten steps, regulation by phosphofructokinase, net ATP and NADH
Pyruvate oxidation and the citric acid cycle
Electron transport and oxidative phosphorylation; the proton gradient and ATP synthase
Gluconeogenesis, glycogen and fat metabolism; hormonal control by insulin and glucagon
Pathways as stoichiometric matrices; steady state and an introduction to flux balance

syllabus.title: Membranes, transport and cell signalling
topics: Membrane structure: the fluid mosaic, lipid bilayers and membrane proteins
Passive diffusion, facilitated transport and active transport; the sodium-potassium pump
Membrane potential: the Nernst and Goldman equations; the action potential
Receptors, G proteins, kinase cascades and second messengers
Signalling as an information network: amplification, feedback and crosstalk

syllabus.title: Cell structure, the cell cycle and cancer
topics: Prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells; organelles and the cytoskeleton
The cell cycle: phases, cyclins, CDKs and checkpoints
Mitosis and meiosis; chromosomes, crossing over and the origin of genetic variation
Apoptosis and the control of cell number
Cancer: oncogenes, tumour suppressors (p53, RB) and the multi-hit model
Cancer in Ghana and Africa: cervical, breast and liver cancer, screening and vaccination

syllabus.title: Gene expression and its regulation
topics: The central dogma; DNA structure, replication and repair
Transcription in bacteria and the lac operon as a switch
Eukaryotic transcription: promoters, enhancers, transcription factors and chromatin
RNA processing: capping, splicing, polyadenylation and alternative splicing
Translation: the genetic code, ribosomes, tRNA and mutations
Epigenetics: DNA methylation and histone modification
Gene regulatory networks: Boolean and differential-equation models of switches and oscillators

syllabus.title: Laboratory techniques and the data they produce
topics: Spectrophotometry and the Beer-Lambert law; standard curves
PCR and quantitative PCR: amplification curves, Ct values and relative expression
Gel electrophoresis and Western blotting: reading bands and sizing fragments
Sequencing, microarrays and mass spectrometry: what each assay measures and its noise
Experimental design: controls, replicates, batch effects and reproducibility

courses.title: Discrete Mathematics
topics: Set theory and binary operations
Number systems
Functions and relations
Sequence and series
Induction and recursion
Graph theory
Logic
Boolean algebra
courses.description: The mathematics that computer science is written in: logic, proof, sets, relations, counting, number theory and graphs, taught by proving and computing rather than memorising. Taught to the depth of the standard mathematics-for-computer-science course, with every proof technique practised on real problems.
modelledOn: Rosen, Discrete Mathematics and Its Applications
Lehman, Leighton and Meyer, Mathematics for Computer Science
Epp, Discrete Mathematics with Applications
outcomes: Translate English statements into propositional and predicate logic and check validity with truth tables and inference rules.
Write correct proofs by direct argument, contrapositive, contradiction, cases and induction, including strong and structural induction.
Work fluently with sets, functions and relations, and prove properties such as injectivity, equivalence and partial order.
Count arrangements with permutations, combinations, the pigeonhole principle and inclusion-exclusion, and solve recurrences.
Apply modular arithmetic, GCD and the Chinese remainder theorem, including to RSA.
Model problems as graphs and reason about paths, trees, colourings and planarity.

syllabus.title: Propositional and predicate logic
topics: Propositions, connectives, truth tables, tautologies and contradictions
Logical equivalence, De Morgan's laws, conditional and biconditional, converse and contrapositive
Rules of inference: modus ponens, modus tollens, resolution; valid and invalid arguments
Predicates and quantifiers; nested quantifiers; negating quantified statements
Normal forms (CNF, DNF) and satisfiability; logic puzzles

syllabus.title: Proof techniques
topics: Axioms, definitions, theorems, lemmas; what a proof is and is not
Direct proof, proof by contrapositive, proof by contradiction, proof by cases
Existence and uniqueness proofs; counterexamples
Common errors: circular reasoning, proving the converse, division by zero
Proof that the square root of 2 is irrational; infinitude of primes

syllabus.title: Sets, functions and relations
topics: Set notation, subsets, power sets, Cartesian products; set operations and identities; Venn diagrams
Binary operations on sets; closure, associativity, commutativity, identity and inverse
Functions: domain, codomain, image; injective, surjective, bijective; composition and inverse
Relations: reflexive, symmetric, antisymmetric, transitive; equivalence relations and partitions
Partial orders, Hasse diagrams, lattices; closures of relations
Cardinality: countable and uncountable sets, Cantor's diagonal argument

syllabus.title: Number systems and number theory
topics: Integers, rationals, reals; positional number systems and base conversion
Divisibility, primes, the fundamental theorem of arithmetic
The division algorithm, Euclid's algorithm, extended Euclid and Bezout's identity
Modular arithmetic, congruences, inverses mod n; Fermat's little theorem and Euler's theorem
Chinese remainder theorem; RSA encryption as an application
Representing integers and floating-point numbers in a computer

syllabus.title: Sequences, series, induction and recursion
topics: Sequences and summation notation; arithmetic and geometric series; telescoping sums
Weak and strong induction; well-ordering principle; common induction mistakes
Recursive definitions of sequences, sets and functions; structural induction
Solving linear recurrences: characteristic equations, Fibonacci closed form
Recursive algorithms and proving them correct; towers of Hanoi, merge sort recurrence
Asymptotic notation: big-O, big-Omega, big-Theta

syllabus.title: Counting and combinatorics
topics: Sum and product rules; permutations and combinations; binomial theorem and Pascal's triangle
Pigeonhole principle and its generalisation
Inclusion-exclusion; derangements
Counting with repetition; stars and bars; distributing objects into boxes
Introduction to discrete probability: sample spaces, events, conditional probability

syllabus.title: Boolean algebra
topics: Boolean algebra as a mathematical structure; axioms and duality
Boolean functions, truth tables, sum-of-products and product-of-sums expressions
Simplification with identities and Karnaugh maps
Logic gates and circuits as Boolean expressions; functional completeness of NAND
Boolean algebra and set algebra as the same lattice

syllabus.title: Graph theory
topics: Graphs, digraphs, multigraphs; degree, handshaking lemma; adjacency matrix and list
Paths, cycles, connectivity, components; Euler circuits and Hamiltonian cycles
Trees, spanning trees, rooted trees; properties and counting of trees
Shortest paths with Dijkstra; minimum spanning trees with Kruskal and Prim
Graph colouring, chromatic number, bipartite graphs and matching
Planar graphs and Euler's formula; modelling road networks and timetables as graphs

courses.title: Economics for Technology and Business
topics: Demand, supply and elasticity
Costs and market structures

Pricing of digital goods and services

Economics of IT investment and cloud pricing
courses.description: The economics a technologist needs: markets, costs, competition, platforms, digital pricing, incentives, the macroeconomy and the business case for IT spending. Students fit demand curves, simulate platform adoption, price digital products and argue investment cases in scenarios drawn from Ghana and the wider continent.
modelledOn: Mankiw, Principles of Economics
Shapiro and Varian, Information Rules: A Strategic Guide to the Network Economy
Parker, Van Alstyne and Choudary, Platform Revolution
Brealey, Myers and Allen, Principles of Corporate Finance (investment appraisal chapters)
outcomes: Explain market outcomes with demand, supply, elasticity and surplus, and predict the effect of a price control, tax or subsidy.
Derive cost curves and profit-maximising output, and compare competitive, monopolistic and oligopolistic markets using simple game models.
Model network effects and two-sided platforms, and simulate how adoption tips toward one provider.
Design and evaluate pricing schemes for digital goods, including versioning, subscriptions and auctions.
Read macroeconomic indicators and trace how inflation, interest rates and exchange rates affect technology organisations.
Build and defend a quantified investment case for an IT or cloud project using net present value and sensitivity analysis.

syllabus.title: Scarcity, demand and supply
topics: Scarcity, opportunity cost, the production possibility frontier and comparative advantage
The demand curve, its determinants, and movements along versus shifts of the curve
The supply curve, its determinants, market equilibrium and comparative statics
Consumer and producer surplus; efficiency of competitive markets
Price elasticity of demand and supply (arc and point), income and cross elasticity, the total revenue test
Price ceilings, floors, taxes and subsidies: incidence and deadweight loss, with fuel and cocoa price examples

syllabus.title: Production, costs and market structures
topics: Production function, diminishing marginal returns, short run versus long run
Fixed, variable, marginal and average cost curves; economies and diseconomies of scale
Perfect competition: profit maximisation at MR = MC, the shutdown rule, long-run equilibrium
Monopoly: marginal revenue, deadweight loss, natural monopoly and regulation
Oligopoly: Cournot and Bertrand competition, kinked demand, cartels
Game theory basics: payoff matrices, dominant strategies, Nash equilibrium, the prisoner's dilemma

syllabus.title: Network effects and platform economics
topics: Direct and indirect network effects; Metcalfe's law and its critique; critical mass
Two-sided markets: cross-side effects, pricing structure, the chicken-and-egg problem
Switching costs, lock-in, multi-homing and compatibility
Tipping and winner-takes-most dynamics: positive feedback and adoption curves
Standards, interoperability and open versus closed platforms, with mobile money interoperability as a case

syllabus.title: Pricing of digital goods and services
topics: Zero marginal cost, high fixed cost and why digital goods differ from physical ones
Price discrimination: first, second and third degree; versioning and bundling
Freemium, subscriptions, advertising-funded and data-driven business models
Dynamic and surge pricing; first-price, second-price and ad auctions
Estimating willingness to pay and the revenue-maximising price from demand data
Data bundles and mobile money tariffs in Ghana: pricing under regulation

syllabus.title: Information, incentives and market failure
topics: Adverse selection: the market for lemons, screening and signalling
Moral hazard and principal-agent problems; contract and incentive design
Reputation and rating systems; trust in online marketplaces
Externalities and public goods: open source software and digital public infrastructure
Behavioural biases in decisions: anchoring, loss aversion and defaults in interface design

syllabus.title: Macroeconomic indicators and policy
topics: GDP by expenditure, income and output; real versus nominal; growth rates
Inflation, construction of the consumer price index, and measures of unemployment
Aggregate demand and supply; fiscal policy and the multiplier
Money, banking and monetary policy: policy rates and central bank tools
Exchange rates and the balance of payments: effect of cedi depreciation on imported IT equipment
Growth, productivity and the digital economy; development indicators

syllabus.title: Economics of IT investment and cloud pricing
topics: Total cost of ownership; capital versus operating expenditure
Net present value, internal rate of return, payback and discounting for IT projects
Cloud pricing models (on-demand, reserved, spot) and the break-even against on-premise hardware
Risk and real options in technology investment; sensitivity and scenario analysis
Measuring returns: the productivity paradox and benefit realisation

syllabus.title: Policy, regulation and the economic case
topics: Competition policy and platform regulation: market power, mergers, data portability
Transaction levies on mobile money and their incidence on users and providers
Digital inclusion and development: mobile money, savings, remittances and farm-gate prices
Capstone: a written economic case with cost-benefit analysis for a Ghanaian digital service

courses.title: Fundamentals of Computer Science
topics: Overview of the computer
Information management
Files and databases
Computer networks, Internet and the Web
Technology and society
Computer safety and ethics
courses.description: A whole-degree tour of what a computer is, how information is represented and moved, and what computing does to society, so that every later course has a map to hang on. Taught to the depth of a leading introductory computer science survey, with hands-on exercises for every idea.
modelledOn: Brookshear and Brylow, Computer Science: An Overview
Schneider and Gersting, Invitation to Computer Science
Petzold, Code: The Hidden Language of Computer Hardware and Software
outcomes: Describe the parts of a computer and trace how a program and its data move from storage to processor and back.
Represent text, numbers, images and sound in binary and estimate storage and bandwidth needs.
Explain what algorithms, programs, operating systems and compilers are and how they fit together.
Organise information in files, spreadsheets and relational databases and query it.
Explain how the Internet and the Web work end to end, from a URL to a rendered page.
Reason about safety, privacy, ethics and the social impact of computing with Ghanaian and global examples.

syllabus.title: What computing is
topics: History of computing: from the abacus and Babbage to the transistor, the microprocessor and the smartphone
Computational thinking: decomposition, abstraction, patterns, algorithms
Hardware, software, data and people as the parts of a computing system
Kinds of computers: embedded, mobile, personal, server, supercomputer, cloud

syllabus.title: Representing information
topics: Bits and bytes; binary, hexadecimal; units from kilobyte to petabyte
Integers and two's complement; floating point and why 0.1 + 0.2 is not 0.3
Text: ASCII, Unicode and UTF-8; representing Twi and other Ghanaian languages
Images (pixels, colour depth, compression), sound (sampling, bit depth) and video
Compression: run-length, Huffman and the difference between lossless and lossy
Error detection: parity and checksums

syllabus.title: Inside the computer
topics: Logic gates and how they add; the processor, registers, clock and the fetch-decode-execute cycle
Memory hierarchy: registers, cache, RAM, SSD, hard disk, cloud storage
Input and output devices, buses and ports
Machine code, assembly, high-level languages, compilers and interpreters
Operating systems: what they do for programs and users; processes and files

syllabus.title: Algorithms and programs
topics: Algorithms as precise procedures; pseudocode and flowcharts
Sequence, selection and iteration; variables and data types
Searching and sorting by hand: linear search, binary search, bubble and selection sort
Why some algorithms are faster: counting steps, growth with input size
Writing and running short programs in Scratch and Python to see the ideas work
Software: system software, application software, open source, licences

syllabus.title: Information management, files and databases
topics: Data, information and knowledge; data quality and data life cycle
File systems, folders, file formats, metadata; backup and archiving
Spreadsheets for data: formulas, sorting, filtering, charts
Relational databases: tables, keys, relationships; simple SQL SELECT queries
Database applications: student records, mobile money ledgers, hospital systems
Big data and data centres: what changes at scale

syllabus.title: Computer networks, the Internet and the Web
topics: LANs, WANs, Wi-Fi, mobile data; switches and routers
IP addresses, DNS, packets and the layered model in plain terms
What happens when you type a URL: HTTP, HTML, CSS, JavaScript, servers and browsers
Email, cloud services, content delivery and why pages load slowly on poor links
Submarine cables and Ghana's connectivity; data costs and digital inclusion
Building a one-page website

syllabus.title: Computer safety, security and ethics
topics: Threats: malware, phishing, mobile money scams, social engineering
Passwords, two-factor authentication, encryption and HTTPS in plain terms
Personal data, privacy and Ghana's Data Protection Act
Professional ethics and the ACM Code; plagiarism and academic integrity
Safe and healthy computer use

syllabus.title: Technology and society
topics: Computing in Ghana and Africa: mobile money, agritech, e-government, health informatics
Automation, AI and the future of work; the digital divide
Environmental cost of computing: energy, e-waste at Agbogbloshie
Careers and the map of the computer science degree ahead

courses.title: Human Anatomy, Physiology and Clinical Terminology
topics: Body systems and their functions
Common diseases and how they present
Clinical vocabulary and medical word roots
Diagnoses, procedures and laboratory tests
Medications and pharmacology basics
Vital signs and clinical measurements
Reading a clinical note and chart
courses.description: The body systems, how they fail, and the language clinicians use to describe them, taught for future health informaticians who must read and code clinical records. Students step through physiology processes, decode terms and notes, query lab results and work branching patient cases drawn from Ghanaian health practice.
modelledOn: Tortora and Derrickson, Principles of Anatomy and Physiology
Chabner, The Language of Medicine
World Health Organization, ICD-10 and ICD-11 classification and the Model List of Essential Medicines
Bickley, Bates' Guide to Physical Examination and History Taking
outcomes: Describe the structure and function of the major body systems and explain how homeostasis is maintained.
Build, split and interpret medical terms from word roots, prefixes and suffixes, and decode common abbreviations safely.
Explain how common diseases in Ghana present, are diagnosed with procedures and laboratory tests, and are classified for coding.
Describe how common drug classes act and calculate simple weight-based doses and half-life effects.
Measure, record and interpret vital signs and clinical measurements, including units, reference ranges and early warning scores.
Read a clinical note and chart end to end and extract the problems, medications, results and plan.

syllabus.title: Organisation of the body and the language of medicine
topics: Levels of organisation from cell to organism; homeostasis and negative and positive feedback
Anatomical position, body planes, directional terms and body cavities
Word roots, combining forms, prefixes and suffixes; building and splitting terms
Abbreviations, eponyms and error-prone shorthand; do-not-use lists
Spelling, pronunciation and plural forms of Greek and Latin terms

syllabus.title: Cardiovascular, blood and respiratory systems
topics: Heart anatomy, the cardiac cycle, the conduction system and the electrocardiogram
Blood vessels, blood pressure regulation and circulation
Blood: cells, haemoglobin, clotting, blood groups and sickle cell disease
Airways, lungs, ventilation and gas exchange
Lung volumes, oxygen transport and acid-base balance
Common diseases: hypertension, heart failure, anaemia, asthma, pneumonia and tuberculosis

syllabus.title: Digestive, renal, endocrine and reproductive systems
topics: Digestive tract and accessory organs; digestion and absorption
Liver function, metabolism and viral hepatitis
Kidney and nephron: filtration, fluid and electrolyte balance, urinary tract infection
Endocrine glands and hormones; insulin, glucose regulation and diabetes mellitus
Reproductive system, pregnancy, antenatal care and childbirth
Common diseases: peptic ulcer, cholera, typhoid, chronic kidney disease, thyroid disorders

syllabus.title: Nervous, musculoskeletal, skin and immune systems
topics: Brain, spinal cord, neurons, action potentials and reflexes
Special senses: eye, ear, taste and smell
Bones, joints and muscles; fractures and their healing
Skin structure, wound healing and burns
Immune system: innate and adaptive immunity, vaccines and HIV infection
Common diseases: stroke, epilepsy, meningitis, osteoporosis and skin infections

syllabus.title: Diseases, diagnoses, procedures and laboratory tests
topics: Disease processes: infection, inflammation, neoplasia and degeneration; malaria, tuberculosis, HIV and non-communicable diseases in Ghana
Symptoms, signs and syndromes; history taking and differential diagnosis
Diagnosis classification and coding with ICD-10, ICD-11 and SNOMED CT concepts
Imaging and procedures: X-ray, ultrasound, CT, MRI and endoscopy; procedure coding
Laboratory tests: full blood count, malaria rapid test, glucose, liver and kidney panels, urinalysis; reference ranges and LOINC

syllabus.title: Medications and pharmacology basics
topics: Drug names, classes and the essential medicines list; generic versus brand
Pharmacokinetics: absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion and half-life
Pharmacodynamics: receptors, dose-response curves and the therapeutic index
Routes, dosage forms, weight-based dose calculation and prescription abbreviations
Adverse reactions, interactions, allergies, counterfeit medicines and pharmacovigilance

syllabus.title: Vital signs and clinical measurements
topics: Temperature, pulse, respiratory rate, blood pressure and oxygen saturation
Anthropometry: height, weight, BMI, growth charts and mid-upper arm circumference
Early warning scores and triage categories
Units, reference ranges and conversions such as mg/dL and mmol/L; device error and data quality
Consciousness and pain: Glasgow coma scale and pain scales

syllabus.title: Reading a clinical note and chart
topics: SOAP note structure: history, examination, assessment and plan
Medication charts, orders and administration records
Referral letters, discharge summaries and the problem list
Decoding a complete chart end to end, with confidentiality of patient records

courses.title: Introduction to Robotics
topics: What a robot is and its components
Actuators and motors
Sensors and signal conditioning
Microcontroller programming
Basic feedback control
Building a mobile robot
Team robot challenge
courses.description: A hands-on first course in robotics: how robots sense, decide and move, from a single motor to a team-built mobile robot. Students wire motors and sensors on the hardware bench, program a microcontroller, tune feedback loops and finish with a robot challenge.
modelledOn: Siegwart, Nourbakhsh and Scaramuzza, Introduction to Autonomous Mobile Robots
Mataric, The Robotics Primer
Dudek and Jenkin, Computational Principles of Mobile Robotics
Arduino and AVR microcontroller documentation
outcomes: Describe a robot as a sense-plan-act system and draw the block diagram of a given robot.
Select, drive and size DC, servo and stepper motors for a given load using PWM and an H-bridge.
Choose, calibrate and filter sensors, and convert raw readings to physical units.
Program a microcontroller with digital and analog I/O, timers, interrupts and state machines.
Implement and tune proportional and PID feedback controllers for speed, position and line following.
Build, test and demonstrate a mobile robot as part of a team, documenting design decisions and safety measures.

syllabus.title: What a robot is and its components
topics: Definitions and history; types of robot (arm, mobile, legged, aerial) and levels of autonomy
Components of a robot: structure, actuators, sensors, controller and power, and the sense-plan-act loop
Degrees of freedom, joints, workspace and a first look at the geometry of a two-link arm
Robots in Africa: farm spraying, mining inspection, medical drone delivery and the safety and ethics questions they raise
Electronics for robots: voltage, current, Ohm's law, power budget and battery selection

syllabus.title: Actuators and motors
topics: The brushed DC motor: torque, speed, back-EMF and stall current
H-bridge drivers and PWM speed control; reversing direction
Hobby servo motors: pulse widths, position control and range limits
Stepper motors: full, half and micro-stepping, steps per revolution, open-loop positioning
Gearboxes, the torque-speed trade-off, wheel size and motor power sizing
Motor driver protection: flyback diodes, current limits and electrical noise

syllabus.title: Sensors and signal conditioning
topics: Sensor characteristics: range, resolution, accuracy, precision, noise and response time
Light, line and proximity sensing: infrared reflectance, ultrasonic ranging, time of flight
Quadrature encoders: counting ticks, speed estimation and wheel odometry
Inertial sensing: accelerometer, gyroscope, IMU and gyro drift
Analog conditioning: voltage dividers, op-amp amplifiers, the ADC and quantisation error
Digital filtering: moving average, exponential low-pass and median filters for spikes

syllabus.title: Microcontroller programming
topics: Microcontroller architecture (AVR): GPIO, timers, ADC and interrupts
Digital I/O, analog read and PWM output: buttons, LEDs and motor speed
Reading sensors, serial debugging and calibration routines
Timers and interrupts: non-blocking loops and encoder interrupt handlers
Behaviour as a finite state machine in code
A single-board computer in the loop: serial, I2C and MQTT messaging between boards

syllabus.title: Basic feedback control
topics: Open loop versus closed loop; setpoint, error and actuator saturation
On-off control with hysteresis
Proportional control and steady-state error
PID control: integral windup, derivative kick and discrete-time implementation
Step-response tuning: rise time, overshoot, settling time and the Ziegler-Nichols rules
Line following and wall following as feedback problems

syllabus.title: Mobile robot motion and navigation
topics: Differential-drive kinematics: wheel speeds to forward and turning velocity
Odometry and dead reckoning; how errors accumulate
Reactive obstacle avoidance and Braitenberg-style behaviours
Grid maps and path search: breadth-first search and A-star on an occupancy grid
Behaviour-based control: subsumption and behaviour arbitration

syllabus.title: Building a mobile robot
topics: Requirements, chassis design, wheel placement and centre of mass
Wiring, power distribution and subsystem testing
Integration, test plans and debugging with logs
Safety: emergency stop, fail-safe states and battery handling

syllabus.title: Team robot challenge
topics: Challenge specification, scoring rules and project planning
Team roles, version control and design documentation
Demonstration, run analysis and failure review
Reflection: reliability, cost, ethics and local impact of the robot

courses.title: Molecular Biology for Computing
topics: Cells and biomolecules
DNA structure and replication
Transcription and translation
Genes, genomes and mutation
Proteins and their functions
Laboratory techniques that produce data
Biological databases
courses.description: The molecular biology a computer scientist needs to work with biological data: cells and biomolecules, DNA structure and replication, transcription and translation, genes, genomes and mutation, protein structure and function, the laboratory techniques that generate sequence and expression data, and the databases that store it. Assumes no prior biology and is taught through interactive simulations of molecules and processes and small programs that manipulate real sequences in the browser, at the depth of a first-year molecular biology course for quantitative students.
modelledOn: Alberts et al., Essential Cell Biology
Watson et al., Molecular Biology of the Gene
Lodish et al., Molecular Cell Biology
Zvelebil and Baum, Understanding Bioinformatics
outcomes: Describe the structure of cells and the main classes of biomolecules and explain how their chemistry determines their function.
Explain DNA structure, replication and repair and represent sequences and their operations as strings and algorithms.
Trace the flow of information from gene to protein through transcription, RNA processing and translation, and implement it in code.
Classify mutations and genomic variation and predict their effects, using sickle cell disease and drug-resistant malaria as worked examples.
Relate protein structure to function and describe how enzymes, receptors and antibodies work.
Explain how sequencing, PCR, microarrays and other laboratory techniques produce data and retrieve and interpret records from biological databases.

syllabus.title: Cells and biomolecules
topics: Why computing needs biology: genomics, drug discovery, epidemiology and precision medicine
Prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells; organelles; membranes and transport; viruses as a special case
Chemistry of life: water, bonds, pH; carbohydrates, lipids, nucleic acids and proteins
Energy and metabolism in outline: enzymes, ATP, respiration and photosynthesis
The cell cycle, mitosis and meiosis; how traits are inherited

syllabus.title: DNA structure and replication
topics: Nucleotides, the double helix, base pairing, antiparallel strands and 5' to 3' direction
Chromosomes, chromatin, histones and packaging; genome sizes across organisms
Semi-conservative replication: helicase, polymerases, primers, leading and lagging strands, Okazaki fragments
Replication errors, proofreading and DNA repair pathways
DNA as data: alphabets, reverse complements, GC content and k-mers written as small programs

syllabus.title: Transcription and translation
topics: The central dogma and its exceptions: reverse transcription in HIV, RNA viruses
Transcription: promoters, RNA polymerase, transcription factors, termination
RNA processing in eukaryotes: capping, polyadenylation, splicing and alternative splicing
The genetic code: codons, reading frames, start and stop codons, codon usage; translating sequences in code
Translation: ribosomes, tRNA, initiation, elongation, termination; post-translational modification
Gene regulation: operons, enhancers, epigenetics and non-coding RNAs in outline

syllabus.title: Genes, genomes and mutation
topics: Gene structure: exons, introns, untranslated regions, regulatory regions; genome organisation and repeats
Types of mutation: substitutions, insertions, deletions, frameshifts, copy number and structural variants
Sickle cell disease: the single substitution in the beta-globin gene, inheritance patterns and its prevalence in West Africa
Malaria and human genetics: the sickle cell trait, G6PD deficiency and balancing selection
Pathogen genomes: Plasmodium falciparum, drug-resistance mutations and genomic surveillance
Population genetics in brief: alleles, Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium, African genetic diversity

syllabus.title: Proteins and their functions
topics: Amino acids and their properties; peptide bonds
Levels of structure: primary, secondary, tertiary and quaternary; folding and misfolding
Haemoglobin and how one amino acid change causes sickling
Enzymes and kinetics in outline; inhibitors and drug targets such as antimalarials
Antibodies, receptors and signalling; vaccines and the immune response
Predicting and visualising protein structure; the impact of structure prediction models

syllabus.title: Laboratory techniques that produce data
topics: Extraction, gel electrophoresis, restriction enzymes and cloning
PCR and quantitative PCR; rapid diagnostic tests for malaria and their limits
Sanger sequencing and next-generation sequencing: reads, quality scores, FASTQ files, coverage; long-read and portable sequencing
Measuring expression: microarrays and RNA-seq; mass spectrometry for proteins
Genome editing with CRISPR-Cas9 and its ethical questions
Sources of error and noise in experimental data; replicates and controls

syllabus.title: Biological databases
topics: Sequence formats: FASTA, GenBank and FASTQ; parsing them with code
Primary databases: GenBank, ENA and DDBJ; UniProt for proteins and the Protein Data Bank for structures
Genome browsers, Ensembl and variant databases such as dbSNP and ClinVar
Searching with BLAST and interpreting a result; ontologies such as the Gene Ontology
Data sharing, consent and benefit-sharing in African genomics research; capstone: annotate a malaria parasite gene from database records

courses.title: Principles of Programming
topics: Programming concepts and terminologies (LLL, HLL, translators)
Algorithms, pseudo-code, flowcharts
Character set, constants, data types, variables, operators, expressions
Flow control: if, if-else, switch, while, do-while, for
Basic object-oriented concepts
Identifying and fixing errors
courses.description: First contact with programming: thinking in algorithms, writing them as pseudocode and flowcharts, then as real code with variables, control flow, functions and a first look at objects. Taught to the depth of a leading first programming course, with a working program every week.
modelledOn: Zelle, Python Programming: An Introduction to Computer Science
Guttag, Introduction to Computation and Programming
Roberts, The Art and Science of Java
outcomes: Explain how source code becomes a running program and the roles of compilers, interpreters and linkers.
Design an algorithm for a stated problem and express it as pseudocode and a flowchart before coding.
Write programs that use variables, expressions, selection and loops correctly, and trace them by hand.
Decompose a program into functions with clear parameters and return values.
Explain objects, classes, attributes and methods and use simple objects in a program.
Find and fix syntax, runtime and logic errors with a systematic debugging method and tests.

syllabus.title: Programs, languages and translators
topics: What a program is; machine code, low-level and high-level languages; why there are many languages
Compilers, interpreters, assemblers and linkers; the edit-run-debug loop
Setting up an editor and running a first program; printing and reading input
Programming vocabulary: source, syntax, semantics, statement, expression, bug

syllabus.title: Algorithms, pseudocode and flowcharts
topics: Properties of an algorithm: finite, definite, effective; inputs and outputs
Pseudocode conventions; flowchart symbols for process, decision, loop, input/output
Tracing an algorithm with a trace table
Everyday algorithms: making change in cedis, computing a GPA, finding the largest of three numbers
From flowchart to code and back

syllabus.title: Data: character set, constants, types, variables
topics: Character set, identifiers, keywords and naming rules
Literals and constants; integer, floating-point, character, string and boolean types
Variables, declaration, assignment and memory as named boxes
Type conversion and casting; integer division and rounding surprises
Input, output and formatting numbers and strings

syllabus.title: Operators and expressions
topics: Arithmetic, relational, logical, assignment and increment operators
Precedence and associativity; evaluating expressions by hand
Boolean expressions and short-circuit evaluation
Common expression errors: off-by-one, mixing types, confusing = and ==

syllabus.title: Selection
topics: if, if-else, else-if ladders and nested ifs
switch statements and when to prefer them
Designing conditions: grade bands, tax brackets, leap years
Testing every branch; boundary values

syllabus.title: Iteration
topics: while, do-while and for loops; loop variable, condition, update
Counting, summing, averaging and finding maxima in a loop
Sentinel-controlled and flag-controlled loops; break and continue
Nested loops: multiplication tables, patterns, simple matrices
Infinite loops and termination; choosing the right loop

syllabus.title: Functions and program structure
topics: Defining and calling functions; parameters, arguments, return values
Scope and lifetime of variables; local and global
Decomposition and stepwise refinement; top-down design
Library functions: maths, strings, random numbers
Introduction to recursion: factorial and Fibonacci

syllabus.title: Collections and strings
topics: Arrays and lists: indexing, traversal, searching, finding min and max
Strings as sequences of characters; common string operations
Reading and writing a simple text file
Simple sorting by hand: bubble sort and selection sort

syllabus.title: Basic object-oriented concepts
topics: Objects as data plus behaviour; classes as blueprints
Attributes and methods; creating and using objects
Encapsulation and why it matters; a Student or BankAccount class
Objects already met: strings, lists, files

syllabus.title: Identifying and fixing errors
topics: Syntax, runtime and logic errors and how each shows itself
Reading error messages and stack traces
Debugging strategy: reproduce, isolate, hypothesise, test; print statements and a debugger
Writing test cases before and after fixing; defensive input checking
Code style, comments and documentation

courses.title: Spreadsheet Analytics
topics: Organising data in tables
Formulas, references and functions
Lookup and logical functions
Pivot tables and summaries
Charts in spreadsheets
What-if analysis and goal seek
Building a simple business model
courses.description: Using spreadsheets to organise, analyse and model data: structured tables, formulas and references, lookup and logical functions, pivot tables, charts, descriptive statistics, what-if analysis with goal seek and Solver, and building a sound business model. Every skill is practised on real-looking local datasets in a spreadsheet that runs in the browser, with each exercise checked automatically for correct formulas as well as correct answers.
modelledOn: Winston, Microsoft Excel Data Analysis and Business Modeling
Powell and Baker, Business Analytics: The Art of Modeling with Spreadsheets
Ragsdale, Spreadsheet Modeling and Decision Analysis
Microsoft Office Specialist: Excel Expert certification
outcomes: Organise raw data into clean, validated tables suitable for analysis.
Write correct formulas with relative, absolute and mixed references and use statistical, text, date, lookup and logical functions.
Summarise and explore data with conditional aggregation, pivot tables and descriptive statistics.
Choose and build charts and simple dashboards that communicate findings honestly.
Perform what-if analysis with data tables, scenarios, goal seek and Solver.
Build, document and check a small business model that separates inputs, calculations and outputs.

syllabus.title: Organising data in tables
topics: Rows as records and columns as fields; one table per subject; avoiding merged cells and blank rows
Data types and formats: numbers, text, dates, currency in cedis and percentages
Structured tables and named ranges
Data validation with drop-down lists and input rules
Sorting, filtering, removing duplicates, text to columns and importing CSV files
Running dataset: a market trader's daily sales log

syllabus.title: Formulas, references and functions
topics: Operators and precedence; relative, absolute and mixed references
Mathematical and statistical functions: SUM, AVERAGE, MEDIAN, MIN, MAX, COUNT, COUNTA, ROUND
Text functions: LEFT, RIGHT, MID, LEN, TRIM, PROPER, CONCAT, TEXTJOIN; cleaning phone numbers
Date and time functions: TODAY, DATE, EOMONTH, NETWORKDAYS, DATEDIF
Dynamic arrays: FILTER, SORT, UNIQUE and SEQUENCE
Error values and formula auditing: trace precedents and dependents, evaluate formula

syllabus.title: Lookup and logical functions
topics: IF, nested IF, IFS, AND, OR, NOT and IFERROR
Conditional aggregation: SUMIFS, COUNTIFS, AVERAGEIFS, MAXIFS
VLOOKUP and HLOOKUP and their limitations; INDEX with MATCH; XLOOKUP
Approximate-match lookups for bands: mobile money fee tiers and income tax brackets
Combining lookups across sheets; building a price list and invoice

syllabus.title: Pivot tables and summaries
topics: Creating pivot tables: rows, columns, values and filters
Summarising by sum, count, average and percentage of total; grouping dates and numbers
Calculated fields, slicers and timelines
Cross-tabulating district health data by region, month and condition
Refreshing pivots when the source data changes

syllabus.title: Charts in spreadsheets
topics: Choosing a chart: column, bar, line, scatter, pie, histogram and box plot
Formatting axes, labels and titles; combination charts and secondary axes
Misleading charts: truncated axes, 3-D effects and cherry-picked ranges
Conditional formatting, data bars and sparklines
Building a one-page dashboard

syllabus.title: Descriptive statistics and trends
topics: Measures of centre and spread: mean, median, mode, range, standard deviation, percentiles
Frequency distributions and histograms with FREQUENCY and COUNTIFS
Correlation and scatter plots; trendlines
Simple linear regression with SLOPE, INTERCEPT and LINEST; forecasting with FORECAST and moving averages
Analysing seasonal cocoa prices or rainfall

syllabus.title: What-if analysis and goal seek
topics: One- and two-variable data tables; sensitivity analysis
Scenario manager: best, worst and expected cases
Goal seek: break-even volume and target price
Solver for optimisation: linear programming for product mix and delivery routes
Financial functions: PMT, FV, NPV and IRR; a loan amortisation schedule

syllabus.title: Building a simple business model
topics: Model design: separating inputs, calculations and outputs; documenting assumptions
Revenue, costs, profit and loss and a monthly cash-flow forecast for a small business such as a chop bar or a cocoa cooperative
Error checks, consistency totals and spreadsheet risk; well-known spreadsheet errors and their costs
Protecting sheets and cells, version control and sharing models
Presenting results and recommendations to a non-technical owner
Capstone: a complete, checked business model with a short report

courses.title: Circuit Analysis
topics: Voltage, current, resistance and Ohm's law

courses.description: Analysing linear electric circuits from Ohm's and Kirchhoff's laws through nodal and mesh analysis, network theorems, first- and second-order transients, sinusoidal steady state with phasors and AC power, ending with diodes and transistors as circuit elements. Every circuit is built and measured on a simulated bench in the browser, with virtual meters and an oscilloscope checking each hand calculation.

Hayt, Kemmerly and Durbin, Engineering Circuit Analysis
Nilsson and Riedel, Electric Circuits

Derive and sketch the transient response of first- and second-order RC, RL and RLC circuits after switching.

courses.description: The craft of designing games that people want to play: what makes a game, the mechanics-dynamics-aesthetics framework, core loops, level design, balancing and difficulty, narrative, playtesting and designing games that teach. Polar coordinates and parametric curves
Geometry for graphics: angles between lines, reflection, rotation, areas of polygons

syllabus.title: Vectors

Lines and planes in space; distance from a point to a plane

syllabus.title: Matrices and systems of linear equations

Systems of linear equations; Gaussian and Gauss-Jordan elimination; row echelon form; rank
Determinants: cofactor expansion, properties, Cramer's rule
Inverse of a matrix; solving AX = B; LU decomposition preview
Matrices as transformations: rotation, scaling, shear; composition of transformations
Markov chains and PageRank as matrix problems

syllabus.title: Eigenvalues and eigenvectors
topics: Characteristic polynomial, eigenvalues and eigenvectors of 2x2 and 3x3 matrices
Diagonalisation and powers of a matrix

Numerical computation of eigenvalues in R and MATLAB

syllabus.title: Applications in R and MATLAB
topics: Matrix operations, solving systems, determinants, inverses and eigen-decomposition in both tools

Fitting a line to data by least squares as a matrix problem
A capstone: image transformation or a simple recommendation using vector similarity

courses.title: Multivariable Calculus
topics: Partial derivatives and gradients
Multiple integrals
Vector fields and line integrals
Jacobians and change of variables
Taylor expansion in several variables
Constrained optimisation and Lagrange multipliers
Matrix calculus for machine learning
courses.description: Calculus of functions of several variables: gradients, optimisation, multiple integrals, vector fields and the great integral theorems, ending in the matrix calculus used in machine learning. Students plot surfaces and fields, compute derivatives and integrals symbolically and numerically, and code gradient-based methods in the lab.
modelledOn: Stewart, Calculus: Early Transcendentals (multivariable chapters)
Marsden and Tromba, Vector Calculus
Deisenroth, Faisal and Ong, Mathematics for Machine Learning (analytic geometry and vector calculus chapters)
outcomes: Compute and interpret partial derivatives, gradients, directional derivatives and tangent planes.
Locate and classify local and global extrema, including constrained extrema with Lagrange multipliers.
Evaluate double and triple integrals in Cartesian, polar, cylindrical and spherical coordinates, using the Jacobian for changes of variables.
Compute line and surface integrals and apply Green, Stokes and divergence theorems.
Differentiate vector and matrix expressions and use them to derive gradients for least squares and neural networks.
Verify analytic results numerically with plots, finite differences, quadrature and Monte Carlo methods.

syllabus.title: Vectors, curves, surfaces and coordinates
topics: Vectors in R^n: dot and cross products, lines and planes
Parametric curves: velocity, tangent vector, arc length and curvature
Surfaces and level sets: quadric surfaces, contour plots
Polar, cylindrical and spherical coordinates
Functions of several variables: limits along paths and continuity

syllabus.title: Partial derivatives and the gradient
topics: Partial derivatives, tangent planes and linear approximation
The multivariable chain rule with tree diagrams
Directional derivatives and the gradient as direction of steepest ascent
Implicit differentiation and the implicit function theorem
Gradient descent: steepest descent on a loss surface, learning rate and zig-zagging
Total differential and propagation of measurement error

syllabus.title: Taylor expansion and local extrema

Critical points and the second-derivative test
Saddle points and classification using Hessian eigenvalues
Global extrema on closed bounded regions
Convex functions, positive-definite Hessians and why convexity makes optimisation easy

syllabus.title: Constrained optimisation
topics: Lagrange multipliers with one equality constraint
Several constraints and the geometry of parallel gradients
The multiplier as a shadow price: sensitivity of the optimum
Inequality constraints and an introduction to the KKT conditions
Applications: allocating land among crops, maximum entropy and the margin of a support vector machine

syllabus.title: Multiple integrals
topics: Double integrals over rectangles and general regions; Fubini theorem and order of integration
Double integrals in polar coordinates
Triple integrals in Cartesian, cylindrical and spherical coordinates
Mass, centre of mass, moments of inertia and joint probability densities
The Gaussian integral and the normal distribution normalising constant
Monte Carlo integration and its error in high dimensions

syllabus.title: Jacobians and change of variables
topics: The Jacobian matrix as the best linear approximation of a map
Jacobian determinant and change of variables in double and triple integrals
Transforming probability densities under a change of variable
Inverse functions, invertibility and the inverse function theorem

syllabus.title: Vector fields and line integrals
topics: Vector fields, flow lines and gradient fields
Line integrals of scalar functions and of vector fields; work and circulation
Conservative fields, potential functions and the fundamental theorem for line integrals
Green's theorem and area as a line integral
Divergence and curl: meaning and computation

syllabus.title: Surface integrals and the integral theorems
topics: Parametrised surfaces, tangent vectors and surface area
Surface integrals and flux of a vector field
Stokes' theorem
The divergence theorem
Applications: fluid flow, heat flow and conservation laws

syllabus.title: Matrix calculus for machine learning
topics: Gradient of a scalar with respect to a vector; Jacobian of a vector function
Derivatives of linear and quadratic forms; the Hessian matrix
The chain rule in matrix form and backpropagation through a layer
Least squares: deriving the normal equations and the gradient of the loss
Automatic differentiation: forward and reverse mode compared with finite differences

courses.title: Probability and Statistics
topics: Probability theory
Random variables
Special distributions
Moments and moment generating functions
Special probability theorems
Joint probability distributions
Computer simulation in R
courses.description: Probability theory and statistics built for computer scientists, with every distribution simulated in R before and after it is derived. Taught to the depth of a full probability course for computer scientists.
modelledOn: Ross, A First Course in Probability
Bertsekas and Tsitsiklis, Introduction to Probability
Walpole, Myers, Myers and Ye, Probability and Statistics for Engineers and Scientists
outcomes: Compute probabilities of events with counting, conditional probability, independence and Bayes' theorem.
Work with discrete and continuous random variables, their PMFs, PDFs, CDFs, expectations and variances.
Recognise and apply the standard distributions, including Bernoulli, binomial, geometric, Poisson, uniform, exponential and normal.
Use moments and moment generating functions to derive properties and sums of random variables.
Apply the law of large numbers and central limit theorem and construct confidence intervals and hypothesis tests.
Simulate random processes in R and use the results to check analytic answers and estimate hard quantities.

syllabus.title: Probability theory
topics: Sample spaces, events, set operations; axioms of probability
Counting: permutations, combinations, multinomials; birthday problem and hash collisions
Conditional probability, multiplication rule, law of total probability
Bayes' theorem: medical tests, spam filters, malaria rapid tests with false positives
Independence and conditional independence; reliability of series and parallel systems

syllabus.title: Random variables
topics: Discrete random variables, probability mass functions, cumulative distribution functions
Continuous random variables, probability density functions; the CDF as the bridge
Expectation, variance, standard deviation; linearity of expectation
Functions of random variables; expectation of a function
Indicator variables and counting with expectation (expected number of collisions, fixed points)

syllabus.title: Special distributions

Poisson distribution and the Poisson process: arrivals at a bank, packets at a router
Uniform, exponential (memorylessness) and gamma distributions
Normal distribution: standardisation, tables, the 68-95-99.7 rule; normal approximation to binomial
Choosing a distribution for a real situation; fitting and checking in R

MGFs of the standard distributions; sums of independent random variables
Characteristic functions and probability generating functions in brief

syllabus.title: Joint probability distributions

Conditional expectation and the law of iterated expectation
Sums of random variables, convolution; distribution of the maximum and minimum

Weak and strong laws of large numbers
Central limit theorem: statement, intuition and simulation

syllabus.title: Statistics: estimation and testing

Confidence intervals for means and proportions; t-distribution
Hypothesis testing: null and alternative, p-values, type I and II errors, z and t tests, chi-square tests
Simple linear regression and correlation; A/B testing a web page

syllabus.title: Computer simulation in R
topics: Pseudo-random numbers; sample, runif, rnorm, rbinom and friends; setting seeds
Simulating games, queues and random walks; estimating probabilities and expectations
Inverse transform and rejection sampling to generate any distribution
Bootstrap confidence intervals; visualising sampling distributions
Project: simulate a mobile-money transaction system or a classroom's exam scores and compare with theory

courses.title: Programming with C

courses.description: C as the language of the machine: types, pointers, memory, structures, files and the toolchain, taught by writing and debugging real systems-style programs. Taught to the depth of a leading systems programming course.
modelledOn: Kernighan and Ritchie, The C Programming Language
Bryant and O'Hallaron, Computer Systems: A Programmer's Perspective (C and memory chapters)
King, C Programming: A Modern Approach
outcomes: Write well-structured C programs using the full type system, operators, control flow and functions.
Use arrays, strings and pointers correctly and explain their representation in memory.
Allocate and free dynamic memory and build linked structures without leaks or dangling pointers.
Model data with structures, unions and enumerations and persist it with text and binary files.
Drive the preprocessor, compiler, linker and debugger, and split a program across multiple files.
Find memory errors with tools such as a debugger and a sanitizer and reason about undefined behaviour.

syllabus.title: C syntax, types and operators

Constants, variables, declarations, initialisation; const and typedef
Arithmetic, relational, logical, bitwise and assignment operators; precedence; implicit conversions
printf and scanf formatting; getchar and putchar

syllabus.title: Control flow and functions
topics: if, switch, while, do-while, for; break, continue, goto
Function definition and declaration, prototypes, header files
Call by value; scope, storage classes (auto, static, extern, register)
Recursion and the call stack; stack frames
Modular design: splitting a program into functions and files

Compiler flags, warnings as errors and optimisation levels

syllabus.title: Debugging, safety and undefined behaviour
topics: gdb: breakpoints, stepping, inspecting memory and the stack

Defensive coding, assertions and unit tests in C
Project: a small system utility or data manager combining files, structs and pointers

courses.title: Analogue Electronics and Devices

Razavi, Fundamentals of Microelectronics
Horowitz and Hill, The Art of Electronics

Bias a transistor stage at a stable operating point and derive its small-signal gain and impedances.
Design operational-amplifier circuits for summing, filtering, instrumentation and signal conditioning.

Design active filters, oscillators and linear power stages to a specification, and verify them by measurement.

courses.title: Biostatistics

Probability distributions in health data
Estimation and hypothesis testing

Multiple testing
courses.description: Statistics for biology, medicine and public health: study design, describing biological and clinical data, probability distributions in health data, estimation and hypothesis testing, regression for continuous, binary and count outcomes, survival analysis and the problem of multiple testing in genomic studies. Every method is computed by hand on small examples, then run on real health datasets with interactive plots and notebooks in the browser, taught to the depth of a strong biostatistics course for computing and health science students.

Kirkwood and Sterne, Essential Medical Statistics
Pagano and Gauvreau, Principles of Biostatistics
Altman, Practical Statistics for Medical Research

Summarise and visualise biological and clinical data and compute measures of disease frequency and association.
Apply probability distributions to model counts, proportions and measurements in health data, and evaluate diagnostic tests.
Estimate parameters with confidence intervals and carry out and interpret hypothesis tests, including power and sample size calculations.
Fit, check and interpret linear, logistic and Poisson regression models and Kaplan-Meier and Cox survival models.
Control error rates when testing many hypotheses and report analyses reproducibly according to reporting guidelines.

syllabus.title: Study design in biology and medicine

Cross-sectional surveys, case-control and cohort studies; randomised controlled trials, blinding and allocation concealment
Bias, confounding and effect modification; causation and the Bradford Hill considerations
Sampling methods: simple random, stratified, cluster and multistage designs as used in demographic and health surveys

syllabus.title: Describing biological data

Measures of association: risk difference, risk ratio, odds ratio, rate ratio

Model building, collinearity and overfitting; prediction models and their validation

syllabus.title: Multiple testing

topics: Bayesian inference in brief: priors, posteriors and credible intervals for a prevalence estimate

BPMN notation
As-is and to-be analysis

Startup ecosystems in Africa: hubs, incubators and accelerators
