topics: Business case: cost-benefit analysis, NPV, IRR and payback period
Balanced scorecard and KPIs for digital initiatives
Benefits realisation management and value tracking
Risk, scenario analysis and real options
Digital ethics, inclusion and sustainability impact

syllabus.title: Capstone: building a transformation roadmap
topics: Diagnosing an organisation: maturity scores and pain points
Building a prioritised roadmap and initiative portfolio
Presenting the case to an executive board
Review and reflection on the course cases

courses.title: Electric Machines and Drives
topics: DC motor models
Brushless and stepper motors
H-bridges and power electronics
Motor drive control
Servo systems
Batteries and power budgets
Gearing and transmission
courses.description: How electric motors convert energy and how robots drive them: DC, brushless and stepper motors, H-bridges, closed-loop control, servos, batteries and gearing. Students model motors, simulate drives on the circuit bench, and build and tune a small motor controller on the hardware bench.
modelledOn: Chapman, Electric Machinery Fundamentals
Mohan, Undeland and Robbins, Power Electronics: Converters, Applications and Design
Franklin, Powell and Emami-Naeini, Feedback Control of Dynamic Systems
outcomes: Derive the equivalent-circuit and torque-speed model of a DC motor and identify its parameters from measurements.
Select between brushed, brushless and stepper motors for a given torque, speed and cost requirement.
Design an H-bridge PWM drive with correct dead time, flyback protection and current limiting.
Tune cascaded current, speed and position loops and judge them by step response.
Compute a battery and power budget for a mobile robot and choose a gear ratio that matches motor and load.

syllabus.title: Energy conversion and electromechanics
topics: Magnetic circuits: flux, reluctance, Faraday's law and the Lorentz force
Torque production and back-EMF as the two faces of one coupling
Power flow and losses: copper, iron and friction; efficiency maps
Mechanical load models: constant torque, viscous, fan and inertial loads; the torque-speed plane
Sizing a motor for a duty cycle: peak, continuous and RMS torque

syllabus.title: DC motor models
topics: The permanent-magnet DC motor equivalent circuit: armature resistance, inductance, torque and back-EMF constants
Torque-speed and current-speed lines; stall torque and no-load speed
Electromechanical transfer function: electrical and mechanical time constants
Separately excited, shunt, series and compound DC machines
Speed control by armature voltage and by field weakening
Parameter identification from no-load and locked-rotor tests

syllabus.title: Brushless, stepper and AC motors
topics: Stepper motors: variable reluctance, permanent magnet and hybrid; full, half and microstepping
Stepper torque-speed behaviour: resonance, missed steps and current chopping
Brushless DC motors: construction, Hall-sensor commutation and the six-step sequence
Sensorless commutation by back-EMF and an introduction to field-oriented control
Induction and synchronous motors: rotating field, slip and the V/f relation
Choosing a motor type for a robot joint, wheel, pump or conveyor

syllabus.title: H-bridges and power electronics
topics: Power MOSFETs and IGBTs as switches: gate drive, conduction and switching losses
The H-bridge: four-quadrant operation, braking and shoot-through with dead time
PWM generation: duty cycle, frequency choice and average voltage
Inductive loads: flyback diodes, current ripple and voltage spikes
Motor driver ICs, current sensing, overcurrent and thermal protection

syllabus.title: Motor drive control
topics: Open-loop drives: voltage-frequency control and stepper pulse trains
Closed-loop speed control with a PI controller
Cascaded current and speed loops; loop bandwidths
Feedback sensing: optical encoders, quadrature decoding, tachometers and Hall sensors
PID tuning: Ziegler-Nichols, step-response methods and anti-windup
Current limiting, dynamic braking and regenerative braking

syllabus.title: Servo systems
topics: Servo architecture: hobby servo PWM protocol versus an industrial servo drive
Position control loop: step response, overshoot, settling time and steady-state error
Motion profiles: trapezoidal and S-curve acceleration limits
Multi-axis coordination for a robot arm and a differential-drive base
Friction, backlash and disturbance compensation; feedforward

syllabus.title: Batteries and power budgets
topics: Battery chemistries: lead-acid, Li-ion and LiFePO4; capacity, C-rate and energy density
Discharge curves, internal resistance, state of charge and Peukert's effect
Battery management: cell balancing, protection and charge profiles
Power budget of a mobile robot: duty cycles, peak currents and runtime estimates
Solar charging and off-grid operation for a field robot in Ghana
Regulated rails: DC-DC conversion for logic, sensors and motors

syllabus.title: Gearing and transmission
topics: Gear ratio, torque-speed trade and reflected inertia
Efficiency, backlash and wear in spur, helical and worm gears
Planetary and harmonic drives; gear trains
Belts, chains, lead screws and linear actuators
Matching motor and load: the optimum gear ratio and thermal limits

courses.title: Electromagnetics, Antennas and RF Engineering
topics: Maxwell equations and wave propagation
transmission lines and Smith chart
waveguides and resonators
antenna types and radiation patterns
link budgets and propagation models
RF amplifiers, mixers and filters
electromagnetic compatibility
courses.description: Fields, waves, transmission lines, antennas and radio-frequency circuits, from Maxwell's equations to a working link budget. Students solve fields numerically, match lines on the Smith chart, design signal-integrity fixes on the circuit bench and size radio links for rural Africa.
modelledOn: Hayt and Buck, Engineering Electromagnetics
Pozar, Microwave Engineering
Balanis, Antenna Theory: Analysis and Design
Johnson and Graham, High-Speed Digital Design
outcomes: Apply vector calculus and Maxwell's equations to static fields, plane waves and boundary problems.
Analyse transmission lines with reflection coefficient, VSWR, bounce diagrams and the Smith chart, and design matching networks.
Diagnose and fix signal-integrity problems on fast digital interconnects using termination, stackup and decoupling.
Characterise antennas by pattern, gain and impedance, and design simple dipoles, arrays and patches.
Build a link budget with a propagation model and decide whether a radio link in a given terrain will work.
Analyse RF chains for gain, noise and nonlinearity, and apply shielding and filtering for electromagnetic compatibility.

syllabus.title: Vector fields and static fields
topics: Vector calculus review: gradient, divergence, curl in Cartesian, cylindrical and spherical coordinates
Electrostatics: Coulomb's law, Gauss's law, potential and capacitance
Laplace and Poisson equations; numerical solution by finite differences
Magnetostatics: Biot-Savart law, Ampere's law, flux and inductance
Materials and boundary conditions: dielectrics, conductors and magnetic media

syllabus.title: Maxwell's equations and plane waves
topics: Faraday's law, displacement current and the four Maxwell equations in integral and differential form
The wave equation and uniform plane waves in lossless media; phase velocity and wave impedance
Waves in lossy media and good conductors; attenuation and skin depth
Polarisation: linear, circular and elliptical; polarisation loss
Power flow and the Poynting vector
Reflection and transmission at a dielectric interface: normal and oblique incidence, Snell's law, Brewster angle

syllabus.title: Transmission lines and the Smith chart
topics: Distributed circuit model and the telegrapher's equations; characteristic impedance and propagation constant
Lossless and low-loss lines; reflection coefficient, standing waves and VSWR
Input impedance, the quarter-wave transformer and open and short stubs
The Smith chart: impedance and admittance, moving along a line
Impedance matching with single-stub and lumped L-networks
Transients on lines: step response and the bounce (lattice) diagram

syllabus.title: Signal integrity for high-speed digital design
topics: When an interconnect is a transmission line: edge rate versus trace length
Microstrip and stripline impedance, PCB stackup and return paths
Termination schemes: series, parallel and Thevenin; reflections and ringing
Crosstalk, ground bounce and simultaneous switching noise
Decoupling, power integrity, eye diagrams and jitter

syllabus.title: Waveguides, resonators and optical fibre
topics: Rectangular waveguide: TE and TM modes and cutoff frequency
Dispersion, phase and group velocity in guided waves
Cavity resonators and quality factor
Planar lines: microstrip, coplanar waveguide and substrate choice
Optical fibre as a dielectric waveguide: modes, attenuation, dispersion

syllabus.title: Antennas
topics: Radiation from a current element; radiation pattern, beamwidth, directivity, gain and efficiency
Half-wave dipole and monopole: pattern, input impedance and bandwidth
Antenna arrays: array factor, element spacing, grating lobes and beam steering
Aperture antennas: horn and parabolic reflector; gain and illumination efficiency
Microstrip patch antennas: design equations, feeding and bandwidth
Antenna measurement, polarisation matching and Sub-Saharan deployments: VHF/UHF masts, rural 4G and VSAT dishes

syllabus.title: Propagation and link budgets
topics: Free-space propagation: the Friis equation, EIRP and path loss
Terrestrial models: two-ray ground reflection, log-distance and empirical macro-cell models
Fading and shadowing: Rayleigh and Rician fading, fade margin
Line-of-sight microwave links: Fresnel zones, earth bulge, tower height and rain attenuation
Satellite links: G/T, noise temperature and Eb/N0
Link budget design and rural coverage planning: cell radius, TV white space and community networks

syllabus.title: RF circuits and systems
topics: Two-port networks and S-parameters; reading a vector network analyser plot
Noise figure and the Friis cascade formula; receiver sensitivity
Low-noise and power amplifiers: gain, stability and matching
Mixers, local oscillators and the superheterodyne receiver; image frequency
Filters (LC, coupled-line) and nonlinearity: 1 dB compression and third-order intercept

syllabus.title: Electromagnetic compatibility
topics: Sources and victims of interference; conducted and radiated emissions
Coupling mechanisms: common impedance, capacitive, inductive and radiative
Shielding effectiveness, apertures and cable shields
Grounding, filtering and ferrites; lightning and surge protection for tropical installations
EMC standards and pre-compliance testing practice

courses.title: Engineering Mechanics and Dynamics
topics: Statics and free-body diagrams
Particle kinematics
Rigid-body kinematics
Newton-Euler dynamics
Work, energy and momentum
Vibrations and oscillators
Simulation of mechanical systems
courses.description: The mechanics every robot, vehicle and machine rests on: forces in equilibrium, motion of particles and rigid bodies, energy and momentum, Lagrangian methods and vibration. Students solve problems with vectors and matrices and simulate mechanisms and oscillators numerically in the lab.
modelledOn: Hibbeler, Engineering Mechanics: Statics and Dynamics
Meriam and Kraige, Engineering Mechanics: Dynamics
Rao, Mechanical Vibrations
Spong, Hutchinson and Vidyasagar, Robot Modeling and Control (dynamics chapters)
outcomes: Draw free-body diagrams and solve 2D and 3D static equilibrium problems, including trusses, frames and friction.
Describe the motion of particles and rigid bodies with velocity and acceleration vectors in several coordinate systems.
Apply Newton-Euler equations, work-energy and impulse-momentum methods to particles and rigid bodies.
Derive equations of motion with Lagrange equations for systems with generalised coordinates.
Analyse free, damped and forced vibration and predict natural frequency, damping ratio and resonance.
Integrate equations of motion numerically and judge accuracy, stability and energy conservation.

syllabus.title: Vectors, forces and moments
topics: Vector algebra for mechanics: dot and cross products, components and unit vectors
Forces, moment of a force about a point and an axis, couples
Equivalent force systems: resultant force and couple, wrench
SI units, dimensional analysis and significant figures in engineering calculations
Modelling assumptions: particle, rigid body, point load and idealised supports

syllabus.title: Equilibrium of rigid bodies and structures
topics: Free-body diagrams and support reactions: pin, roller, fixed and cable
Equations of equilibrium in two and three dimensions; two-force and three-force members
Plane trusses: method of joints, method of sections and zero-force members
Frames and machines: multi-body free-body diagrams and internal pin forces
Dry friction: impending slip, wedges, screws and belt friction
Centroids, distributed loads, and shear force and bending moment diagrams for beams

syllabus.title: Kinematics of particles
topics: Rectilinear motion: position, velocity, acceleration and their graphs
Projectile motion with and without air drag
Curvilinear motion in Cartesian, normal-tangential and polar coordinates
Relative and dependent motion of two particles
Numerical differentiation and integration of measured motion data

syllabus.title: Kinetics of particles: force, energy and momentum
topics: Newton second law for particles in rectilinear and curvilinear motion
Work, kinetic energy and power; the work-energy principle
Conservative forces and potential energy; energy conservation
Linear impulse and momentum; collisions and the coefficient of restitution
Angular momentum of a particle and motion under a central force

syllabus.title: Kinematics of rigid bodies
topics: Planar rigid-body motion: translation and fixed-axis rotation
General plane motion and the instantaneous centre of zero velocity
Relative velocity and acceleration between points on a rigid body
Rotating reference frames and the Coriolis acceleration
Three-dimensional rotation: rotation matrices, Euler angles and angular velocity vector
Linkages: four-bar mechanism, slider-crank and the Grashof condition

syllabus.title: Kinetics of rigid bodies: Newton-Euler dynamics
topics: Mass moment of inertia, radius of gyration and the parallel-axis theorem
Newton-Euler equations of planar motion: translation, rotation and general plane motion
Work and energy for rigid bodies; rolling without slipping
Impulse and momentum for rigid bodies; eccentric impact
Rolling, sliding and the transition between them on a rough surface
Three-dimensional dynamics: inertia tensor, principal axes and Euler equations

syllabus.title: Analytical mechanics
topics: Generalised coordinates, degrees of freedom and holonomic constraints
Principle of virtual work and generalised forces
Lagrange's equations from kinetic and potential energy
Worked systems: pendulum, double pendulum, cart-pole and a two-link arm
From Lagrange equations to the manipulator equation M(q)q-double-dot + C(q,q-dot)q-dot + g(q) = tau

syllabus.title: Vibrations and oscillators
topics: Free vibration of a single degree-of-freedom mass-spring system; natural frequency
Viscous damping: underdamped, critically damped and overdamped response; logarithmic decrement
Forced harmonic vibration: amplitude ratio, phase, resonance and the quality factor
Base excitation, transmissibility and vibration isolation; vehicle suspension on rough roads
Two degree-of-freedom systems: natural frequencies, mode shapes and the vibration absorber
Rayleigh's energy method and the mechanical-electrical analogy

syllabus.title: Simulation of mechanical systems
topics: Writing equations of motion as first-order state-space ordinary differential equations
Euler, midpoint and fourth-order Runge-Kutta integration; step size and truncation error
Stability, stiffness and energy drift; symplectic integration for conservative systems
Simulating a pendulum, a slider-crank and a mass-spring-damper and validating against closed forms
Mini project: simulate a mechanism of your choice and compare model with measured data

courses.title: Financial Mathematics
topics: Interest and time value of money
Annuities and loans
Bonds and yields
Risk and return
Portfolio theory
Options and derivatives basics
Microfinance and credit scoring
courses.description: The mathematics of money and risk: interest and the time value of money, annuities and loans, bonds and yields, risk and return, portfolio theory, options and derivatives, and the mathematics of microfinance and credit scoring. Every formula is derived and then computed, plotted and simulated in the browser on real cases such as treasury bills, mobile loans and susu groups.
modelledOn: Kellison, The Theory of Interest
Luenberger, Investment Science
Bodie, Kane and Marcus, Investments
Hull, Options, Futures, and Other Derivatives
outcomes: Compute present and future values under simple, compound and continuous interest and compare nominal, effective and real rates.
Value annuities and perpetuities and build amortisation schedules for loans, mortgages and microloans.
Price bonds and treasury bills, compute their yields, duration and convexity and interpret the yield curve.
Measure risk and return, construct efficient portfolios and apply the capital asset pricing model.
Price forwards and options with no-arbitrage, binomial and Black-Scholes models and explain their use for hedging.
Build and evaluate a credit scoring model and analyse the true cost of microfinance and mobile loans.

syllabus.title: Interest and the time value of money
topics: Simple and compound interest; accumulation and discount functions
Nominal and effective rates, compounding frequency, continuous compounding and the force of interest
Present and future value; equations of value and solving for unknown rates and times
Inflation and real interest rates; the Fisher equation; the Bank of Ghana policy rate and its effect on lending rates
Comparing savings options: bank deposits, mobile money interest and a susu collector's fee as an implied rate

syllabus.title: Annuities and cash-flow valuation
topics: Annuities immediate and due; perpetuities; deferred annuities
Annuities with varying payments: arithmetic and geometric growth
Net present value, internal rate of return and payback period; choosing between projects
Building cash-flow models in a spreadsheet and in code

syllabus.title: Loans and amortisation
topics: Amortisation schedules: interest and principal in each instalment; outstanding balance (prospective and retrospective)
Sinking funds; flat-rate versus reducing-balance interest and why flat rates mislead
Annual percentage rate, fees and the true cost of credit; consumer credit disclosure
Mortgages, car loans, hire purchase and refinancing decisions
Pricing a mobile nano-loan with a fee and a short tenor, and converting it to an annual rate

syllabus.title: Bonds and yields
topics: Bond terminology: face value, coupon, maturity, clean and dirty price, accrued interest
Bond pricing and yield to maturity; premium, par and discount bonds
Treasury bills: discount and interest yields, the 91-day and 182-day bill auctions in Ghana
Term structure: spot rates, forward rates, bootstrapping the yield curve, theories of the term structure
Duration, modified duration and convexity; immunisation of a liability
Credit risk, default and sovereign debt restructuring, with Ghana's domestic debt exchange as a case

syllabus.title: Risk and return
topics: Holding-period returns, arithmetic and geometric means, annualising returns
Random returns: expected value, variance, standard deviation, covariance and correlation
Risk preferences and utility functions; risk aversion and certainty equivalents
Value at risk and the limits of the normal distribution: fat tails and skew
Returns on the Ghana Stock Exchange and other African markets analysed from price data

syllabus.title: Portfolio theory
topics: Two-asset and multi-asset portfolios; diversification and the effect of correlation
Mean-variance optimisation; the efficient frontier and the minimum-variance portfolio
The risk-free asset, the capital market line and the tangency portfolio; the Sharpe ratio
The capital asset pricing model: beta, the security market line, systematic and idiosyncratic risk
Factor models and arbitrage pricing theory in outline; market efficiency
Computing an efficient frontier numerically in the browser

syllabus.title: Options and derivatives basics
topics: Forwards and futures: payoffs, no-arbitrage pricing, cost of carry; currency forwards for the cedi
Options: calls and puts, payoffs and profit diagrams, put-call parity and option strategies
The binomial model: replicating portfolios, risk-neutral valuation, multi-period trees, American options
Brownian motion in outline and the Black-Scholes formula; the Greeks and delta hedging
Monte Carlo pricing of options and convergence of the binomial tree to Black-Scholes
Uses of derivatives in Africa: commodity hedging for cocoa and gold, and the risks of speculation

syllabus.title: Microfinance
topics: Microfinance models: group lending, joint liability, village banking and rotating savings (susu and ROSCAs)
Analysing a susu group or ROSCA as a sequence of loans and savings; the implied interest rate for each position
Microfinance interest rates: operating costs, loan size, portfolio at risk and sustainability
Mobile credit and digital lending: nano-loans on mobile money, over-indebtedness and consumer protection

syllabus.title: Credit scoring
topics: Credit risk measures: probability of default, loss given default, exposure at default and expected loss
Scorecards: logistic regression, weight of evidence, information value and points scaling
Model evaluation: ROC curves, the Gini coefficient, the KS statistic, calibration and cut-off choice
Alternative data for thin-file borrowers: mobile money histories, airtime top-ups and credit bureau data, and fairness concerns
Capstone: build and evaluate a credit scoring model for a microfinance lender on a synthetic loan book

courses.title: Functional Programming
topics: Pure functions and immutability
Higher-order functions and folds
Algebraic data types and pattern matching
Recursion and tail calls
Lazy evaluation and infinite structures
Type inference and polymorphism
Monads and handling effects
courses.description: Programming with functions as values: the lambda calculus, pure functions, folds, algebraic data types, laziness, type inference and monads. Students write functional programs in the code runner, using Python and JavaScript in a strict functional style, and step through evaluation and call stacks in the visualiser.
modelledOn: Hutton, Programming in Haskell
Abelson and Sussman, Structure and Interpretation of Computer Programs
Bird and Wadler, Introduction to Functional Programming
outcomes: Reduce lambda-calculus terms by hand and encode booleans, numbers and recursion with Church encodings and fixed points.
Write programs from pure functions, higher-order functions and folds without mutating state.
Model data with algebraic data types and process it by exhaustive pattern matching and structural recursion.
Convert recursive definitions to tail-recursive form and explain stack use, memoisation and lazy evaluation.
Infer principal types for small programs and use parametric polymorphism, functors and monoids.
Structure effects with Maybe, Either, State and Writer monads and keep side effects at the edge of a program.

syllabus.title: The lambda calculus
topics: Lambda terms: abstraction, application, free and bound variables, alpha conversion
Beta reduction, normal forms, normal-order versus applicative-order evaluation, and the Church-Rosser theorem
Church encodings of booleans, pairs and natural numbers; arithmetic by function application
Recursion without names: fixed points and the Y combinator

syllabus.title: Purity and immutability
topics: Pure functions and referential transparency; equational reasoning
Side effects and why they complicate testing, caching and concurrency
Immutable data and persistent structures with structural sharing
Substitution model versus environment model of evaluation
Proving properties of functions by equation and induction, such as map fusion

syllabus.title: Higher-order functions and folds
topics: First-class functions, closures and lexical scope
map, filter and zip as the vocabulary of list processing
foldr and foldl: definitions, differences and expressing sum, length and reverse as folds
Currying, partial application and function composition
Pipelines, point-free style and list comprehensions

syllabus.title: Algebraic data types and pattern matching
topics: Product types and sum types; tagged unions in Python and JavaScript
Pattern matching and exhaustiveness checking
Recursive types: lists, binary trees and expression trees
Option and Either types replacing null and exceptions
Structural recursion and folds over trees (catamorphisms)

syllabus.title: Recursion and tail calls
topics: Structural recursion and its correspondence with induction
Accumulators, tail recursion and tail-call elimination
Mutual recursion and trampolines to avoid stack overflow
Cost of recursion: stack depth, repeated work in naive Fibonacci and memoisation
Divide and conquer in functional style: merge sort and quicksort on immutable lists

syllabus.title: Lazy evaluation and infinite structures
topics: Call-by-value, call-by-name and call-by-need; thunks and sharing
Infinite lists and streams: naturals, Fibonacci numbers and the sieve of Eratosthenes with generators
Laziness and control: short-circuit operators and user-defined control structures
Space leaks, strictness and when laziness costs memory
Lazy dynamic programming and memoisation through lazy tables

syllabus.title: Types, inference and polymorphism
topics: Parametric polymorphism: type variables, generic functions and free theorems
Hindley-Milner type inference: constraint generation and unification
Ad-hoc polymorphism: type classes, interfaces and overloading
Functors: mapping over containers and the functor laws
Monoids, semigroups and folding with associativity: parallel reduction

syllabus.title: Monads, effects and project
topics: Applicative functors: combining independent effectful computations
The monad interface: bind, return and the monad laws
Maybe, Either, List, State and Writer monads worked through examples
Effects at the edge: functional core with an imperative shell, and input and output
Project: a parser-combinator library and an interpreter for a small expression language

courses.title: Genetics and Population Genomics
topics: Mendelian and quantitative inheritance
Pedigrees and linkage analysis
Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium and allele frequencies
Drift, selection and the coalescent
Population structure and ancestry inference
Genome-wide association and QTL mapping
Heritability and polygenic scores
courses.description: How traits are inherited, how allele frequencies change in populations, and how genomic data is used to map genes and predict traits. In the lab students simulate crosses and populations, test Hardy-Weinberg and structure, and run a small association study and polygenic score from scratch.
modelledOn: Griffiths et al., Introduction to Genetic Analysis
Hartl and Clark, Principles of Population Genetics
Lynch and Walsh, Genetics and Analysis of Quantitative Traits (selected chapters)
Hamilton, Population Genetics
outcomes: Predict offspring ratios for Mendelian, sex-linked and quantitative traits and test them with chi-square statistics.
Estimate recombination fractions, map distances and LOD scores from crosses and pedigrees.
Test Hardy-Weinberg proportions and model the effects of drift, selection, mutation and migration on allele frequencies.
Describe and compute population structure with F-statistics, principal components and admixture models.
Run, quality-control and interpret a genome-wide association scan, including multiple-testing and stratification corrections.
Build and evaluate a polygenic score and explain its limits across ancestries.

syllabus.title: Mendelian inheritance
topics: Mendel's laws, monohybrid and dihybrid crosses, Punnett squares and chi-square goodness of fit
Dominance, codominance, incomplete dominance, epistasis, penetrance and expressivity
Sex-linked and mitochondrial inheritance; X inactivation
Genes, alleles and variants at the molecular level: SNPs, indels and copy-number variants
Worked cases from West Africa: sickle cell (HbS), G6PD deficiency and malaria protection
Probability rules in genetics: product, sum and binomial rules, and Bayes' rule for risk

syllabus.title: Quantitative inheritance
topics: Polygenic traits, the normal distribution and the additive model of genotype effects
Variance components: genetic, environmental, additive, dominance and epistatic variance
Broad-sense and narrow-sense heritability; parent-offspring regression and twin studies
The breeder's equation and response to selection in crops and livestock such as cassava, cocoa and cattle
Genotype-by-environment interaction and reaction norms

syllabus.title: Pedigrees and linkage analysis
topics: Pedigree notation and recognising autosomal dominant, autosomal recessive and X-linked patterns
Recombination, genetic distance, Haldane and Kosambi mapping functions
Three-point test crosses, gene order and interference
LOD scores and parametric linkage analysis
Carrier risk in pedigrees with Bayesian updating
Variation in recombination rate: hotspots and sex differences

syllabus.title: Allele frequencies and Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium
topics: Allele and genotype frequencies; the Hardy-Weinberg principle and its assumptions
Testing equilibrium: chi-square and exact tests, and genotyping error as a cause of deviation
Inbreeding coefficient, identity by descent and consanguinity
Multiple alleles and X-linked loci; estimating frequencies by expectation-maximisation (ABO blood groups)
Non-random mating: assortative mating and its effect on genotype frequencies

syllabus.title: Drift, selection and the coalescent
topics: Genetic drift in the Wright-Fisher model; fixation probability and effective population size
Natural selection: fitness, selection coefficient and heterozygote advantage (sickle cell as balanced polymorphism)
Mutation-selection balance, migration and gene flow; the island model
Neutral theory and the site frequency spectrum
Coalescent theory: genealogies, time to the most recent common ancestor and simulation
Detecting selection: Tajima's D, extended haplotype homozygosity and Fst outlier scans

syllabus.title: Population structure and ancestry
topics: Wright's F-statistics, Fst and isolation by distance
Principal component analysis of genotype matrices
Model-based clustering and admixture proportions; choosing the number of clusters
Admixture and local ancestry; African genetic diversity, the Bantu expansion and the out-of-Africa gradient
Linkage disequilibrium: D, r-squared, haplotype blocks and LD decay
Limits and ethics of genetic ancestry testing

syllabus.title: QTL mapping and genome-wide association
topics: QTL mapping in crosses: interval mapping, LOD thresholds and permutation tests
GWAS design and single-variant regression for quantitative and case-control traits
Quality control: call rate, minor allele frequency, Hardy-Weinberg filters and relatedness
Multiple testing: Bonferroni, genome-wide significance and false discovery rate; Manhattan and QQ plots
Confounding by stratification: genomic control, principal components and mixed models
Fine mapping, imputation and reference panels, including the under-representation of African ancestries

syllabus.title: Heritability and polygenic scores
topics: SNP heritability and the missing heritability problem
Constructing polygenic scores: clumping, thresholding and effect-size shrinkage
Evaluating prediction: R-squared, AUC, calibration and portability across ancestries
Genetic correlation, pleiotropy and an introduction to Mendelian randomisation
Ethics and governance of genomic research in Africa: consent, data sharing and benefit sharing
Capstone: a reproducible pipeline from simulated cohort to association scan to polygenic score

courses.title: Health Information Systems
topics: Health systems and their information needs
District health information systems
Health facility workflows
Indicators and reporting
Data quality in health
Evaluating health information systems
Health information systems in Africa
courses.description: How information flows through a health system and how software supports it: the building blocks of health systems, district health information systems such as DHIS2, facility workflows from registration to claims, indicators and routine reporting, data quality, evaluation of information systems and the history and governance of health information systems in Africa. Taught through case-based simulations of a district health directorate, with realistic reporting cycles, dashboards and data quality reviews built in browser-based tools.
modelledOn: WHO, Framework and Standards for Country Health Information Systems (Health Metrics Network)
WHO, Data Quality Review: A Toolkit for Facility Data Quality Assessment
Wager, Lee and Glaser, Health Care Information Systems: A Practical Approach for Health Care Management
Braa and Sahay, Integrated Health Information Architecture: Power to the Users
outcomes: Describe the building blocks of a health system and map the information needs of patients, clinicians, managers and policy makers at each level.
Configure a district health information system with organisation units, data elements, data sets and indicators and use it to collect and aggregate routine data.
Model health facility workflows from registration to discharge and insurance claims and identify where information is created, used and lost.
Define, calculate and interpret health indicators and produce reports and dashboards that support decisions at facility, district and national level.
Assess routine data for completeness, timeliness and consistency, and design interventions that improve data quality and use.
Evaluate a health information system against its goals using established frameworks and propose improvements suited to African health systems.

syllabus.title: Health systems and their information needs
topics: The WHO health system building blocks; health information as one of six; universal health coverage
Levels of care in Ghana: CHPS compounds, health centres, district, regional and teaching hospitals; the Ghana Health Service
Who needs what information: patients, clinicians, facility managers, district and regional directorates, ministries, donors
Data, information, knowledge and decisions; the information cycle from collection to action
Sources of health data: routine facility data, surveys (DHS, MICS), censuses, civil registration and vital statistics, surveillance

syllabus.title: Health information system architecture

courses.title: Healthcare Delivery, Quality and Patient Safety

courses.description: How health systems are organised, paid for and held to account, and how errors, delays and variation are measured and reduced. modelledOn: Shi and Singh, Delivering Health Care in America
World Health Organization, Patient Safety Curriculum Guide
Institute for Healthcare Improvement, Model for Improvement and Quality Improvement Essentials

outcomes: Describe how a health system is financed, organised and staffed, using the Ghanaian system as a worked example.
Trace a patient through primary, secondary and tertiary care and identify points where care can break down.
Analyse a patient-safety incident with root cause methods and propose system-level defences.
Select quality indicators, plot them over time and judge whether a change is a real improvement.
Map and redesign a clinical workflow using process diagrams and improvement cycles.
Assess the performance of a low-resource health system and plan patient engagement measures.

Risk adjustment, benchmarking and funnel plots for comparing facilities

courses.description: Propositional and predicate logic, proof, automated reasoning and the formal methods that use them to show programs and systems correct. modelledOn: Huth and Ryan, Logic in Computer Science
Baier and Katoen, Principles of Model Checking
Gries, The Science of Programming

syllabus.title: PowerShell for administration
topics: Cmdlets, verb-noun naming, Get-Help, Get-Member and the object pipeline
Filtering and shaping objects: Where-Object, Select-Object, Sort-Object, Group-Object and calculated properties
Variables, arrays, hashtables, string handling and here-strings
Functions and advanced functions with typed, validated parameters
Error handling: try, catch, finally, ErrorAction and Write-Verbose
Modules, execution policy, CSV and JSON import and export, and remoting basics

syllabus.title: Scheduling and task automation
topics: cron syntax, crontab files and systemd timers
Windows Task Scheduler: triggers, actions, run-as accounts and Register-ScheduledTask
Safe recurring jobs: lock files, overlapping runs, exit codes and alerting
Backup automation: rsync, tar and Robocopy, retention rotation and restore verification
Health-check and watchdog scripts for services, disk space and certificate expiry

syllabus.title: Bulk user and account management
topics: Linux accounts in scripts: useradd, usermod, groups, password ageing and sudoers drop-ins
Creating accounts in bulk from a CSV file with input validation
Active Directory with PowerShell: New-ADUser, Get-ADUser, organisational units and group membership
Onboarding and offboarding workflows: home folders, quotas, permissions, disabling and archiving
Handling secrets: initial passwords, SecureString and avoiding plaintext credentials
Idempotent re-runs, dry runs and audit trails of every decision

syllabus.title: Log parsing and reporting
topics: Log formats: syslog, authentication logs, web server access logs and the Windows Event Log
Extracting fields with awk, regular expressions, Select-String and Get-WinEvent filters
Aggregation: top clients, failed logins per user and address, and errors per hour
Detecting suspicious patterns: brute-force thresholds and time windows
Producing reports in CSV, JSON and HTML; log rotation with logrotate
Python for administration: pathlib, subprocess, re, csv, json and argparse

syllabus.title: Configuration and package automation
topics: Package managers: apt, dnf, winget and Chocolatey; version pinning and unattended updates
Provisioning a server from a script: packages, users, services, firewall rules and SSH keys
Configuration files as code: idempotent edits, templating and drift detection
Desired-state tools: declarative versus imperative, playbooks, inventories and idempotency
Containers as repeatable environments: Dockerfile and compose basics
Calling REST APIs from scripts: curl, Invoke-RestMethod, tokens, retries and JSON parsing

syllabus.title: Safe testing of scripts
topics: Dry runs and tracing: WhatIf, Confirm, set -x, shellcheck and PSScriptAnalyzer
Disposable test environments: snapshots, virtual machines and containers
Automated tests for scripts with bats and Pester, using test data and mocks
Defensive scripting: least privilege, quoting, injection through eval, path hazards and guard rails around rm
Change management: version control, review, signing, staged rollout and rollback plans

syllabus.title: Automation project and its value
topics: Designing an end-to-end workflow from onboarding to backup to reporting
Documentation: runbooks, comments and usage text
Measuring value: time saved, errors avoided and payback for a school lab or small ISP
When not to automate: maintainability, rare tasks and handover

courses.title: Security Risk Management and Governance
topics: Asset and threat identification
Risk assessment methods
Security policy and standards
Controls and control frameworks
Business continuity and disaster recovery
Security awareness and human factors
Audit and assurance
courses.description: How organisations decide what to protect, how much risk to accept and how to prove their security works: assets and threats, risk assessment, policy, controls, continuity, people and audit. Students work through branching case studies where they gather evidence, make decisions and are scored against a rubric.
modelledOn: ISO/IEC 27001, 27002 and 27005 information security management standards
NIST SP 800-30 and the NIST Cybersecurity Framework
Whitman and Mattord, Management of Information Security
ISACA CISM and CRISC certification bodies of knowledge
outcomes: Build an asset inventory and a threat and vulnerability picture for an organisation, with business impact ratings.
Carry out qualitative and quantitative risk assessments and choose and justify a risk treatment.
Write a security policy hierarchy that is enforceable, proportionate and mapped to a recognised standard.
Select and map controls from ISO 27002, NIST and CIS frameworks on cost-benefit grounds.
Develop a business continuity and disaster recovery plan with defined recovery objectives and test it by exercise.
Plan and report an audit of security controls and communicate findings to a board.

syllabus.title: Security management and governance foundations
topics: Security goals (confidentiality, integrity, availability) and the role of the security function and the CISO
Governance versus management; board duties and the three lines model
Aligning security with strategy: budgets, key performance indicators and key risk indicators
Legal and regulatory setting: Ghana Data Protection Act 2012, Cybersecurity Act 2020, Bank of Ghana directives and GDPR
Standards landscape: ISO/IEC 27001 and 27002, NIST CSF, NIST SP 800-53 and COBIT

syllabus.title: Asset and threat identification
topics: Asset inventory and information classification; identifying crown-jewel assets
Business impact analysis: criticality, dependencies and valuation
Threat actors, motives and capabilities; threat intelligence and MITRE ATT&CK as a shared vocabulary
Vulnerability sources: scanners, penetration test reports, CVE and CVSS scoring
Scenario building and attack trees; third-party and supply chain exposure

syllabus.title: Risk assessment methods
topics: Risk concepts: likelihood, impact, inherent and residual risk, appetite and tolerance
Qualitative assessment with risk matrices and their known weaknesses
Structured methods: the ISO 27005 process, NIST SP 800-30 and OCTAVE
Quantitative assessment: single and annualised loss expectancy, FAIR and Monte Carlo loss distributions
Risk treatment: avoid, reduce, transfer (including cyber insurance) or accept; the risk register
Risk communication, aggregation and reporting to the board

syllabus.title: Security policy and standards
topics: The document hierarchy: policy, standard, procedure and guideline; writing enforceable policy
Core policies: acceptable use, access control, passwords, remote work and bring-your-own-device
Data classification and handling, retention, privacy policy and data protection impact assessment
Policy lifecycle: approval, exceptions, communication and review
The ISMS: ISO 27001 clauses, scope, statement of applicability and the Plan-Do-Check-Act cycle

syllabus.title: Controls and control frameworks
topics: Control types: preventive, detective, corrective and deterrent; administrative, technical and physical
ISO 27002 and NIST SP 800-53 control families, the CIS Controls and mapping between frameworks
Selecting controls by cost-benefit and risk reduction; defence in depth
Identity and access governance: least privilege, segregation of duties and joiner-mover-leaver processes
Vendor and cloud risk: third-party assessment, shared responsibility and service level agreements
Incident response governance: roles, playbooks, notification duties and lessons learned

syllabus.title: Business continuity and disaster recovery
topics: The business continuity lifecycle (ISO 22301): MTPD, RTO and RPO from the business impact analysis
Continuity strategies: backups, hot, warm and cold sites, cloud failover and manual workarounds; power and connectivity risks in West Africa
Disaster recovery plans, runbooks and call trees
Exercising plans: walkthroughs, tabletop exercises and full failover tests; measuring results
Crisis management and communication with customers, regulators and the media

syllabus.title: Security awareness and human factors
topics: Social engineering: phishing, pretexting, SIM-swap and mobile money fraud
Insider threat: malicious and negligent insiders, monitoring and its ethics
Why people bypass controls: usable security, behavioural models and nudges
Designing awareness programmes and measuring them: phishing simulations and behaviour metrics
Security culture, reporting and a just culture

syllabus.title: Audit and assurance
topics: Audit types and roles: internal, external and certification audits; independence and the audit charter
The audit process: planning, evidence collection, sampling, control testing and findings
Compliance regimes: PCI DSS, SOC 2 and ISO 27001 certification; governance, risk and compliance tooling
Metrics, continuous monitoring and maturity models
Capstone: governance review of a regional bank or utility, producing a risk register and a board report

courses.title: Signals and Systems
topics: Continuous and discrete-time signals
Linear time-invariant systems and convolution
Fourier series
Fourier transform and frequency response
Laplace transform
Sampling and aliasing
The z-transform
courses.description: The mathematics of signals and the systems that transform them: continuous- and discrete-time signals, linear time-invariant systems and convolution, Fourier series and transforms, frequency response, sampling and aliasing, and the Laplace and z-transforms. Every transform is computed by hand and then explored interactively in the browser, where students sketch signals, convolve them and hear the effect of filtering and aliasing.
modelledOn: Oppenheim, Willsky and Nawab, Signals and Systems
Lathi, Linear Systems and Signals
Haykin and Van Veen, Signals and Systems
outcomes: Classify and manipulate continuous- and discrete-time signals and determine the properties of a system from its description.
Compute the response of linear time-invariant systems by convolution and by solving differential and difference equations.
Represent periodic and aperiodic signals with Fourier series and transforms and interpret frequency response in magnitude and phase.
Apply the sampling theorem to choose sampling rates, predict aliasing and design reconstruction.
Analyse causality, stability and transient response with the Laplace transform and the z-transform using poles, zeros and regions of convergence.

syllabus.title: Continuous and discrete-time signals
topics: Continuous-time and discrete-time signals; analogue, sampled and digital signals
Transformations of the independent variable: shifting, scaling and reversal
Even and odd, periodic and aperiodic, energy and power signals
Elementary signals: unit step, unit impulse, ramp, real and complex exponentials, sinusoids
Periodicity of discrete-time sinusoids and the uniqueness of discrete frequencies
Real signals: an ECG trace, a voice recording and a day of national grid electricity demand

syllabus.title: Systems and their properties
topics: Systems as mappings from input to output; block diagram notation
Memory, causality, invertibility and BIBO stability
Linearity and time invariance, with tests and counter-examples
Series, parallel and feedback interconnections
Systems described by linear constant-coefficient differential and difference equations

syllabus.title: Linear time-invariant systems and convolution
topics: Impulse response and the representation of signals as sums of shifted impulses
The convolution sum and the convolution integral; graphical convolution step by step
Properties of convolution: commutative, associative and distributive; LTI systems in series and parallel
Causality, stability and memory read from the impulse response; step response
Solving differential and difference equations: natural and forced response, zero-state and zero-input response
Smoothing daily mobile money transaction counts with a moving-average system

syllabus.title: Fourier series
topics: Complex exponentials as eigenfunctions of LTI systems
Continuous-time Fourier series: synthesis and analysis equations; trigonometric form
Convergence, Dirichlet conditions and the Gibbs phenomenon
Properties of Fourier series and Parseval's relation; line spectra
Discrete-time Fourier series
LTI response to periodic inputs; harmonics drawn from the mains by non-linear loads

syllabus.title: Fourier transform and frequency response
topics: The continuous-time Fourier transform as the limit of the Fourier series; common transform pairs
Properties: linearity, shifting, scaling, duality, differentiation and Parseval's theorem
The convolution and multiplication properties; filtering as multiplication in frequency
The discrete-time Fourier transform and its periodicity
Frequency response: magnitude and phase, group delay, Bode plots; ideal and practical filters
Amplitude modulation and demodulation; how FM radio stations share the spectrum

syllabus.title: Sampling and aliasing
topics: Impulse-train sampling and the Nyquist-Shannon sampling theorem
Aliasing in time and frequency; anti-aliasing filters
Reconstruction: ideal band-limited interpolation, zero-order and first-order hold
Discrete-time processing of continuous-time signals
Quantisation in brief; why telephone speech is sampled at 8 kHz

syllabus.title: The Laplace transform
topics: The bilateral Laplace transform and the region of convergence
Inverse Laplace transform by partial fractions
Properties of the Laplace transform; initial and final value theorems
System functions, poles and zeros; causality and stability in the s-plane
The unilateral transform for differential equations with initial conditions; circuit analysis in the s-domain
Block diagrams and feedback systems; a preview of control

syllabus.title: The z-transform
topics: The z-transform and the region of convergence; common pairs
Inverse z-transform by partial fractions and power series
Properties of the z-transform; convolution becomes multiplication
System functions, poles and zeros, and stability relative to the unit circle
The unilateral z-transform for difference equations with initial conditions
Relating the z-transform, the DTFT and the Laplace transform; mapping the s-plane to the z-plane

syllabus.title: Signals and systems in practice
topics: Removing 50 Hz mains hum from an ECG recording with a notch filter
Communication systems in outline: modulation, multiplexing and channel distortion
State-space descriptions in brief
Capstone: model, simulate and filter a real recorded signal end to end

courses.title: Statistical Inference
topics: Sampling distributions
Point and interval estimation
Hypothesis testing
Comparing groups: t-tests and ANOVA
Categorical data and chi-square tests
Linear regression and its assumptions
Non-parametric and resampling methods
courses.description: Drawing conclusions from samples with stated uncertainty: sampling distributions, estimation, confidence intervals, hypothesis tests, t-tests and ANOVA, chi-square tests for categorical data, linear regression with its assumptions checked, and non-parametric and resampling methods. Every procedure is first watched at work on thousands of simulated samples in the browser, then derived, then applied to real data such as district health records and market prices.
modelledOn: Casella and Berger, Statistical Inference
Wasserman, All of Statistics: A Concise Course in Statistical Inference
Rice, Mathematical Statistics and Data Analysis
Efron and Hastie, Computer Age Statistical Inference
outcomes: Derive and simulate the sampling distributions of common statistics and explain the role of the central limit theorem.
Construct point estimators by the method of moments and maximum likelihood and compare them by bias, variance and mean squared error.
Build and interpret confidence intervals and carry out hypothesis tests, reporting p-values, effect sizes and power correctly.
Compare groups with t-tests, ANOVA and chi-square tests and choose the right test for the design and data type.
Fit linear regression models, check their assumptions with diagnostics and draw valid inferences from the coefficients.
Apply non-parametric tests, the bootstrap and permutation tests when parametric assumptions fail.

syllabus.title: Populations, samples and sampling distributions
topics: Populations, parameters, samples and statistics; simple random, stratified, cluster and systematic sampling; sampling frames and bias
Random variables refresher: expectation, variance, the normal, binomial, Poisson and exponential families
Sampling distribution of the mean and of a proportion; standard error; the law of large numbers
The central limit theorem stated, simulated and its limits with skewed data and small samples
Distributions derived from the normal: chi-square, Student's t and F; their shapes and degrees of freedom
Simulating thousands of household surveys in a Ghanaian district to watch estimates vary

syllabus.title: Point estimation
topics: Estimators and estimates; bias, variance, mean squared error and consistency
Method of moments estimators
Maximum likelihood: the likelihood and log-likelihood, solving the score equation, numerical maximisation
Properties of maximum likelihood estimators: invariance, asymptotic normality, Fisher information and the Cramer-Rao bound
Sufficiency and efficiency in brief; Bayesian point estimates as a contrast

syllabus.title: Interval estimation
topics: Confidence intervals: the pivotal method and what the confidence level does and does not mean
Intervals for a mean with known and unknown variance; intervals for a proportion (Wald, Wilson) and for a variance
Sample size calculation for a desired margin of error; finite population correction
Intervals for differences in means and proportions
Estimating malaria test positivity across district clinics with honest margins of error

syllabus.title: Hypothesis testing
topics: Null and alternative hypotheses; test statistics, rejection regions and p-values; one- and two-sided tests
Type I and type II errors; significance level, power and power curves; sample size for a target power
The Neyman-Pearson lemma and likelihood ratio tests; the duality of tests and confidence intervals
Tests for a mean, a proportion and a variance; z and t tests
Multiple testing: family-wise error, Bonferroni and Holm corrections, false discovery rate with Benjamini-Hochberg
Misuse of p-values, p-hacking and the replication crisis; reporting effect sizes and intervals instead of only significance

syllabus.title: Comparing groups: t-tests and ANOVA
topics: Two-sample t-test with pooled and Welch variances; paired t-test; checking normality and equal variance
One-way analysis of variance: partitioning sums of squares, the F statistic and the ANOVA table
Post hoc comparisons: Tukey's HSD and planned contrasts
Two-way ANOVA with interaction; randomised block designs
Effect sizes: Cohen's d and eta squared; basics of experimental design and randomisation
Comparing maize yields across fertiliser treatments in a field trial

syllabus.title: Categorical data and chi-square tests
topics: Contingency tables; joint, marginal and conditional proportions
Chi-square goodness-of-fit test; expected counts and the small-count rule
Chi-square test of independence and test of homogeneity; standardised residuals
Fisher's exact test; McNemar's test for paired proportions
Measures of association: relative risk, odds ratio and their confidence intervals; Simpson's paradox

syllabus.title: Linear regression and its assumptions
topics: Correlation and simple linear regression by least squares; the regression line and R squared
Inference for slope and intercept; confidence intervals for the mean response and prediction intervals
Multiple regression in matrix form; categorical predictors and interactions; the overall F test
Assumptions and diagnostics: linearity, independence, constant variance, normal errors; residual and Q-Q plots
Leverage, influence and Cook's distance; multicollinearity and variance inflation factors; transformations
Correlation versus causation; confounding and omitted variables
Modelling tomato prices at Kumasi Central Market against season, rainfall and transport cost

syllabus.title: Non-parametric and resampling methods
topics: Rank-based tests: sign test, Wilcoxon signed-rank, Mann-Whitney U and Kruskal-Wallis
Spearman's rank correlation; Kolmogorov-Smirnov test
The bootstrap: resampling, bootstrap standard errors, percentile and BCa confidence intervals
Permutation tests for group differences and correlation
When resampling fails: dependence, very small samples and extreme statistics

syllabus.title: Inference in practice
topics: Choosing a method: a decision guide by question, design and data type
Frequentist and Bayesian inference compared: prior, posterior and credible intervals in brief
Survey data in practice: weights, non-response and design effects
Reproducible analysis and honest reporting; preregistration
Capstone: a full inferential analysis of a public Ghanaian dataset with a written report

courses.title: Web Application Programming I
topics: HTML building blocks and document sections
Lists and tables
Links and images
Forms
Cascading Style Sheets
Responsive HTML
HTML media
JavaScript basics
courses.description: Building web pages that work on every device and every connection: semantic HTML, modern CSS layout, responsive design, media and the JavaScript that brings pages to life. Taught to the depth of a leading front-end web development course.
modelledOn: MDN Web Docs learning pathway
Duckett, HTML and CSS: Design and Build Websites
Duckett, JavaScript and jQuery: Interactive Front-End Web Development
W3C Web Content Accessibility Guidelines
outcomes: Write valid, semantic, accessible HTML documents with correct structure, lists, tables, links, images and forms.
Style pages with CSS selectors, the box model, flexbox and grid, and organise stylesheets maintainably.
Build layouts that adapt to phones, tablets and desktops and remain fast on slow connections.
Embed and control audio, video and canvas content.
Write JavaScript that manipulates the DOM, handles events and validates forms.
Debug and test pages with browser developer tools and publish them to a web host.

syllabus.title: How the Web works and HTML building blocks
topics: Clients, servers, HTTP requests and responses, URLs, browsers and rendering
HTML document structure: doctype, head, body, metadata, character encoding
Elements, attributes, nesting; headings, paragraphs, emphasis, line breaks, comments
Document sections: header, nav, main, article, section, aside, footer; why semantics matter
Validation and developer tools; writing a first multi-page site

syllabus.title: Lists and tables
topics: Ordered, unordered and description lists; nested lists for menus
Tables: rows, cells, headers, caption, thead/tbody/tfoot, rowspan and colspan
Accessible tables with scope and headers; when not to use a table
Tabular data from a Ghanaian school timetable or a market price list

syllabus.title: Links and images
topics: Anchors, absolute and relative URLs, fragments, mailto and tel links; link states
Images: formats (JPEG, PNG, GIF, SVG, WebP), alt text, dimensions, figure and figcaption
Responsive images with srcset and picture; image optimisation for low bandwidth
Icons, favicons and image maps

syllabus.title: Forms
topics: form, input types (text, email, number, date, password, checkbox, radio, file), select, textarea, button
Labels, fieldsets, placeholders and accessibility
HTML5 validation attributes: required, pattern, min, max
GET versus POST and what happens when a form is submitted

syllabus.title: Cascading Style Sheets
topics: Inline, internal and external CSS; selectors (type, class, id, attribute, pseudo-class, pseudo-element); specificity and the cascade
Colour, typography, web fonts, units (px, em, rem, %, vw)
The box model: margin, border, padding, content; box-sizing; display and visibility
Positioning: static, relative, absolute, fixed, sticky; z-index; floats
Flexbox and CSS grid for page layout; alignment and spacing
Transitions, transforms and simple animations; CSS variables; organising stylesheets

syllabus.title: Responsive HTML
topics: Viewport meta tag; fluid layouts; mobile-first design
Media queries for width, orientation and dark mode
Responsive navigation, images and tables
Performance on 2G/3G: minimising requests, compression, lazy loading; testing with throttling
Accessibility basics: contrast, keyboard navigation, ARIA landmarks

syllabus.title: HTML media
topics: audio and video elements, sources, formats, controls, captions with track
Embedding maps, YouTube and other iframes safely
SVG inline graphics and the canvas element
Considerations for data cost and autoplay

syllabus.title: JavaScript basics
topics: Adding scripts; variables (let, const), types, operators, strings, arrays, objects
Functions, arrow functions, conditionals and loops; the console and debugging
The DOM: selecting elements, changing content and styles, creating and removing nodes
Events: click, input, submit, keyboard; event listeners and the event object
Form validation and dynamic forms; local storage
Fetching JSON from an API and rendering it; introduction to promises
Project: a responsive multi-page site with an interactive feature, published to a static host

courses.title: Accounting and Finance for Information Systems
topics: Double-entry bookkeeping
Financial statements
Costing and budgeting
Investment appraisal
Accounting information systems
Payroll and tax basics
Financial controls and fraud
courses.description: The accounting and finance that information systems professionals must understand to build and audit business software: double-entry bookkeeping, financial statements and their analysis, costing and budgeting, investment appraisal, accounting information systems, payroll and tax basics, and the controls that prevent and detect fraud. Every transaction is posted in a simulated ledger in the browser, traced through to the statements, and then implemented as data structures and controls in a small accounting system.
modelledOn: Wood and Sangster, Frank Wood's Business Accounting
Romney and Steinbart, Accounting Information Systems
Drury, Management and Cost Accounting
IFRS Foundation, IFRS for SMEs Accounting Standard
outcomes: Record business transactions by double-entry bookkeeping through journals, ledgers and a trial balance, including period-end adjustments.
Prepare and interpret an income statement, statement of financial position and statement of cash flows, and analyse them with ratios.
Calculate product and service costs, prepare budgets and analyse variances to support management decisions.
Appraise IT and business investments using payback, accounting rate of return, net present value and internal rate of return.
Design the data model, transaction cycles and internal controls of an accounting information system.
Calculate payroll and basic tax obligations and identify control weaknesses that allow fraud.

syllabus.title: Accounting and the business
topics: Why accounting matters to IS professionals; financial versus management accounting
Users of accounting information; the accounting equation: assets, liabilities and equity
Accounting concepts: accruals, going concern, consistency, prudence and materiality
The regulatory framework: IFRS, IFRS for SMEs and the Institute of Chartered Accountants, Ghana
Forms of business: sole traders, partnerships, companies, cooperatives and susu groups

syllabus.title: Double-entry bookkeeping
topics: Debits and credits; the chart of accounts and account types
Books of prime entry: sales, purchases, cash book and general journal; posting to the ledger
Balancing accounts and the trial balance; errors the trial balance does and does not reveal
Period-end adjustments: accruals, prepayments, depreciation, inventory and bad debts
Bank reconciliation, including mobile money wallet and agent float accounts
Bookkeeping for a market trader in Kumasi from sales notebook to ledger

syllabus.title: Financial statements
topics: The income statement: revenue recognition, cost of sales, gross and net profit
The statement of financial position: current and non-current assets and liabilities; equity
The statement of cash flows by the direct and indirect methods; profit versus cash
Ratio analysis: profitability, liquidity, efficiency and gearing ratios; limitations of ratios
Reading the published annual report of a listed company on the Ghana Stock Exchange

syllabus.title: Costing
topics: Cost classification: direct and indirect, fixed and variable, product and period costs
Absorption costing and overhead allocation; activity-based costing
Marginal costing, contribution and cost-volume-profit analysis; break-even charts
Relevant costing for decisions: make or buy, pricing and limiting factors
Costing a bag of processed shea butter for a women's cooperative

syllabus.title: Budgeting and performance
topics: The budgeting process: sales, production, cash and master budgets
Fixed and flexible budgets; variance analysis for materials, labour and overheads
Cash flow forecasting for small businesses and seasonal trades
Budgeting for an IT department: capital and operating expenditure; total cost of ownership

syllabus.title: Investment appraisal
topics: The time value of money: compounding, discounting and annuities
Payback and accounting rate of return
Net present value and internal rate of return; conflicts between them; profitability index
Inflation, high interest rates, risk and sensitivity analysis in investment decisions
Sources of finance: equity, loans, leases, microfinance and mobile lending
Appraising a solar power and server investment for a rural clinic

syllabus.title: Accounting information systems
topics: Transaction processing cycles: revenue, expenditure, production, payroll and financing
Data modelling for accounting: the REA model and relational design of ledgers and journals
Implementing double entry in software: balanced transactions, immutability, reversal entries and rounding
Documentation: data flow diagrams, flowcharts and business process diagrams for AIS
Accounting packages, ERP finance modules and cloud accounting for SMEs; e-invoicing
Integrating mobile money payments and bank feeds

syllabus.title: Payroll and tax basics
topics: Payroll calculation: gross pay, allowances, overtime and net pay
Statutory deductions in Ghana: PAYE income tax bands and SSNIT pension tiers
Value added tax and related levies; withholding tax; filing with the Ghana Revenue Authority
Payroll systems, payslips and posting payroll to the general ledger
Corporate tax principles and tax compliance for small businesses

syllabus.title: Financial controls and fraud
topics: Internal control frameworks: the COSO components of control
Segregation of duties, authorisation, reconciliation and physical controls; application controls in software
The fraud triangle; common frauds: ghost employees, fictitious suppliers, skimming and lapping
Audit trails, continuous auditing, Benford's law and data analytics for fraud detection
Capstone: building and auditing a small double-entry accounting system for a susu group

courses.title: Assembly Language and Microprocessors
topics: Microprocessor architecture and registers
Instruction formats and addressing modes
Arithmetic and logic instructions
Branching, loops and subroutines
Stack and interrupts
Memory and I/O interfacing
Assembling, linking and debugging
courses.description: Programming a processor in its own language: registers, instruction encoding, addressing modes, the stack, interrupts and the bus that connects the CPU to memory and devices. Taught to the depth of a leading machine-level programming and computer organisation course.
modelledOn: Patterson and Hennessy, Computer Organization and Design (RISC-V edition)
Bryant and O'Hallaron, Computer Systems: A Programmer's Perspective (machine-level chapters)
Mazidi, Causey and Naimi, The x86 PC: Assembly Language, Design and Interfacing
outcomes: Describe the register set, buses, flags and instruction cycle of a microprocessor and the role of each pin and signal.
Decode and encode instructions and choose the right addressing mode for a data access.
Write assembly programs with arithmetic, logic, branching, loops and subroutines that follow a calling convention.
Use the stack for calls, locals and interrupts, and write an interrupt service routine.
Interface memory and I/O devices to a processor with address decoding and polling or interrupts.
Assemble, link, trace and debug programs, and relate compiled C to the assembly it produces.

syllabus.title: Microprocessor architecture and registers
topics: Von Neumann and Harvard architectures; CPU, memory and I/O on address, data and control buses
Inside the CPU: ALU, general-purpose and special registers, program counter, stack pointer, flags
The fetch-decode-execute cycle; clock, machine cycles and timing diagrams
Case processors: the 8086/x86 family, ARM Cortex-M and RISC-V compared; choosing one for the labs
Running programs in a simulator or on a real board; the assembler and debugger toolchain

syllabus.title: Instruction formats and addressing modes
topics: Instruction fields: opcode, operands, immediates; fixed and variable length encodings
Machine code by hand: encoding and decoding a few instructions
Addressing modes: immediate, register, direct, indirect, indexed, base-plus-offset, PC-relative
Data in memory: endianness, alignment, segments or flat memory
Accessing arrays and structures with addressing modes

syllabus.title: Data movement, arithmetic and logic instructions
topics: MOV, loads and stores; constants and labels; data directives
ADD, SUB, ADC, SBB, INC, DEC, NEG; multi-word arithmetic with the carry flag
MUL, IMUL, DIV, IDIV and their quirks; signed versus unsigned
AND, OR, XOR, NOT, TEST; shifts and rotates; masking and bit manipulation
Flags after each instruction; comparing and setting
BCD and ASCII arithmetic; converting numbers to printable strings

syllabus.title: Branching, loops and subroutines
topics: Unconditional and conditional jumps; translating if-else and switch
Loops: counted, while and do-while patterns; loop instructions
CALL and RET; passing arguments in registers and on the stack; return values
Calling conventions: caller- and callee-saved registers, stack frames, recursion
String and block instructions; writing strlen, strcpy and a bubble sort in assembly
Reading compiler output: how C becomes assembly

syllabus.title: Stack and interrupts
topics: Stack organisation, PUSH and POP, stack overflow and underflow
Local variables and the frame pointer
Interrupt types: hardware, software, exceptions; the interrupt vector table
Interrupt sequence: saving state, the service routine, returning; priorities and nesting
Writing an interrupt handler for a timer or key press
System calls on Linux or DOS: writing to the console and exiting

syllabus.title: Memory and I/O interfacing
topics: Memory map and address decoding with gates and decoders; RAM and ROM chips on the bus
Memory-mapped versus port-mapped I/O; IN and OUT
Parallel I/O with the 8255 or a GPIO port; LEDs, switches, seven-segment displays
Serial I/O with a UART; timers and counters
Polling versus interrupts; DMA in brief
Bus timing and wait states

syllabus.title: Assembling, linking and debugging
topics: Two-pass assembly, symbol tables, object files, relocation and linking
Macros, conditional assembly and include files
Mixing C and assembly: inline assembly and calling assembly from C
Debugging: breakpoints, single-stepping, watching registers and memory, disassembly

courses.title: Computer Networking II
topics: Routing and switching
VLANs
Access lists
DNS and DHCP
Basic WAN concepts
Point-to-Point Protocol
Frame Relay
Network Address Translation
Bandwidth, response time, reliability and QoS
courses.description: Routing, switching and the services that make a campus or enterprise network run: VLANs, access lists, DNS and DHCP, WAN links, NAT and quality of service, all configured and tested in the simulator. Taught to the depth of the industry routing-and-switching certification and a leading networking course.

Kurose and Ross, Computer Networking: A Top-Down Approach
Odom, CCNA 200-301 Official Cert Guide

Design and configure VLANs, trunks, inter-VLAN routing and spanning tree on switched networks.
Write standard and extended access control lists to enforce a stated security policy.
Deploy DNS and DHCP services and troubleshoot name and address assignment faults.
Explain WAN technologies and configure PPP, Frame Relay and NAT on a border router.
Measure bandwidth, response time and reliability and apply QoS to protect voice and critical traffic.

syllabus.title: Routing fundamentals

Static routes, default routes, administrative distance and metrics
Distance-vector routing: Bellman-Ford, RIP, count-to-infinity, split horizon
Link-state routing: Dijkstra, OSPF areas, LSAs, neighbour adjacency
Path-vector routing and BGP: autonomous systems, policies, how Ghana's ISPs peer
Configuring and verifying RIP and OSPF in Packet Tracer or GNS3

EtherChannel and link aggregation

syllabus.title: VLANs
topics: Why VLANs: broadcast domains, segmentation, security
Creating VLANs, assigning access ports, 802.1Q trunking and the native VLAN
Inter-VLAN routing: router-on-a-stick and layer-3 switches
VLAN design for a university: staff, students, labs, management, voice
Troubleshooting VLAN and trunk mismatches

syllabus.title: Access control lists
topics: ACL logic: top-down matching, implicit deny, wildcard masks
Standard and extended numbered and named ACLs; placement rules
Applying ACLs to interfaces and to VTY lines; logging
Writing ACLs for a policy: block social media in labs, allow only web and DNS from guests
IPv6 ACLs in brief

syllabus.title: DNS and DHCP
topics: DNS hierarchy, resolvers, authoritative servers, record types (A, AAAA, CNAME, MX, NS, PTR, TXT), TTL and caching
Setting up a DNS server; split-horizon and internal zones; DNS over HTTPS in brief
DHCP discover-offer-request-acknowledge; pools, leases, reservations, options; DHCP relay
Troubleshooting name resolution and address assignment with dig, nslookup and packet capture

syllabus.title: Basic WAN concepts

VPNs over the Internet: site-to-site and remote-access, IPsec and WireGuard in brief
WAN options for connecting branches across Ghana and their costs

syllabus.title: Point-to-Point Protocol
topics: PPP frame, LCP and NCP phases; options negotiation
Authentication with PAP and CHAP
Configuring and verifying PPP on serial links; PPPoE for broadband
Multilink PPP and compression

syllabus.title: Frame Relay
topics: Virtual circuits, DLCIs, LMI, Inverse ARP; hub-and-spoke topologies
Committed information rate, bursting, FECN/BECN and discard eligibility
Configuring Frame Relay point-to-point and multipoint subinterfaces; split-horizon issues
Legacy status of Frame Relay and what replaced it (MPLS, Metro Ethernet)

syllabus.title: Network Address Translation
topics: Private addressing and the reasons for NAT; inside and outside, local and global addresses
Static NAT, dynamic NAT, PAT (overload); configuring and verifying translations
Port forwarding for hosting a server behind NAT; NAT traversal problems for VoIP and peer-to-peer
Carrier-grade NAT and IPv6 as the long-term fix

syllabus.title: Bandwidth, response time, reliability and QoS
topics: Measuring bandwidth, latency, jitter and packet loss; iperf, ping, SNMP graphs; SLAs
Redundancy and reliability: HSRP/VRRP, link redundancy, MTBF and availability calculations
QoS models: best effort, IntServ, DiffServ; classification, marking (DSCP), queuing, policing, shaping
Configuring QoS for VoIP and video on a congested link
Capacity planning and a network design project for a campus with a WAN link to a branch

courses.title: Data Structures and Algorithms
topics: Data structures and abstract data types

Lists
Stacks and queues
Recursion

Trees
Graphs

courses.description: The classic data structures and algorithm design techniques, each analysed for correctness and running time and implemented in C++ with tests. Taught to the depth of a leading algorithms course.

Sedgewick and Wayne, Algorithms
Kleinberg and Tardos, Algorithm Design
Weiss, Data Structures and Algorithm Analysis in C++

Analyse the time and space complexity of iterative and recursive algorithms, including amortised analysis.
Implement and choose among lists, stacks, queues, hash tables, balanced trees, heaps and graphs.
Implement and compare sorting and searching algorithms and justify their bounds.
Apply greedy, divide-and-conquer, dynamic programming, randomised and backtracking techniques to new problems.

syllabus.title: Data structures, abstract data types and analysis of algorithms
topics: Abstract data types versus implementations; interfaces, invariants and encapsulation in C++ classes and templates
Models of computation; counting operations; best, worst and average case
Asymptotic notation: O, Omega, Theta; growth rates and limits
Analysing loops and nested loops; recurrences and the master theorem
Amortised analysis: dynamic arrays and the aggregate and accounting methods
Measuring running time experimentally and comparing with theory

syllabus.title: Lists, stacks and queues
topics: Array lists and dynamic resizing; singly, doubly and circular linked lists; iterators
Stacks: array and linked implementations; expression evaluation, balanced brackets, undo
Queues and deques; circular buffers; priority queue as an ADT
The C++ STL: vector, list, deque, stack, queue and their complexity guarantees

syllabus.title: Recursion
topics: Recursive thinking and the call stack; base cases and progress
Recursion versus iteration; tail recursion; memoisation
Classic problems: permutations, subsets, Tower of Hanoi, flood fill, binary search
Proving recursive algorithms correct by induction

syllabus.title: Sorting

Merge sort and quicksort: analysis, pivot choice, randomised quicksort

Hash functions, uniform hashing, universal hashing

Hash tables in practice: unordered_map, string hashing, Bloom filters
Applications: dictionaries, counting, deduplication, caching

syllabus.title: Trees
topics: Tree terminology; binary trees and traversals (preorder, inorder, postorder, level order)
Binary search trees: search, insert, delete; expected height
Balanced trees: AVL rotations; red-black trees; 2-3 trees and B-trees for disks
Tries and suffix trees for strings; Huffman coding trees
Augmented trees: order statistics, interval trees; segment trees and Fenwick trees
std::map and std::set and their guarantees

syllabus.title: Graphs
topics: Graph representations: adjacency matrix and list; weighted and directed graphs
Breadth-first and depth-first search; connected components; cycle detection
Topological sort and DAGs; strongly connected components
Shortest paths: Dijkstra with a heap, Bellman-Ford, Floyd-Warshall; the tro-tro route problem
