Randomised algorithms: randomised quicksort, hashing, Monte Carlo and Las Vegas
Backtracking and branch-and-bound: N-queens, sudoku, subset sum
Introduction to NP-completeness and what to do when no fast algorithm is known

courses.title: Data Visualisation
topics: Principles of visual perception
Choosing the right chart
Colour, labels and annotation
Plotting with code
Interactive and web-based visualisation
Maps and geographic data
Data storytelling and avoiding misleading charts
courses.description: Turning data into charts and maps that people read correctly: how visual perception works, choosing the right chart for the question, colour, labelling and annotation, plotting with code, interactive web visualisation, geographic data and maps, and telling an honest story with data. Munzner, Visualization Analysis and Design
Wilke, Fundamentals of Data Visualization
Cairo, How Charts Lie: Getting Smarter about Visual Information

syllabus.title: Why visualise and the data behind a chart
topics: Exploration versus explanation; Anscombe's quartet and the Datasaurus dozen
Data types: nominal, ordinal, interval, ratio, temporal and spatial; tidy data and long versus wide formats
Munzner's what, why and how framework: data abstraction, task abstraction and idioms
A short history: Playfair, Nightingale, Minard, Snow and Tukey

syllabus.title: Principles of visual perception
topics: Preattentive processing and pop-out; visual search
Marks and channels; the ranking of channels for quantitative and categorical data (Cleveland and McGill, Mackinlay)
Gestalt principles: proximity, similarity, enclosure, connection, continuity and closure
Weber's law, area and angle judgement errors; why 3D and pie charts mislead
Change blindness, working memory limits and the data-ink ratio

syllabus.title: Choosing the right chart

Distributions: histograms and bin width, density plots, box plots, violin and strip plots

syllabus.title: Colour, labels and annotation

Sequential, diverging and qualitative palettes; why the rainbow scale misleads
Colour-vision deficiency, contrast ratios and accessible chart design
Titles that state the finding, direct labelling instead of legends, axis and tick choices

syllabus.title: Plotting with code

Symbol, dot-density and flow maps; cartograms and hexagonal tile maps
Web maps with tiles and a library such as Leaflet; simplifying geometries for small downloads
Mapping rainfall across northern Ghana and access to health facilities by district

syllabus.title: Data storytelling and avoiding misleading charts
topics: Narrative structures: martini glass, drill-down and scrollytelling; knowing the audience

Misleading techniques: truncated and dual axes, cherry-picked ranges, area distortion, hidden denominators

courses.title: Design and Analysis of Algorithms

Divide and conquer
Dynamic programming

Graph algorithms and network flow
NP-completeness and reductions

courses.description: The core paradigms for designing algorithms and the mathematics for proving how fast and how correct they are: divide and conquer, dynamic programming, greedy methods, graph and flow algorithms, NP-completeness, and randomised and approximation methods. modelledOn: Cormen, Leiserson, Rivest and Stein, Introduction to Algorithms
Kleinberg and Tardos, Algorithm Design
Dasgupta, Papadimitriou and Vazirani, Algorithms
Sedgewick and Wayne, Algorithms
outcomes: Analyse the running time and space of an algorithm using asymptotic notation, recurrences and amortised analysis.
Choose and apply divide and conquer, dynamic programming or a greedy strategy to a new problem and prove it correct.
Solve shortest-path, spanning-tree, matching and maximum-flow problems and justify the choice of algorithm.
Prove a problem NP-complete by a polynomial-time reduction and recognise intractable problems in practice.
Design and analyse randomised and approximation algorithms with stated expected-time or approximation guarantees.
Compare predicted and measured performance and explain any gap.

syllabus.title: Foundations of algorithm analysis
topics: The RAM model, input size, and worst-case, average-case and best-case analysis
Big-O, Omega, Theta and little-o: definitions, proofs from the definition, growth-rate ordering
Analysing loops and nested loops; common summations
Solving recurrences: substitution method and recursion trees
The master theorem and when it does not apply

Quicksort with random pivots and its expected running time
Linear-time selection with median of medians
Integer multiplication by Karatsuba and fast matrix multiplication with seven products

syllabus.title: Dynamic programming
topics: Optimal substructure and overlapping subproblems; memoisation versus tabulation
Longest common subsequence and edit distance
0/1 knapsack and pseudo-polynomial time
Matrix-chain multiplication and optimal binary search trees
Shortest paths by dynamic programming: Bellman-Ford and DAG paths
Reconstructing solutions and reducing space

syllabus.title: Greedy algorithms and matroids
topics: The greedy-choice property and exchange arguments; interval scheduling

Minimum spanning trees: the cut property, Kruskal and Prim

topics: Breadth-first and depth-first search, topological sort, strongly connected components

ISO 20022 and ISO 8583 financial messaging standards
PCI DSS (Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard)
GSMA Mobile Money API specification and Mobile Money Certification

syllabus.title: Money, payments and payment systems

syllabus.title: Error analysis and floating point

IEEE 754 floating point: mantissa, exponent, machine epsilon, overflow, underflow, NaN
Absolute and relative error; significant digits; loss of significance and cancellation
Propagation of error; conditioning and stability of algorithms
Taylor series as the basis of numerical methods; order of convergence and big-O
Setting up Python with NumPy, or MATLAB, and writing reusable numerical routines

syllabus.title: Nonlinear equations in one variable
topics: Bisection: bracketing, error bound, number of iterations
Fixed-point iteration and the contraction condition
Newton's method: derivation, quadratic convergence, failure cases, multiple roots
Secant and false-position methods; Muller's method in brief
Roots of polynomials: Horner's scheme, deflation; stopping criteria and convergence acceleration (Aitken)
Applications: break-even and interest-rate calculations, projectile range

syllabus.title: Direct methods for linear systems
topics: Gaussian elimination with partial and scaled pivoting; operation counts
LU, Cholesky and LDL decompositions; solving multiple right-hand sides
Matrix norms, condition number and error bounds; ill-conditioned systems (Hilbert matrix)
Tridiagonal and banded systems; Thomas algorithm
Linear least squares via normal equations and QR

syllabus.title: Iterative methods and eigenvalue approximation
topics: Jacobi, Gauss-Seidel and SOR; convergence conditions and diagonal dominance
Conjugate gradient in brief for large sparse systems
Power method and inverse power method for dominant and smallest eigenvalues; Rayleigh quotient
QR algorithm for all eigenvalues; Gershgorin circles
Applications: PageRank, vibration modes, principal components

syllabus.title: Interpolation, curve fitting and polynomial approximation
topics: Lagrange and Newton divided-difference interpolation; error term; Runge's phenomenon
Hermite interpolation; Chebyshev nodes
Piecewise interpolation and cubic splines (natural and clamped)
Least-squares curve fitting: linear, polynomial and linearised exponential models
Orthogonal polynomials and approximation; Bezier curves for graphics
Fitting rainfall or sales data and judging the fit

syllabus.title: Numerical differentiation and integration
topics: Forward, backward and central difference formulas; error and step-size trade-off; Richardson extrapolation
Newton-Cotes rules: trapezoidal, Simpson's, higher order; composite rules and error bounds
Romberg integration; adaptive quadrature
Gaussian quadrature; improper and multiple integrals
Applications: area under measured curves, work and energy, probability from densities

syllabus.title: Initial value problems and ODEs
topics: Existence and well-posedness; Euler's method and its global error
Taylor methods; Runge-Kutta methods including classical RK4; adaptive step size (RK45)
Multistep methods: Adams-Bashforth and Adams-Moulton; predictor-corrector
Systems of ODEs and higher-order equations; stiffness and implicit methods
Stability regions; choosing a method

courses.title: Optimisation for Machine Learning
topics: Convex sets and functions
Gradient descent and its variants
Stochastic optimisation
Momentum and adaptive methods
Constrained optimisation and Lagrange multipliers
Second-order methods
Optimisation in practice: tuning and diagnostics
courses.description: The optimisation theory and algorithms that train machine learning models: convex sets and functions, gradient descent and its convergence, stochastic and mini-batch methods, momentum and adaptive methods such as Adam, constrained optimisation with Lagrange multipliers and duality, second-order and quasi-Newton methods, and the practice of tuning and diagnosing training. Every algorithm is derived, implemented from scratch and watched moving across loss surfaces in the browser before it is used on real models.
modelledOn: Boyd and Vandenberghe, Convex Optimization
Nocedal and Wright, Numerical Optimization
Beck, First-Order Methods in Optimization
Goodfellow, Bengio and Courville, Deep Learning (optimisation chapters)
outcomes: Formulate learning problems as optimisation problems and recognise when they are convex.
Prove and apply the convergence properties of gradient descent under smoothness and strong convexity.
Implement stochastic, mini-batch, momentum and adaptive methods and explain their trade-offs in noise, speed and memory.
Solve constrained problems with Lagrange multipliers, KKT conditions and duality, including the support vector machine.
Apply Newton, quasi-Newton and other second-order methods and judge when their cost is justified.
Diagnose and tune training in practice using learning-rate schedules, gradient checks and loss curves.

syllabus.title: Optimisation problems in machine learning
topics: Empirical risk minimisation as an optimisation problem; loss functions and regularisers
Calculus refresher: gradients, Jacobians, Hessians, directional derivatives and Taylor expansions
Local and global minima, saddle points; first- and second-order optimality conditions
Visualising loss surfaces and level sets for linear regression, logistic regression and small networks

syllabus.title: Convex sets and functions
topics: Convex sets: hyperplanes, half-spaces, balls, polyhedra and cones; operations that preserve convexity
Convex functions: definitions, first- and second-order conditions, Jensen's inequality
Operations that preserve convexity; common convex losses in machine learning
Strong convexity, Lipschitz continuity and smoothness; condition number of a problem
Subgradients and non-smooth convex functions such as the L1 norm and hinge loss
Convex problem classes: least squares, linear and quadratic programming

syllabus.title: Gradient descent and its variants
topics: Gradient descent derived from a quadratic upper bound; step size choice
Convergence rates for smooth convex and strongly convex functions
Line search: exact, backtracking and the Armijo and Wolfe conditions
Ill-conditioning, zig-zagging and the role of feature scaling and preconditioning
Subgradient methods, proximal gradient descent and ISTA for lasso
Coordinate descent

syllabus.title: Stochastic optimisation
topics: Stochastic gradient descent: unbiased gradient estimates and their variance
Mini-batches, sampling with and without replacement, epochs and shuffling
Convergence of SGD with decreasing step sizes; the noise ball
Variance reduction: SVRG and SAGA
Generalisation and the implicit regularisation of SGD; large-batch training
Training on a laptop with limited memory: streaming data and small batches

syllabus.title: Momentum and adaptive methods
topics: Heavy-ball momentum and Nesterov accelerated gradient; optimal rates for first-order methods
Adaptive learning rates: AdaGrad, RMSProp and Adam; bias correction
AdamW and decoupled weight decay; when adaptive methods generalise worse
Comparing optimisers on the same problem and reading their trajectories

syllabus.title: Constrained optimisation and Lagrange multipliers
topics: Equality constraints and Lagrange multipliers; geometric interpretation
Inequality constraints and the Karush-Kuhn-Tucker conditions
Lagrangian duality: the dual function, weak and strong duality, Slater's condition
The support vector machine as a quadratic program; the dual and the kernel trick
Projected gradient descent, penalty and barrier methods; an overview of interior-point methods
Allocating a fertiliser budget across farms as a constrained problem

syllabus.title: Second-order methods
topics: Newton's method: derivation, quadratic convergence and damped Newton
Gauss-Newton and Levenberg-Marquardt for least squares; iteratively reweighted least squares for logistic regression
Quasi-Newton methods: BFGS and limited-memory L-BFGS
Hessian-vector products, conjugate gradient and Hessian-free optimisation
Cost and memory of second-order methods at scale

syllabus.title: Optimisation in practice: tuning and diagnostics
topics: Non-convex optimisation in deep learning: saddle points, plateaus and the loss landscape
Learning-rate schedules: step decay, cosine annealing, warm-up and the learning-rate range test
Initialisation, normalisation and gradient clipping; vanishing and exploding gradients
Diagnostics: gradient checking, loss curves, divergence and NaNs; reproducibility and random seeds
Hyperparameter optimisation: grid, random, Bayesian optimisation and early stopping
Capstone: implementing and benchmarking optimisers on a real model with a written analysis

courses.title: Sensors and Actuators
topics: Sensing principles
Position, speed and distance sensors
Inertial and environmental sensors
Signal conditioning
DC, stepper and servo motors
Motor drivers and power
Sensor fusion basics
courses.description: How machines measure the physical world and act on it: sensing principles and sensor characteristics, position, speed and distance sensors, inertial and environmental sensors, signal conditioning and data conversion, DC, stepper and servo motors, motor drivers and power electronics, and the basics of fusing several sensors into one estimate. Practised in browser-based circuit and motor simulations with virtual instruments, building towards field devices such as soil-moisture irrigation controllers and line-following delivery robots.
modelledOn: Fraden, Handbook of Modern Sensors: Physics, Designs, and Applications
Bolton, Mechatronics: Electronic Control Systems in Mechanical and Electrical Engineering
Hughes and Drury, Electric Motors and Drives: Fundamentals, Types and Applications
Horowitz and Hill, The Art of Electronics
outcomes: Explain the physical principles behind common transducers and characterise a sensor by its range, sensitivity, resolution, accuracy, linearity and dynamic response.
Select and interface position, speed, distance, inertial and environmental sensors for a given measurement task and calibrate them.
Design signal conditioning circuits with bridges, amplifiers and filters and choose sampling rates and ADC resolution to avoid aliasing and quantisation error.
Model DC, stepper and servo motors and select a motor and gearing from torque, speed and power requirements.
Design motor drive circuits with H-bridges, PWM and protection and size power supplies and batteries for a mobile system.
Combine readings from several sensors with complementary and Kalman filters to estimate orientation and position.

syllabus.title: Sensing principles
topics: Measurement systems: transducer, conditioning, conversion, processing; sensors and actuators in a control loop

Static characteristics: range, sensitivity, resolution, accuracy, precision, linearity, hysteresis, offset and drift
Dynamic characteristics: first- and second-order response, time constant, bandwidth, settling time
Errors and uncertainty: systematic and random error, noise, calibration curves and least-squares fitting
Reading sensor datasheets and choosing a sensor against cost, power and environment

syllabus.title: Position, speed and distance sensors

Rotary and linear encoders: incremental quadrature decoding, absolute encoders, counts per revolution
Speed measurement from encoder pulses, tachogenerators and frequency or period counting
Distance sensing: ultrasonic time of flight, infrared triangulation, optical time-of-flight and lidar in outline
Proximity and line sensors: inductive, capacitive and reflective optical; a line-following array for a delivery robot
Error sources: echo dropouts, temperature effects on the speed of sound, surface reflectivity

syllabus.title: Inertial and environmental sensors
topics: MEMS accelerometers and gyroscopes: proof masses, capacitive sensing, bias, noise density and drift
Magnetometers and compass heading; hard- and soft-iron calibration
Temperature sensing: thermistors, RTDs, thermocouples with cold-junction compensation, digital sensors
Humidity, pressure, light and gas sensors; soil moisture by resistive and capacitive probes
Strain gauges and load cells for weighing produce; the Wheatstone bridge
Sensors for agriculture and weather stations in Ghana: rainfall gauges, soil moisture and grain storage monitoring

syllabus.title: Signal conditioning
topics: Voltage dividers, bridges and current loops (4-20 mA) for industrial sensors
Operational amplifier circuits: inverting, non-inverting, differential and instrumentation amplifiers
Analogue filtering: passive and active RC filters, anti-aliasing filter design
Sampling and the Nyquist criterion; ADC resolution, reference voltage, quantisation noise, oversampling
Digital filtering of sensor data: moving average, exponential smoothing, median filters
Noise, grounding, shielding and protection against ESD and overvoltage

syllabus.title: DC, stepper and servo motors
topics: Electromagnetic principles: force on a conductor, back EMF, torque constant
Brushed DC motors: equivalent circuit, torque-speed curve, efficiency, transfer function model
Brushless DC motors and electronic commutation in outline
Stepper motors: permanent-magnet and hybrid types, full, half and microstepping, holding torque, missed steps
RC servos and closed-loop position control; PID control of motor speed in outline
Gearing, inertia matching and selecting a motor for a robot wheel or irrigation valve; solenoids and relays as actuators

syllabus.title: Motor drivers and power
topics: Switching loads with transistors and MOSFETs; flyback diodes and inductive kickback
H-bridges for direction and braking; PWM speed control, switching frequency and current ripple
Stepper drivers with current chopping; integrated driver ICs and their thermal limits
Current sensing, overcurrent and thermal protection; electrical noise from motors
Power supplies, regulators and batteries: capacity, discharge rates, lithium and lead-acid chemistries
Solar power budgeting for an off-grid pump or sensor node

syllabus.title: Sensor fusion basics and project
topics: Why fuse sensors: complementary strengths and uncorrelated errors
Complementary filter for tilt from an accelerometer and gyroscope
The one-dimensional Kalman filter: prediction, update, covariance; tuning noise parameters
Dead reckoning from wheel encoders corrected with other sensors

courses.title: Sequence Analysis and Alignment
topics: Sequences and file formats
Pairwise alignment with dynamic programming
Scoring matrices and gap penalties
Database search with BLAST
Multiple sequence alignment
Motifs and profiles
Hidden Markov models for sequences
courses.description: Comparing DNA and protein sequences computationally: sequence formats and databases, pairwise alignment by dynamic programming, substitution matrices and gap penalties, BLAST database search and its statistics, multiple sequence alignment, motifs and profiles, and hidden Markov models for sequence families. Practised by implementing the core algorithms in the browser and applying them to public data such as the haemoglobin beta gene behind sickle cell disease and Plasmodium falciparum drug-resistance genes.
modelledOn: Durbin, Eddy, Krogh and Mitchison, Biological Sequence Analysis: Probabilistic Models of Proteins and Nucleic Acids
Mount, Bioinformatics: Sequence and Genome Analysis
Pevsner, Bioinformatics and Functional Genomics
Jones and Pevzner, An Introduction to Bioinformatics Algorithms
outcomes: Retrieve, parse and convert nucleotide and protein sequences in FASTA, GenBank and FASTQ formats and navigate the major public sequence databases.
Derive and implement global, local and semi-global alignment by dynamic programming, including affine gap penalties and traceback.
Explain how PAM and BLOSUM substitution matrices are built from log-odds scores and choose matrices and gap penalties suited to a comparison.
Search sequence databases with BLAST and interpret bit scores, E-values and alignment coverage when judging homology.
Construct and assess multiple sequence alignments and summarise conserved regions as consensus sequences, position weight matrices and sequence logos.
Build and apply hidden Markov models with the Viterbi, forward and Baum-Welch algorithms to gene finding and protein family classification.

syllabus.title: Biological sequences, formats and databases
topics: From the central dogma to data: DNA, RNA and protein alphabets; codons, reading frames and translation
Sequence file formats: FASTA, GenBank flat files, FASTQ with Phred quality scores; parsing them in code
Primary and curated databases: GenBank, ENA, RefSeq, UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot, Ensembl; accession numbers and versions
Basic sequence operations: reverse complement, GC content, k-mer counting, open reading frame finding
Retrieving the human HBB gene with the sickle cell mutation (Glu6Val) and Plasmodium falciparum genes from public databases

syllabus.title: Dot plots and the alignment problem

Dot plots with windows and stringency; spotting repeats, inversions and domain duplications
Edit distance and the alignment as a path through a grid; how many possible alignments there are
Recursion with memoisation versus tabulation; why brute force fails

syllabus.title: Pairwise alignment with dynamic programming
topics: Needleman-Wunsch global alignment: recurrence, initialisation, filling the matrix, traceback
Smith-Waterman local alignment and semi-global (overlap) alignment; when each is appropriate
Affine gap penalties with Gotoh's three-matrix algorithm; gap opening versus extension
Time and space complexity; linear-space alignment with Hirschberg's divide and conquer
Banded alignment for long similar sequences; implementing and visualising each algorithm step by step

syllabus.title: Scoring matrices and gap penalties

Low-complexity filtering, repeat masking and avoiding false positives
Iterative profile search with PSI-BLAST; the risk of profile drift
Identifying an unknown pathogen sequence or a resistance gene such as pfcrt or pfkelch13 by BLAST

syllabus.title: Multiple sequence alignment
topics: Why multiple alignment is hard: the sum-of-pairs objective and NP-hardness

syllabus.title: Motifs and profiles
topics: Consensus sequences, regular-expression patterns and PROSITE

Scanning sequences with a weight matrix for transcription factor binding sites
Motif discovery by expectation maximisation (MEME) and Gibbs sampling

Viterbi decoding, the forward and backward algorithms, posterior decoding; working in log space
Parameter estimation by counting and by Baum-Welch expectation maximisation

Gene finding with HMMs: exons, introns and splice signals

syllabus.title: Applications and project
topics: Reproducible sequence analysis with Biopython and notebooks; recording tool versions and parameters

Annotating a newly sequenced gene: search, align, identify domains, predict function

courses.description: How to tell whether an intervention caused an outcome, from randomised experiments and A/B tests to observational designs such as matching, difference-in-differences and instrumental variables. Angrist and Pischke, Mostly Harmless Econometrics
Kohavi, Tang and Xu, Trustworthy Online Controlled Experiments

Design, randomise and analyse an experiment, including blocking, clustering and noncompliance.

Estimate treatment effects from observational data with matching, weighting, regression, difference-in-differences and instrumental variables.
Read a causal graph to choose adjustment sets and avoid collider and mediator bias.
Assess how sensitive a causal conclusion is to unmeasured confounding and report it honestly.

syllabus.title: Causal questions and potential outcomes
topics: Association versus causation; Simpson's paradox with a worked example

Estimands: average treatment effect, effect on the treated, conditional effects; SUTVA and interference

syllabus.title: Randomised experiments

Sentence processing: garden-path sentences, incremental parsing and surprisal

Deductive reasoning: the Wason selection task, mental logic versus mental models
Problem solving and analogy: means-ends analysis, insight and structure mapping

syllabus.title: Decision making and heuristics
topics: Expected utility theory and its violations: the Allais and Ellsberg paradoxes
Prospect theory: reference dependence, loss aversion and probability weighting
Heuristics and biases: availability, representativeness, anchoring and base-rate neglect
Bounded rationality: satisficing and fast-and-frugal heuristics such as take-the-best
Bayesian cognition: probabilistic judgement, calibration and the Brier score
Choice architecture and nudges in everyday finance such as mobile money savings and loans

syllabus.title: Neural models of cognition
topics: Neurons, synapses and cortical areas; EEG, fMRI and what imaging can and cannot show
Connectionist models: perceptrons, Hebbian learning and backpropagation
Parallel distributed processing models of word reading and past-tense formation
Attractor networks, competitive learning and self-organising maps
Deep networks and the ventral visual stream; representational similarity analysis
Predictive coding and reinforcement-learning accounts of dopamine and the basal ganglia

syllabus.title: Human-AI interaction and trust
topics: Mental models of AI systems; anthropomorphism and the ELIZA effect
Trust calibration, automation bias and over-reliance on advice
Explanations people can use: cognitive load, explanation types and their evaluation
Human-AI teaming in practice: clinic triage support and crop-advice apps for smallholder farmers
Fairness perceptions, ethics of studying people and responsible reporting

syllabus.title: Synthesis project
topics: Choosing a phenomenon and building a cognitive model of it
Fitting to human benchmark data and comparing against a null model
Critical evaluation: parameters, falsifiability and model comparison with AIC
Open questions: common sense, consciousness and the limits of current AI

courses.title: Computer Graphics
topics: Raster and vector graphics
Line and circle drawing algorithms
2D and 3D transformations
Viewing and projection
Clipping and hidden surfaces
Shading and lighting
Introduction to WebGL
courses.description: From putting a pixel on the screen to rendering lit, shaded 3D scenes in the browser: rasterisation algorithms, transformations, viewing, clipping, visibility, shading and a working WebGL pipeline. Taught to the depth of a leading introductory computer graphics course.
modelledOn: Marschner and Shirley, Fundamentals of Computer Graphics
Hearn, Baker and Carithers, Computer Graphics with OpenGL
Cantor and Jones, WebGL Beginner's Guide
outcomes: Explain raster and vector representations, colour models and the graphics pipeline.
Implement line, circle and polygon rasterisation and filling algorithms and anti-aliasing.
Compose 2D and 3D transformations with homogeneous matrices and quaternions.
Set up cameras, projections and viewports and clip primitives against the view volume.
Resolve visibility with z-buffer and related methods and shade surfaces with Phong and physically based models.
Write WebGL programs with vertex and fragment shaders, buffers, textures and interaction.

syllabus.title: Raster and vector graphics
topics: Images as pixel grids; frame buffers, resolution, colour depth; displays from CRT to OLED
Colour: RGB, CMYK, HSV, gamma; colour perception and dithering
Vector graphics: paths, SVG, Bezier curves; scalable versus raster
The graphics pipeline overview: modelling, transformation, rasterisation, shading, display
Drawing pixels on an HTML canvas; image formats and compression (PNG, JPEG)

syllabus.title: Line, circle and polygon drawing algorithms
topics: DDA and Bresenham line algorithms; symmetry and integer arithmetic
Midpoint circle and ellipse algorithms
Scan-line polygon fill, edge tables, boundary and flood fill
Anti-aliasing: supersampling, Wu's algorithm, coverage
Thick lines, line styles and character rasterisation

syllabus.title: 2D transformations
topics: Translation, rotation, scaling, shear, reflection as matrices; homogeneous coordinates
Composition and order; rotation about an arbitrary point
Window-to-viewport mapping; coordinate systems
Hierarchical modelling: a 2D articulated figure

syllabus.title: 3D transformations and modelling
topics: 3D homogeneous transforms; rotation about arbitrary axes; Euler angles, gimbal lock, quaternions
Scene graphs and model-view hierarchies
Representing surfaces: polygon meshes, normals, indexed triangles; parametric surfaces and subdivision in brief
Loading and displaying an OBJ model

syllabus.title: Viewing and projection
topics: Camera model: eye, look-at, up; the view matrix
Orthographic and perspective projection matrices; field of view, near and far planes
Normalised device coordinates and the viewport transform
Depth precision and the perspective divide

syllabus.title: Clipping and hidden surfaces
topics: Cohen-Sutherland and Liang-Barsky line clipping; Sutherland-Hodgman polygon clipping; clipping in homogeneous space
Back-face culling
Z-buffer algorithm; painter's algorithm; BSP trees; scan-line visibility
Ray casting as an alternative; bounding volumes and spatial subdivision

syllabus.title: Shading and lighting
topics: Light sources: ambient, directional, point, spot; attenuation
Lambertian diffuse, Phong and Blinn-Phong specular; material properties
Flat, Gouraud and Phong shading; vertex normals
Texture mapping, mipmaps, bump and normal mapping; environment maps
Shadows (shadow maps), global illumination and ray tracing in brief; physically based rendering overview

syllabus.title: Introduction to WebGL
topics: WebGL context, buffers, attributes, uniforms; GLSL vertex and fragment shaders
Drawing triangles, applying matrices with a maths library, animation with requestAnimationFrame
Lighting and texturing in shaders; loading textures and models
Mouse and keyboard interaction: orbit camera, picking
Performance on low-end phones; three.js as a higher-level alternative
Project: an interactive 3D scene such as a model of a Ghanaian landmark or a data visualisation

courses.title: Computer Organization and Architecture
topics: Computer evolution and performance
Top-level view of function and interconnection
Cache memory
Instruction sets
Processor structure and function
RISC
Instruction-level parallelism and superscalar processors
Control unit operation
Microprogrammed control
Parallel processing
Multicore computers
Pipelining, memory hierarchy, virtual memory, I/O
courses.description: How a processor, its memory hierarchy and its I/O system are organised and why they perform as they do: instruction sets, datapaths, pipelining, caches, virtual memory, superscalar and multicore design, with a simulated processor built and measured along the way. Taught to the depth of a leading computer architecture course.
modelledOn: Stallings, Computer Organization and Architecture
Patterson and Hennessy, Computer Organization and Design
Hennessy and Patterson, Computer Architecture: A Quantitative Approach (selected chapters)
outcomes: Measure and reason about performance with execution time, CPI, Amdahl's law and benchmarks.
Describe an instruction set architecture and trace instructions through a single-cycle and a multi-cycle datapath.
Design a pipelined processor and handle structural, data and control hazards with forwarding, stalls and branch prediction.
Analyse cache and virtual memory behaviour and compute hit rates, miss penalties and address translations.
Explain hardwired and microprogrammed control and superscalar, out-of-order and multicore execution.
Describe I/O organisation, interrupts, DMA and the interconnection structure of a modern system.

syllabus.title: Computer evolution and performance
topics: Generations of computers; Moore's law, Dennard scaling and the end of frequency scaling
Performance metrics: execution time, throughput, clock rate, CPI, MIPS and their traps
Amdahl's law; benchmarks (SPEC) and performance comparison
Power, energy and cooling as design constraints; mobile versus server design points

syllabus.title: Top-level view of function and interconnection
topics: Von Neumann architecture; the instruction cycle with interrupts
Buses: address, data, control; arbitration, timing, hierarchies
Point-to-point interconnects: QPI, PCIe, on-chip networks
Program execution traced at the register-transfer level

syllabus.title: Instruction sets
topics: Machine instruction characteristics, operand types, data types, operations
Addressing modes and instruction formats; fixed versus variable length
RISC-V (or MIPS) as the running example: registers, loads and stores, arithmetic, branches, procedure calls, the stack
x86 and ARM compared; CISC versus RISC and the RISC argument
Translating C to assembly to machine code; the compiler, assembler, linker and loader
Floating point: IEEE 754 arithmetic in hardware

syllabus.title: Processor structure and function: the datapath
topics: Register organisation, user-visible and control registers, flags
Building a single-cycle datapath: instruction fetch, register file, ALU, data memory, control signals
Multi-cycle datapath and finite-state control
Control unit operation: micro-operations, hardwired control design
Microprogrammed control: control memory, microinstruction formats, sequencing, horizontal versus vertical
Implementing the datapath in a simulator and tracing a program

syllabus.title: Pipelining
topics: The five-stage pipeline; speedup and its limits; pipeline registers
Structural hazards; data hazards and forwarding; load-use stalls
Control hazards: stalling, delayed branches, static and dynamic branch prediction (BHT, BTB, two-bit predictors)
Exceptions and interrupts in a pipeline; precise exceptions
Deeper pipelines and their costs

syllabus.title: Instruction-level parallelism, superscalar and RISC
topics: RISC characteristics revisited: register windows, compiler scheduling, large register files
Superscalar execution: multiple issue, instruction window, dependencies (true, anti, output)
Out-of-order execution: register renaming, Tomasulo's algorithm, reorder buffer, speculation
VLIW and the limits of ILP; Spectre-style side channels as a consequence of speculation

syllabus.title: Cache memory and the memory hierarchy
topics: Locality and the memory hierarchy; SRAM versus DRAM; memory organisation and interleaving
Cache mapping: direct, set-associative, fully associative; block size, replacement policies, write policies
Multi-level caches; average memory access time; the three Cs of misses; cache-aware programming (matrix multiply)
Virtual memory: pages, page tables, TLBs, page faults; address translation worked examples; protection
Cache coherence in multiprocessors: snooping and MESI

syllabus.title: Input/output
topics: I/O modules, programmed I/O, interrupt-driven I/O, direct memory access
I/O channels and processors; buses and interfaces: USB, PCIe, SATA, NVMe
Storage: magnetic disks, SSDs, RAID levels; reliability and availability
Interrupt handling and the operating system's view of devices

syllabus.title: Parallel processing and multicore computers
topics: Flynn's taxonomy; SIMD and vector units; GPUs as throughput processors
Symmetric multiprocessors, NUMA, clusters; cache coherence and memory consistency
Multithreading: fine-grained, coarse-grained, simultaneous (hyper-threading)
Multicore organisation: shared caches, interconnects, heterogeneous cores (big.LITTLE in phones)
Parallel speed-up, Amdahl again, and writing a parallel program that scales

courses.title: Concurrent and Parallel Programming
topics: Threads and shared memory
Races, locks and deadlock
Message passing and actors
Memory models and atomics
Lock-free and wait-free structures
Data parallelism and task parallelism
Speed-up, Amdahl's law and scalability
courses.description: How to write programs that do many things at once without corrupting data, deadlocking or running slower than the sequential version. Students run threaded programs, step through interleavings and measure speed-up in the browser lab.
modelledOn: Herlihy and Shavit, The Art of Multiprocessor Programming
Goetz et al., Java Concurrency in Practice
Grama, Gupta, Karypis and Kumar, Introduction to Parallel Computing
Mattson, Sanders and Massingill, Patterns for Parallel Programming
outcomes: Identify data races, race conditions and deadlocks in a program and repair them with the right synchronisation primitive.
Design thread-safe programs using locks, semaphores, monitors, channels and actors, and justify the choice.
Explain a memory model and use atomic operations and memory orderings correctly.
Implement and reason about the linearizability of simple lock-free structures such as a stack and a queue.
Decompose a problem into data-parallel and task-parallel pieces and predict its speed-up using Amdahl's law and the work-span model.
Test and measure concurrent programs with stress tests, schedule exploration and profiling.

syllabus.title: Threads and shared memory
topics: Processes, threads and the thread life cycle; creating threads, joining and thread pools
Shared memory, stacks and heaps per thread, and the cost of context switches
Concurrency versus parallelism; interleavings and nondeterministic execution
Thread-safe design by confinement, immutability and thread-local state
Futures, promises and async/await compared with explicit threads

syllabus.title: Races, locks and deadlock
topics: Data races versus race conditions; critical sections; mutual exclusion and Peterson's algorithm
Mutexes, spin locks, reentrant locks and read-write locks
Semaphores, monitors and condition variables; spurious wake-ups
Classic problems: producer-consumer, readers-writers and dining philosophers
Deadlock: the four Coffman conditions, lock ordering, detection and recovery; livelock and starvation

syllabus.title: Message passing and actors
topics: Channels and communicating sequential processes: bounded buffers, select and goroutine-style programs
The actor model: mailboxes, no shared state, supervision trees and let-it-crash
MPI-style message passing: send, receive, broadcast, scatter, gather and reduce
Shared memory versus message passing: ordering, latency and programming trade-offs
Deadlock, unbounded queues and backpressure in message-passing systems

syllabus.title: Memory models and atomics
topics: Sequential consistency, store buffers and why hardware and compilers reorder memory operations
The happens-before relation; the Java memory model and C++ memory orders (relaxed, acquire, release, seq_cst)
Atomic operations: compare-and-swap, fetch-and-add, load-linked/store-conditional and test-and-set
Volatile, fences and the broken double-checked locking idiom
Cache coherence with MESI, false sharing and padding

syllabus.title: Lock-free and wait-free structures
topics: Progress guarantees: blocking, obstruction-free, lock-free and wait-free
The Treiber stack and the Michael-Scott queue
The ABA problem; tagged pointers, hazard pointers and epoch-based reclamation
Linearizability as a correctness condition and finding linearization points
Concurrent hash maps and skip lists: striped locks versus lock-free designs

syllabus.title: Data parallelism and task parallelism
topics: Decomposition patterns: data, task and pipeline parallelism; work-stealing schedulers
Parallel map, reduce and prefix scan (Blelloch scan)
Fork-join divide and conquer: parallel merge sort and quicksort, sequential cut-offs
Parallel loops and OpenMP-style directives; the SIMT model of GPUs
Parallel graph traversal and MapReduce-style batch processing

syllabus.title: Speed-up and scalability
topics: Speed-up, efficiency and Amdahl's law
Gustafson's law, strong and weak scaling, and isoefficiency
The work-span model, parallelism and Brent's bound
Granularity, load imbalance, contention and synchronisation overhead
Profiling parallel programs: lock contention, idle threads and memory bandwidth limits

syllabus.title: Verification and project
topics: Testing concurrent code: stress tests, randomised schedules and race detectors such as ThreadSanitizer
Model checking small concurrent algorithms by exhaustive interleaving exploration
Project: parallelise a batch of mobile-money transaction records or crop-image tiles and report speed-up
Course review: choosing between locks, atomics, messages and data-parallel libraries

courses.title: Containers and Kubernetes
topics: Containers and images
Writing Dockerfiles
Container networking and storage
Kubernetes architecture
Pods, deployments and services
Configuration, secrets and scaling
Troubleshooting clusters
courses.description: Packaging and running software with containers and orchestrating it with Kubernetes: how containers isolate processes, building images with Dockerfiles, container networking and storage, the Kubernetes control plane, pods, deployments and services, configuration, secrets and autoscaling, and systematic troubleshooting of broken clusters. Practised hands-on in simulated terminals and a simulated multi-node cluster in the browser, taught to the depth of the Kubernetes administrator and developer certifications.
modelledOn: Burns, Beda, Hightower and Evenson, Kubernetes: Up and Running
Lukša, Kubernetes in Action
CNCF Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA) and Certified Kubernetes Application Developer (CKAD) curricula
Open Container Initiative image and runtime specifications
outcomes: Explain how containers use namespaces, control groups and layered file systems and contrast them with virtual machines.
Write efficient, secure Dockerfiles and multi-container applications and publish images to a registry.
Configure container networking and persistent storage for stateful and stateless workloads.
Describe the Kubernetes architecture and deploy applications with pods, deployments, services and ingress.
Manage configuration, secrets, resource limits and autoscaling and perform rolling updates and rollbacks.
Diagnose and repair failing workloads, nodes and cluster networking using a systematic troubleshooting method.

syllabus.title: Containers and images
topics: Why containers: dependency hell, environment drift, density; containers versus virtual machines
Linux foundations: namespaces, cgroups, capabilities, seccomp, union and overlay file systems
The OCI image format: layers, manifests, digests and tags; registries and pulling by digest
Container runtimes: Docker Engine, containerd, runc and Podman; rootless containers
The container life cycle: run, exec, logs, inspect, stop, remove; restart policies

syllabus.title: Writing Dockerfiles
topics: Dockerfile instructions: FROM, RUN, COPY, ENV, ARG, WORKDIR, USER, EXPOSE, ENTRYPOINT versus CMD
Layer caching and build order; .dockerignore; multi-stage builds for small images
Choosing base images: distroless, Alpine and slim images; image size on slow and metered connections
Image security: running as non-root, pinning versions, scanning for vulnerabilities, signing images
Containerising a Node.js API and a Python service; Docker Compose for multi-container development

syllabus.title: Container networking and storage
topics: Bridge, host and overlay networks; port publishing; DNS-based service discovery between containers
Network namespaces and virtual Ethernet pairs; inspecting traffic between containers
Volumes, bind mounts and tmpfs; data that must survive a container
Running a database in a container: persistence, backups and why it is often a bad idea in production

syllabus.title: Kubernetes architecture
topics: Why orchestration: scheduling, self-healing, scaling, rolling updates; the declarative model and reconciliation loops
Control plane: API server, etcd, scheduler, controller manager, cloud controller manager
Worker nodes: kubelet, kube-proxy, the container runtime interface
Setting up a cluster with kubeadm; managed clusters on EKS, AKS and GKE; lightweight k3s for low-cost hardware
kubectl, kubeconfig, contexts and namespaces; reading and writing YAML manifests

syllabus.title: Pods, deployments and services
topics: Pods: multi-container patterns (sidecar, init containers, ambassador), pod life cycle, probes for liveness, readiness and startup
ReplicaSets and Deployments; rolling updates, rollout history and rollbacks
StatefulSets, DaemonSets, Jobs and CronJobs
Services: ClusterIP, NodePort, LoadBalancer, headless services; endpoints and EndpointSlices
Ingress and the Gateway API; TLS termination; exposing a mobile money payment API through an ingress controller

syllabus.title: Configuration, secrets and scaling
topics: ConfigMaps and Secrets as environment variables and mounted files; encryption of secrets at rest; external secret stores
Resource requests and limits; quality of service classes; LimitRanges and ResourceQuotas
Scheduling: node selectors, affinity and anti-affinity, taints and tolerations, topology spread
Autoscaling: Horizontal Pod Autoscaler, Vertical Pod Autoscaler, cluster autoscaler; metrics server
Persistent storage: PersistentVolumes, PersistentVolumeClaims, StorageClasses and dynamic provisioning
Packaging applications with Helm charts and Kustomize overlays

syllabus.title: Cluster security and networking
topics: Authentication and RBAC: service accounts, roles, role bindings, least privilege
Pod Security Standards and admission control; security contexts
The pod network model; CNI plugins such as Calico and Cilium; NetworkPolicies for isolation
Cluster DNS with CoreDNS; service meshes in brief

syllabus.title: Troubleshooting clusters
topics: A troubleshooting method: observe, hypothesise, test, fix, verify; reading events and describe output
Failing workloads: CrashLoopBackOff, ImagePullBackOff, OOMKilled, pending pods and unschedulable nodes
Failing networking: services without endpoints, DNS failures, NetworkPolicy mistakes, ingress misrouting
Failing nodes and control plane: NotReady nodes, kubelet logs, certificate expiry, etcd backup and restore
Logging and monitoring a cluster with Prometheus, Grafana and centralised logs
Capstone: deploy, scale, secure and repair a multi-service application on a broken cluster under timed conditions

courses.title: Control Systems
topics: Modelling dynamic systems
Transfer functions and block diagrams
Time response and stability
Root locus
Frequency response: Bode and Nyquist
PID controller design and tuning
State-space models and digital control
courses.description: Analysis and design of feedback control systems: modelling physical systems, transfer functions and block diagrams, transient and steady-state response, stability, root locus, Bode and Nyquist methods, PID tuning, state-space design and digital control. Every plant and controller is simulated in the browser, so students tune a controller and immediately see its step response, root locus and frequency response move.
modelledOn: Nise, Control Systems Engineering
Ogata, Modern Control Engineering
Franklin, Powell and Emami-Naeini, Feedback Control of Dynamic Systems
Dorf and Bishop, Modern Control Systems
outcomes: Model electrical, mechanical and electromechanical systems as differential equations, transfer functions and state-space equations.
Reduce block diagrams and signal-flow graphs and determine transient response, steady-state error and stability.
Design compensators with the root locus and with Bode and Nyquist frequency-response methods to meet time- and frequency-domain specifications.
Design and tune PID controllers and explain integral windup, derivative filtering and practical tuning rules.
Design state-feedback controllers and observers, and implement controllers digitally with appropriate sampling.

syllabus.title: Introduction to feedback control
topics: Open-loop and closed-loop control; the benefits and costs of feedback
The control design process: specifications, model, design, simulation, implementation
Laplace transform review for control
Examples: water-tank level, room temperature, and a hydroelectric generator speed governor holding grid frequency at 50 Hz

syllabus.title: Modelling dynamic systems
topics: Electrical networks and operational amplifier circuits
Mechanical translational and rotational systems; gears and inertia reflection
Electromechanical systems: the armature-controlled DC motor
Thermal and fluid systems; electrical analogies
Linearisation of non-linear systems about an operating point
Identifying model parameters from measured step responses

syllabus.title: Transfer functions and block diagrams
topics: Transfer functions, poles and zeros; from differential equations to transfer functions
Block diagram algebra and reduction
Signal-flow graphs and Mason's gain formula
Effects of feedback: sensitivity to parameter variation, disturbance rejection, noise

syllabus.title: Time response, stability and steady-state error
topics: First-order response and the time constant
Second-order response: damping ratio, natural frequency, rise time, peak time, percentage overshoot, settling time
Higher-order systems and dominant poles; effect of zeros
Routh-Hurwitz stability criterion, including special cases
Steady-state error, system type and static error constants
Specifying performance for a solar-powered irrigation pump

syllabus.title: Root locus
topics: The root locus: angle and magnitude conditions
Sketching rules: asymptotes, breakaway and break-in points, imaginary-axis crossings, angles of departure
Gain selection to meet transient specifications
Lead, lag and lead-lag compensator design on the root locus
Root contours and parameter sensitivity

syllabus.title: Frequency response: Bode and Nyquist
topics: Frequency response and asymptotic Bode magnitude and phase plots
The Nyquist plot and the Nyquist stability criterion
Gain and phase margins; relation to transient response
Closed-loop frequency response and bandwidth; Nichols chart in brief
Lead, lag and lead-lag design in the frequency domain
Effect of time delay on stability, as in remote or networked control

syllabus.title: PID controller design and tuning
topics: Proportional, integral and derivative actions and their effect on response
Practical PID: integral windup and anti-windup, derivative filtering, set-point weighting, bumpless transfer
Tuning methods: Ziegler-Nichols, Cohen-Coon and IMC-based tuning
Cascade and feedforward control
Tuning a DC motor speed loop and a battery charge controller on the simulator

syllabus.title: State-space models
topics: State variables; converting between transfer functions and state-space forms
Solution of the state equation and the state-transition matrix
Controllability and observability
State feedback and pole placement; Ackermann's formula
Full-order observer design and the separation principle
The linear quadratic regulator in brief

syllabus.title: Digital control
topics: Sampled-data systems and the zero-order hold; z-domain transfer functions
Discretising controllers: forward, backward and Tustin approximations
Stability in the z-plane and the Jury test
Implementing a digital PID on a microcontroller: sampling-rate choice, quantisation and computational delay
Grid frequency control and load shedding as a large-scale control problem

courses.title: Digital Banking, Lending and Insurance Technology
topics: Core banking systems and open banking APIs

Credit scoring and algorithmic lending

Siddiqi, Intelligent Credit Scoring
Bank for International Settlements and FATF published guidance on digital identity, open finance and AML
Anderson, Security Engineering (fraud and payment systems chapters)

Build and evaluate a credit scorecard and a loan product, and assess it for bias and portfolio risk.

syllabus.title: Core banking and open banking APIs
topics: Core banking architecture: accounts, double-entry ledgers, transaction posting and end-of-day batch
Real-time and event-driven cores versus legacy mainframe cores; ISO 20022 message structure
Open banking: consent, OAuth 2.0 authorisation, financial-grade API profiles and sandboxes
Banking as a service, API marketplaces and partner banks
Resilience: idempotent payments, reconciliation, settlement and outage handling

syllabus.title: Digital onboarding and identity verification
topics: Know-your-customer tiers and customer due diligence, including tiered KYC for mobile money wallets
National ID and biometric verification: Ghana Card matching, face match and liveness detection
Document verification, OCR and onboarding fraud: synthetic and stolen identities
Digital identity models: centralised, federated and self-sovereign; consent and data protection
Onboarding funnel design: conversion, drop-off analysis and assurance levels

syllabus.title: Credit scoring and algorithmic lending
topics: Credit risk basics: probability of default, loss given default, exposure and expected loss
Scorecard development: weight of evidence, logistic regression, Gini and KS statistics
Alternative data: mobile money histories, airtime and utility payments, consent and privacy
Machine learning scorers, explainability, bias and fairness testing

syllabus.title: Crowdfunding and peer-to-peer lending

Investor protection, disclosure, default handling and platform failure
Diversification and returns of loan pools under correlated defaults
Savings groups (susu) and digitised rotating credit
Agricultural and small business funding cases in West Africa

syllabus.title: Insurance technology and underwriting
topics: Insurance fundamentals: pooling, premium, claims, reinsurance and loss ratio
Underwriting and pricing: risk classification, frequency and severity models
Claims automation: workflow, image-based assessment and straight-through processing
Parametric and index insurance for farmers: triggers, payouts and basis risk
Microinsurance and mobile distribution
Telematics and usage-based insurance for transport operators

syllabus.title: Fraud detection and anti-money-laundering
topics: Fraud typologies: SIM swap, account takeover, social engineering and mule accounts
Rules and anomaly detection: features, thresholds and the precision-recall trade-off
Graph analytics for mule networks and collusion rings
AML transaction monitoring: structuring, sanctions screening and suspicious transaction reports
Case management and investigation workflow
Regulatory frameworks: FATF recommendations, Bank of Ghana directives and financial intelligence reporting

syllabus.title: Financial inclusion and mobile banking
topics: Mobile money architecture: wallets, agents, float and USSD versus app channels
Interoperability: instant payment switches and wallet-to-bank transfers
Inclusion metrics: access, usage, quality and the Global Findex survey
Designing for low literacy, low connectivity and trust; agent liquidity management
Consumer protection: transparency, complaints handling and over-indebtedness

syllabus.title: Capstone: a digital bank for a rural community
topics: Product design: accounts, savings and loan products for smallholder farmers
Compliance and risk review: KYC, AML, data protection and credit policy
Cloud deployment and resilience of the banking stack
Presentation of the business case and risk register

courses.title: Digital Signal Processing
topics: Discrete-time signals and the DFT
The fast Fourier transform
FIR filter design
IIR filter design
Multirate processing
Spectral analysis
Audio and image processing applications

Proakis and Manolakis, Digital Signal Processing: Principles, Algorithms and Applications
Lyons, Understanding Digital Signal Processing
Mitra, Digital Signal Processing: A Computer-Based Approach
