syllabus.title: Network design and capacity planning
topics: Hierarchical and spine-leaf design models: access, distribution and core
Traffic matrices and demand estimation; busy-hour and peak-to-mean ratios
Queueing models for links: M/M/1 and M/D/1 delay; Erlang B and C for dimensioning
Oversubscription, redundancy and k-connected resilient topologies
Capacity planning for a national backbone: exchange points, submarine cable landings and terrestrial fibre
Cost-performance optimisation of topology and link upgrades

syllabus.title: Advanced routing and traffic engineering
topics: Link-state internals: OSPF areas and LSA types, IS-IS, fast convergence and BFD
BGP in depth: path attributes, policy, route reflectors, communities, convergence and route leaks
Internet exchange points, peering versus transit economics, and RPKI route origin validation
MPLS: label switching, LDP and layer-3 VPNs
Traffic engineering: constraint-based routing, ECMP and segment routing
IP multicast: IGMP and PIM

syllabus.title: Data centre and overlay networks
topics: Data centre topologies: fat-tree, Clos and leaf-spine; east-west traffic
VXLAN and EVPN overlays; underlay versus overlay
Load balancing: ECMP hashing, consistent hashing, layer-4 and layer-7 balancers and anycast
Data centre transport: TCP incast, DCTCP and RDMA over converged Ethernet
Congestion control: Reno, CUBIC and BBR; fairness, bufferbloat and QUIC
Content delivery and edge caching for African networks

syllabus.title: Quality of service
topics: QoS models: best effort, IntServ with RSVP, and DiffServ
Classification and marking with DSCP and CoS; trust boundaries
Queue scheduling: FIFO, priority, WFQ, CBWFQ and LLQ; delay bounds
Policing and shaping with token and leaky buckets
Congestion avoidance with RED, WRED and ECN; voice and video requirements

syllabus.title: Network virtualisation and software-defined networking
topics: SDN architecture: control and data plane separation, OpenFlow match-action
SDN controllers, northbound APIs and flow table design
P4 and programmable data planes
Network function virtualisation: VNFs, service chaining and virtual switches
Network slicing and multi-tenancy with VRF and VXLAN isolation
Container networking: CNI plugins, overlays and service meshes

syllabus.title: Monitoring and telemetry
topics: SNMP, syslog, NetFlow/IPFIX and sFlow
Streaming telemetry with gNMI and YANG models
Active measurement: latency, jitter and loss; Paris traceroute and one-way delay
Anomaly and DDoS detection from flow data
Dashboards, SLOs and root-cause analysis

syllabus.title: Network automation
topics: Infrastructure as code for networks: templates, Jinja2 and Ansible
NETCONF, RESTCONF and YANG data models
Intent-based networking and closed-loop automation
Testing and CI/CD for networks: configuration validation, digital twins and reachability verification
Change management, rollback and network reliability engineering

syllabus.title: Research methods and capstone
topics: Reading networking research: measurement papers and design critiques
Reproducing a result in simulation; experimental methodology and statistics
Capstone: design, simulate and defend a network for a regional ISP or hospital group
Open problems: networks in low-bandwidth settings and the security of routing

courses.title: Advanced Database Systems
topics: Query optimisation and cost models
Storage engines and indexing structures
Transaction processing and concurrency control
Recovery and logging
Distributed and replicated databases
Column stores and in-memory processing
NoSQL and NewSQL trade-offs
courses.description: The internals of database engines at graduate depth: storage layout, indexes, query execution and optimisation, concurrency control, recovery, distribution, column stores and the NoSQL and NewSQL landscape. Students read query plans, simulate transactions and index structures, build small engine components and finish with a benchmarked research-style project.
modelledOn: Garcia-Molina, Ullman and Widom, Database Systems: The Complete Book
Hellerstein, Stonebraker and Hamilton, Architecture of a Database System
Kleppmann, Designing Data-Intensive Applications
outcomes: Estimate the I/O cost of scans, index lookups and join algorithms and predict which one an optimiser will pick.
Implement and analyse B+ tree and LSM-tree operations, including node splits, compaction and write amplification.
Decide serialisability of schedules and explain how two-phase locking, timestamps and snapshot isolation prevent or permit anomalies.
Trace write-ahead logging and ARIES recovery through a crash and show the state of the database after each phase.
Compare partitioning, replication and distributed commit designs and state what each guarantees under failure.
Design, run and critically report a benchmark that compares two storage or execution designs.

syllabus.title: DBMS architecture and storage management
topics: Layers of a DBMS: parser, optimiser, executor, access methods, buffer manager, storage and log manager
Pages, slotted-page layout, record formats and free-space management
Buffer pool replacement: LRU, clock, LRU-K and scan-resistant policies; sequential flooding
Row, column and hybrid (PAX) layouts; the disk and SSD I/O cost model

syllabus.title: Indexing structures
topics: B+ trees: search, insertion with splits, deletion with merges, bulk loading and latch crabbing
Hash indexes: static, extendible and linear hashing
Log-structured merge trees: memtable, sorted runs, compaction strategies and write amplification
Bitmap indexes, Bloom filters and R-trees for spatial data
Index selection: clustered, covering, partial and composite indexes and the cost of maintenance

syllabus.title: Query execution
topics: Iterator (Volcano), vectorised and compiled execution models
External merge sort and its I/O cost
Join algorithms: block nested loop, index nested loop, sort-merge and grace hash join, with cost formulae
Aggregation, duplicate elimination and set operators
Pipelining versus materialisation, and intra-query parallelism

syllabus.title: Query optimisation
topics: Relational algebra equivalences, predicate and projection pushdown, and rule-based rewriting
Statistics: histograms, distinct counts, selectivity and cardinality estimation errors
Plan enumeration: System R dynamic programming, left-deep trees and interesting orders
Transformation-based optimisers: Cascades, memo structures and top-down search
Reading EXPLAIN output, hints, plan regressions and adaptive query processing

syllabus.title: Transactions and concurrency control
topics: ACID, schedules, conflict serialisability and precedence graphs
Two-phase locking, strict 2PL, deadlock detection and prevention, and multigranularity locking
Timestamp ordering and optimistic concurrency control
Multiversion concurrency control, snapshot isolation, write skew and serialisable snapshot isolation
SQL isolation levels and anomalies: dirty read, lost update, non-repeatable read and phantom

syllabus.title: Recovery and logging
topics: Steal and no-force buffer policies; the write-ahead logging rule
ARIES: analysis, redo and undo passes, compensation log records and fuzzy checkpoints
Shadow paging, copy-on-write and log-structured storage compared with update-in-place
Group commit, fsync cost and durability on SSDs and cloud disks
Backup, archive logs and point-in-time recovery

syllabus.title: Distributed and replicated databases
topics: Partitioning: hash, range and consistent hashing; rebalancing and hot spots
Replication: leader-follower, multi-leader, quorum, and replication lag anomalies
Atomic commit: two-phase commit, its blocking problem and three-phase commit
Consensus for replicated logs: Paxos and Raft, leader election and log replication
Distributed transactions and globally consistent databases using synchronised clocks
Distributed query processing: shuffle, broadcast and co-located joins

syllabus.title: Column stores, in-memory systems and NoSQL
topics: Column stores: compression (run-length, dictionary, bit-packing), late materialisation and zone maps
Vectorised execution with SIMD and in-memory databases: logging, snapshots and cache efficiency
NoSQL families (key-value, document, wide-column, graph) and BASE trade-offs
NewSQL and HTAP systems: distributed SQL with transactions, and mixed workloads
Choosing a data system: workload analysis and the TPC-C, TPC-H and YCSB benchmarks

syllabus.title: Research methods and project
topics: Reading and critiquing a systems paper: claim, mechanism, evaluation and threats
Benchmark design: workloads, warm-up, throughput, latency percentiles and confidence intervals
Open problems: learned indexes, learned cardinality estimation and serverless databases
Project: implement and evaluate a storage or query-engine component and report the results

courses.title: Advanced Deep Learning
topics: Optimisation of deep networks
Attention and transformer architectures
Generative models: VAE, GAN, diffusion
Self-supervised and contrastive learning
Scaling, efficiency and distributed training
Interpretability and robustness
Deep reinforcement learning
courses.description: A graduate course on the methods that power modern deep learning, from the optimisation of deep networks to transformers, generative models, self-supervised learning, large-scale training, interpretability and deep reinforcement learning. Students implement and ablate each method at small scale, read recent papers critically and finish by reproducing a published result under a compute budget.
modelledOn: Goodfellow, Bengio and Courville, Deep Learning
Prince, Understanding Deep Learning
Sutton and Barto, Reinforcement Learning: An Introduction
Recent proceedings of the major machine learning conferences (reading list)
outcomes: Analyse the optimisation behaviour of deep networks and choose optimisers, schedules, initialisation and normalisation with justification.
Derive and implement the attention mechanism and the transformer, and explain its computational cost and efficient variants.
Derive the training objectives of VAEs, GANs and diffusion models and evaluate generated samples.
Apply self-supervised, contrastive and parameter-efficient methods to settings with scarce labels, such as low-resource African languages.
Estimate memory, compute and communication costs of distributed training and apply compression for deployment on constrained devices.
Critique a recent paper, design ablations with multiple seeds and report a reproduction honestly.

syllabus.title: Optimisation of deep networks
topics: Loss landscapes: saddle points, sharp versus flat minima and mode connectivity
SGD, momentum and Nesterov acceleration; Adam and AdamW; learning-rate schedules and warm-up
Initialisation and normalisation: Xavier and He schemes, batch normalisation, layer normalisation, signal propagation
Residual connections and trainability; gradient clipping and exploding gradients
Generalisation: implicit regularisation, weight decay, dropout and double descent
Hyperparameter search, seeds and reproducible training runs

syllabus.title: Attention and transformer architectures
topics: Sequence models revisited: recurrent networks, vanishing gradients, LSTM and GRU
Scaled dot-product and multi-head attention; sinusoidal and rotary positional encodings
The transformer encoder and decoder; masking, residual stream and feed-forward blocks
Pretraining objectives (causal and masked language modelling) and subword tokenisation including African languages
Vision transformers and multimodal models
Cost of attention: quadratic scaling, KV caching and efficient attention such as FlashAttention and sparse variants

syllabus.title: Generative models: VAE, GAN and diffusion
topics: Latent variable models, the evidence lower bound and the VAE with the reparameterisation trick
Autoregressive and normalising-flow models as exact-likelihood generators
Generative adversarial networks: minimax objective, mode collapse and Wasserstein GAN
Diffusion models: forward noising, denoising score matching and DDPM sampling
Conditioning, classifier-free guidance and evaluating generators with FID, likelihood and human evaluation

syllabus.title: Self-supervised and contrastive learning
topics: Pretext tasks and masked autoencoders
Contrastive objectives: InfoNCE, SimCLR and MoCo, and the mutual information bound
Non-contrastive methods such as BYOL and collapse avoidance
Transfer and fine-tuning: adapters, LoRA and other parameter-efficient methods
Few-shot and low-resource learning for African languages and satellite imagery

syllabus.title: Scaling, efficiency and distributed training
topics: Scaling laws and compute-optimal training
Data, tensor and pipeline parallelism; ZeRO sharding; the communication cost of all-reduce
Mixed precision, gradient checkpointing and memory accounting for parameters, activations and optimiser state
Compression: quantisation, pruning and knowledge distillation for edge devices
Mixture-of-experts models and conditional computation
Cost, energy and carbon accounting of training and inference

syllabus.title: Interpretability and robustness
topics: Attribution methods: saliency, integrated gradients, SHAP and sanity checks for explanations
Probing and mechanistic interpretability: circuits, attention heads and sparse autoencoders
Adversarial examples: FGSM, PGD, adversarial training and certified defences
Distribution shift, calibration and out-of-distribution detection
Safety evaluation, red teaming and failure analysis of deployed models

syllabus.title: Deep reinforcement learning
topics: Markov decision processes recap; policy gradients, REINFORCE and baselines
Actor-critic methods: A2C and PPO with clipped objectives
Value-based deep RL: DQN, experience replay, target networks and double DQN
Continuous control with DDPG and SAC
Model-based and offline reinforcement learning; reinforcement learning from human feedback

syllabus.title: Research methods and project
topics: Reading and critiquing a recent paper: claims, evidence, baselines and ablations
Experiment tracking, seeds and statistical rigour in deep learning comparisons
Reproducing a published result under a fixed compute budget
Writing and presenting the reproduction report

courses.title: Advanced Digital Communications
topics: signal space and detection theory
modulation and demodulation performance
equalisation and synchronisation
channel coding and capacity limits
OFDM and multicarrier systems
MIMO and diversity
link-level simulation
courses.description: Graduate treatment of digital transmission over noisy, dispersive and fading channels: optimal detection, modulation performance, equalisation, synchronisation, coding, OFDM and MIMO. In the lab students derive error rates, then build and validate a link-level simulation that reproduces theory and a published result.
modelledOn: Proakis and Salehi, Digital Communications
Tse and Viswanath, Fundamentals of Wireless Communication
Goldsmith, Wireless Communications
Moon, Error Correction Coding: Mathematical Methods and Algorithms
outcomes: Derive optimal receivers and error-probability bounds for signals in additive Gaussian noise using signal-space methods.
Compare modulation formats by bit error rate, spectral efficiency and robustness to fading.
Design and simulate equalisers and carrier and timing recovery loops for dispersive channels.
Evaluate channel codes against capacity limits, including convolutional, turbo, LDPC and polar codes.
Analyse and simulate OFDM and MIMO links, including diversity, multiplexing and precoding trade-offs.
Build a validated Monte Carlo link simulator and report results with confidence intervals against theory.

syllabus.title: Signal space and detection theory
topics: Gram-Schmidt orthonormalisation and the vector representation of signals and constellations
The AWGN channel, sufficient statistics, correlator and matched-filter receivers
Hypothesis testing: MAP and ML detection, decision regions and Bayes risk
Union bound and nearest-neighbour approximation for error probability
Q-function, Eb/N0 versus Es/N0 and bit error rate definitions
Noncoherent detection with random phase; Rayleigh and Rician envelopes
Maximum-likelihood estimation and the Cramer-Rao bound for phase and timing

syllabus.title: Modulation and demodulation performance
topics: PAM, PSK and QAM: exact and approximate error rates, Gray mapping
Orthogonal signalling, FSK, MSK and continuous-phase modulation: spectrum and efficiency
Differential and noncoherent schemes: DPSK and noncoherent FSK
Pulse shaping: the Nyquist criterion, raised-cosine and root-raised-cosine filters, eye diagrams
Performance in fading: Rayleigh and Rician average BER, outage and link budgets for mobile networks

syllabus.title: Equalisation and synchronisation
topics: Intersymbol interference, the discrete-time equivalent channel and the whitened matched filter
Zero-forcing and MMSE linear equalisers and noise enhancement
Decision-feedback and maximum-likelihood sequence equalisation; adaptive LMS and RLS algorithms
Carrier phase recovery: phase-locked loops, the Costas loop and decision-directed methods
Symbol timing recovery: early-late gate and zero-crossing timing error detectors
Frame synchronisation, preambles and training sequences; frequency offset estimation

syllabus.title: Channel coding and capacity limits
topics: Shannon capacity of the AWGN channel, the -1.59 dB limit and binary-input capacity
Linear block codes: generator and parity-check matrices, syndrome decoding, BCH and Reed-Solomon codes
Convolutional codes: trellis, hard and soft Viterbi decoding, free distance
Turbo codes and iterative MAP decoding
LDPC codes: Tanner graphs, belief propagation and density evolution
Polar codes: channel polarisation and successive-cancellation decoding
Coded modulation, coding gain and hybrid ARQ

syllabus.title: OFDM and multicarrier systems
topics: Multicarrier principle, subcarrier orthogonality and FFT implementation
Cyclic prefix, guard interval and one-tap frequency-domain equalisation
Peak-to-average power ratio, clipping, selective mapping and amplifier nonlinearity
Preamble-based timing and frequency offset estimation; pilot-aided channel estimation
Bit loading, water-filling and adaptive modulation
OFDMA, SC-FDMA and the numerology of Wi-Fi, LTE and 5G NR

syllabus.title: MIMO and diversity
topics: Time, frequency and space diversity; selection, equal-gain and maximal-ratio combining; diversity order
Two-antenna orthogonal space-time block codes and space-time trellis codes
The MIMO channel model, capacity, singular value decomposition and water-filling
Spatial multiplexing receivers: ZF, MMSE, successive interference cancellation and sphere decoding
The diversity-multiplexing trade-off
Beamforming, precoding and massive MIMO with channel hardening

syllabus.title: Link-level simulation
topics: Monte Carlo BER estimation: sample size, confidence intervals and importance sampling
Building a simulation chain from source to BER counter in baseband-equivalent form
Channel models: AWGN, flat Rayleigh, tapped delay line and Doppler spectra
Validation against theory, seeds, vectorisation and reproducibility
Link adaptation, BLER-versus-SNR curves and throughput

syllabus.title: Reproduction, design and research critique
topics: Reproducing a published BER result and quantifying the mismatch
Link design for rural broadband and TV white space in Africa
Capstone: designing and tuning a coded OFDM link to a throughput target
Open problems: short-packet communication, massive access and non-terrestrial links

courses.title: Advanced Distributed Systems
topics: time, clocks and ordering
consensus and Paxos or Raft
replication and consistency models
distributed transactions and commit
key-value stores and CRDTs
failure detection and membership
fault tolerance case studies
courses.description: Graduate-level study of the algorithms and impossibility results behind replicated, fault-tolerant systems: time, consensus, consistency, distributed transactions, CRDTs, failure detection and resilience engineering. Students step through protocols, inject failures into simulated networks and clusters, and finish with a replicated store project.
modelledOn: Kleppmann, Designing Data-Intensive Applications
Lynch, Distributed Algorithms
Attiya and Welch, Distributed Computing: Fundamentals, Simulations and Advanced Topics
Research papers on Paxos, Raft, Dynamo, Spanner and CRDTs
outcomes: Prove or refute safety and liveness properties of a distributed protocol under a stated failure and timing model.
Derive and apply the FLP, CAP and quorum-intersection results to decide what a design can and cannot guarantee.
Implement and trace single-decree Paxos and Raft, including leader change and log repair.
Compare consistency models and transaction protocols and choose one for a given workload and failure profile.
Design convergent replicated data types and gossip-based membership with analysed convergence.
Evaluate a production-scale fault tolerance design by reading a systems paper and an incident report critically.

syllabus.title: System models, time and ordering
topics: System models: asynchronous, partially synchronous and synchronous; crash, omission and Byzantine faults
Physical clocks: drift, NTP, Cristian's algorithm and averaging-based clock synchronisation, bounded-uncertainty clocks
Logical time: Lamport clocks, vector clocks, version vectors and hybrid logical clocks
Consistent cuts and global snapshots: the Chandy-Lamport algorithm and stable property detection
Impossibility results: Two Generals, FLP, the CAP theorem and PACELC

syllabus.title: Consensus
topics: The consensus problem: agreement, validity and termination; equivalence with atomic broadcast
Single-decree Paxos with its safety proof, and Multi-Paxos
Raft: leader election, log replication, safety argument, membership change and log compaction
Byzantine fault tolerance: the 3f+1 bound, PBFT and view change; blockchain-style consensus compared
Randomised and leaderless consensus: Ben-Or, EPaxos and wide-area latency of consensus

syllabus.title: Replication and consistency models
topics: Primary-backup, state machine replication and chain replication
Consistency models: linearizability, sequential, causal and eventual consistency; session guarantees
Quorum systems: R+W>N, sloppy quorums, hinted handoff and read repair
Checking consistency: Jepsen-style testing, linearizability checkers and common anomalies
Multi-leader and geo-replication; conflict detection and the pitfalls of last-write-wins

syllabus.title: Distributed transactions and commit
topics: ACID in a distributed setting: serialisability, snapshot isolation and write skew
Two-phase commit, its blocking problem, three-phase commit and Paxos Commit
Distributed concurrency control: two-phase locking, timestamp ordering, MVCC and externally consistent transactions
Sagas, compensating transactions, the outbox pattern and idempotency for mobile money transfers
Deterministic transaction execution, coordination avoidance and the CALM theorem

syllabus.title: Key-value stores and CRDTs
topics: Partitioning: consistent hashing, virtual nodes and rendezvous hashing
Dynamo-style stores: gossip, vector clocks and Merkle-tree anti-entropy
LSM-tree storage engines, write-ahead logs and compaction in wide-column stores
State-based and operation-based CRDTs: G-counter, PN-counter, OR-set and sequence CRDTs
Convergence proofs with join-semilattices; offline-first applications

syllabus.title: Failure detection and membership
topics: Heartbeat and phi-accrual failure detectors; completeness, accuracy and the Chandra-Toueg classes
Gossip protocols: SWIM membership, epidemic dissemination and convergence-rate analysis
Leader election, leases and fencing tokens; split-brain
Group membership, view synchrony and reconfiguration
Coordination services: ZooKeeper and etcd, locks, barriers and configuration

syllabus.title: Fault tolerance in practice
topics: Planet-scale systems: a Spanner-style database, a Chubby-style lock service and a Borg-style cluster manager
Reading incident reports: storage and network partition outages, cascading and metastable failures
Resilience engineering: chaos experiments, circuit breakers, bulkheads, retries with backoff and jitter, load shedding
Performance at scale: tail latency, hedged requests, queueing and backpressure
Intermittent connectivity in Africa: delay-tolerant networking, edge computing and offline-first design

syllabus.title: Verification, research and project
topics: Verifying protocols: TLA+ specifications, model checking and deterministic simulation testing
Critical reading of a recent distributed systems paper: claims, assumptions and evaluation gaps
Project: a replicated key-value store tested under injected partitions and crashes
Open problems: scalable Byzantine consensus, verified implementations and wide-area coordination

courses.title: Advanced Game Engine Architecture
topics: Entity-component-system design
Data-oriented design and cache behaviour
Job systems and multithreading
Memory allocators and streaming
Asset pipelines and hot reloading
Scripting and tools integration
Cross-platform builds and profiling
courses.description: A graduate study of how production game engines are structured for speed and scale: entity-component-system design, cache-aware data layout, job systems, custom allocators, asset pipelines and profiling. Students build and benchmark the core of a small engine in the code runner and visualise cache and memory behaviour.
modelledOn: Gregory, Game Engine Architecture
Nystrom, Game Programming Patterns
Fabian, Data-Oriented Design
Williams, C++ Concurrency in Action
outcomes: Design an entity-component-system and justify its storage layout against an object-oriented alternative with measurements.
Predict and measure the effect of data layout on cache misses and frame time.
Implement a job system with dependencies and reason about data races, ordering and determinism.
Write custom allocators and a streaming policy that meet a stated memory budget.
Build an asset pipeline with incremental builds and hot reloading of data and scripts.
Profile an engine build on target hardware, set a frame budget and fix the largest bottleneck.

syllabus.title: Engine architecture and entity-component-system design
topics: Engine subsystems and the main loop: fixed versus variable timestep and the accumulator pattern
Entity-component-system: entities as ids, components as data, systems as functions
Component storage: archetypes versus sparse sets, queries and iteration
Command buffers, deferred structural changes and event queues between systems
Comparing deep inheritance, composition and ECS on a worked game feature

syllabus.title: Data-oriented design and cache behaviour
topics: The memory hierarchy: cache lines, associativity, misses and the cost of a cache miss
Array-of-structures versus structure-of-arrays and hot/cold data splitting
Alignment, padding, false sharing and prefetching
SIMD basics and batching work for vectorisation
Cache-friendly spatial structures: uniform grids, flat BVH and sorting by locality

syllabus.title: Job systems and multithreading
topics: Thread pools, tasks and dependency graphs of jobs
Work-stealing deques and load balancing
Atomics, memory ordering and lock-free queues
Data races, deadlock and designing for determinism
Frame pipelining: simulation, render and audio threads; parallel-for patterns

syllabus.title: Memory allocators and streaming
topics: Linear, stack and pool allocators and per-frame arenas
Free-list and buddy allocators; fragmentation and compaction
Handles, generation counters and safe references instead of raw pointers
Asset streaming: level-of-detail paging, prefetch and memory budgets
Memory profiling and budgets for low-end Android phones and browser targets

syllabus.title: Asset pipelines and hot reloading
topics: Importing, cooking and packing assets; platform-specific formats
Asset databases, stable identifiers, dependency graphs and incremental builds
Compression, texture formats and bundle layout for download size
Hot reloading of data, shaders and code
Serialisation, reflection and versioned save formats

syllabus.title: Scripting and tools integration
topics: Embedding a scripting language: binding native functions and ownership across the boundary
Script cost, coroutines and when to move logic out of scripts
Editor tooling: inspectors, property reflection and undo systems
Data-driven design: configuration files, tuning tables and live editing
Debug tooling: developer console, in-game profiler overlay and deterministic replay

syllabus.title: Cross-platform builds and profiling
topics: Build systems and toolchains; abstraction layers for platform differences
Platform abstraction of graphics, input, audio and file systems
Frame budgets, CPU and GPU profiling, flame graphs and sampling versus instrumentation
Performance regression tests and benchmarking in continuous integration
Optimising for mobile and WebAssembly targets: thermal limits, battery and download size

syllabus.title: Deterministic simulation and engine integration
topics: Deterministic simulation: fixed-point maths, seeded randomness and replay
Physics and collision pipeline integration: broad phase, narrow phase and solver ordering
Rendering architecture: scene graph versus render graph and visibility culling
Published engine post-mortems: lessons from architecture decisions that aged badly
Capstone: assemble and benchmark a mini engine core against a stated frame budget

courses.title: Advanced Machine Learning
topics: Statistical learning framework and generalisation
Kernel methods and support vector machines
Ensembles and boosting
Bayesian methods and Gaussian processes
Dimensionality reduction and representation learning
Online learning and bandits
Semi-supervised, active and transfer learning
courses.description: Graduate machine learning with the theory behind generalisation and the major families of methods beyond the introductory course: kernels, boosting, Bayesian models, representation learning, bandits, and learning with limited labels. Students derive key results, implement the methods from scratch in the lab, and reproduce and critique a published result.
modelledOn: Shalev-Shwartz and Ben-David, Understanding Machine Learning: From Theory to Algorithms
Murphy, Probabilistic Machine Learning: An Introduction and Advanced Topics
Hastie, Tibshirani and Friedman, The Elements of Statistical Learning
Rasmussen and Williams, Gaussian Processes for Machine Learning
outcomes: Derive generalisation bounds from the PAC, VC and Rademacher frameworks and explain what they do and do not guarantee.
Implement and analyse kernel machines, boosted ensembles and Gaussian process models from first principles.
Apply approximate Bayesian inference with the Laplace approximation, variational methods and Markov chain sampling.
Learn low-dimensional and self-supervised representations and judge their quality.
Design online, bandit, active and transfer learning solutions and bound their regret or label cost.
Reproduce a published result with statistical rigour and report calibration, uncertainty and failure modes.

syllabus.title: Statistical learning and generalisation
topics: Empirical risk minimisation, true risk and the generalisation gap
PAC learning and sample complexity for finite hypothesis classes
VC dimension and Rademacher complexity; uniform convergence
Bias-variance decomposition and double descent
Regularisation, structural risk minimisation and implicit bias of gradient descent
Cross-validation, model selection and honest evaluation with nested splits

syllabus.title: Kernel methods and support vector machines
topics: Maximum margin classification: primal and dual SVM
Kernels, Mercer's theorem and reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces
Soft margins, hinge loss and sequential minimal optimisation
Kernel ridge regression and kernel PCA
Scaling kernels: random Fourier features and the Nystrom approximation

syllabus.title: Ensembles and boosting
topics: Bagging, random forests and out-of-bag error
AdaBoost, exponential loss and margin theory
Gradient boosting as functional gradient descent
Regularised second-order boosting with histogram splits
Stacking, diversity and why ensembles generalise

syllabus.title: Bayesian methods and Gaussian processes
topics: Bayesian linear regression: conjugate priors and the posterior predictive
Gaussian processes: kernels as priors over functions, posterior and prediction
Marginal likelihood and hyperparameter learning
Approximate inference: Laplace approximation and variational inference
Markov chain Monte Carlo: Metropolis-Hastings and Hamiltonian Monte Carlo
Bayesian optimisation with acquisition functions

syllabus.title: Dimensionality reduction and representation learning
topics: PCA via the singular value decomposition and probabilistic PCA
Independent components and sparse coding with dictionaries
Manifold learning: spectral embeddings, t-SNE and the idea behind UMAP
Autoencoders and variational autoencoders with the evidence lower bound
Self-supervised and contrastive representation learning

syllabus.title: Online learning and bandits
topics: Regret and online gradient descent
Prediction with expert advice: weighted majority and Hedge
Multi-armed bandits: epsilon-greedy, UCB and Thompson sampling
Contextual bandits and linear upper confidence bounds
Application: adaptive advice for smallholder farmers or mobile-money fraud rules

syllabus.title: Semi-supervised, active and transfer learning
topics: Self-training, consistency regularisation and label propagation
Active learning: uncertainty sampling and query by committee
Transfer learning: fine-tuning and domain adaptation
Distribution shift: covariate shift, importance weighting and detection
Learning with few labels in low-resource languages and sensor data
Calibration and conformal prediction for reliable uncertainty

syllabus.title: Research practice in machine learning
topics: Reproducing a published result: seeds, hyperparameters and discrepancy diagnosis
Ablations and statistical comparison of learning algorithms across datasets
Fairness, robustness and responsible deployment checks
Project report: a method, an experiment and a critical discussion

courses.title: Advanced Network Security
topics: Protocol attacks and defences
Firewalls and intrusion detection
TLS and secure channels
DNS and routing security
Wireless and mobile network security
Denial of service and botnets
Network monitoring and traffic analysis
courses.description: A graduate course in defending networks: secure architecture, protocol hardening, secure channels, detection and response at every layer from the link to inter-domain routing. Students design, harden and monitor simulated enterprise, campus and provider networks, then evaluate how well their defences hold against scripted incidents.
modelledOn: Kaufman, Perlman and Speciner, Network Security: Private Communication in a Public World
Stallings, Network Security Essentials
NIST SP 800-207 Zero Trust Architecture and NIST SP 800-94 Guide to Intrusion Detection and Prevention Systems
IETF RFCs for TLS 1.3, DNSSEC, IPsec and RPKI

courses.description: A graduate study of how modern kernels manage memory, CPUs, storage and isolation at scale, and how performance is measured and tuned. Students trace kernel mechanisms in the step visualiser, run experiments in a Linux virtual machine, and complete a small measurement or implementation project.
modelledOn: Arpaci-Dusseau and Arpaci-Dusseau, Operating Systems: Three Easy Pieces
Love, Linux Kernel Development
Gregg, Systems Performance
Bovet and Cesati, Understanding the Linux Kernel
outcomes: Trace a system call, interrupt and page fault through a kernel and explain the cost of each step.
Evaluate page replacement, multicore scheduling and I/O scheduling policies using workload traces and measurements.
Explain crash consistency in journaling and copy-on-write file systems and test durability assumptions.
Compare full, paravirtual and hardware-assisted virtualisation with containers in isolation strength and overhead.
Use namespaces, cgroups and seccomp to build and limit an isolated process environment.

syllabus.title: Kernel structure and system calls

RAID, replication and erasure coding

courses.description: A graduate course in convex and large-scale optimisation: duality, first-order and second-order methods, proximal and interior-point algorithms, stochastic and distributed training, non-convex landscapes, and an applied strand of prescriptive analytics for real operational decisions. Students derive convergence rates, implement solvers from scratch, and then use them on scheduling, network design and uncertainty problems.

Nocedal and Wright, Numerical Optimization
Bertsimas and Tsitsiklis, Introduction to Linear Optimization

OFDM: cyclic prefix, subcarrier orthogonality and peak-to-average power ratio; SC-FDMA
Link adaptation: adaptive modulation and coding and hybrid ARQ
Channel estimation with pilots and frequency-domain equalisation

syllabus.title: MAC protocols and spectrum access
topics: ALOHA, slotted ALOHA and CSMA/CA throughput; hidden and exposed terminals
IEEE 802.11 DCF and the Bianchi saturation model; 802.11ax OFDMA
Scheduling: round robin, max C/I and proportional fair
Cognitive radio and dynamic spectrum access; TV white space
Spectrum policy: licensed, unlicensed and shared bands in Africa

syllabus.title: Cellular architecture, 5G and beyond
topics: Cell structure: frequency reuse, SINR, sectorisation and interference
LTE evolved packet core and the 5G core service-based architecture
5G NR physical layer: numerology, frame structure and bandwidth parts
5G use cases: eMBB, URLLC, mMTC and network slicing
Open RAN, small cells and heterogeneous networks
Rural coverage and fixed wireless access economics
Beyond 5G: reconfigurable surfaces, terahertz bands and integrated sensing and communication

syllabus.title: Massive MIMO and beamforming
topics: MIMO channel model, spatial multiplexing and SVD-based capacity
Precoding: zero-forcing, MMSE and multi-user MIMO
Massive MIMO: channel hardening, pilot contamination and TDD reciprocity
Beamforming: array factor, beam steering and millimetre-wave beam management
Hybrid analogue-digital beamforming

syllabus.title: Mobility management and handover
topics: Mobility models: random waypoint and Gauss-Markov
Handover: hysteresis, time-to-trigger, the A3 event and ping-pong effects
Location management: tracking areas and paging
Mobile IP and mobility anchoring in the 5G core
Handover failure analysis for high-speed vehicles and trains

syllabus.title: Wireless sensor and IoT networks
topics: Low-power wide-area networks: LoRa spreading factors, duty cycle limits, LoRaWAN and NB-IoT
Short-range links: Bluetooth Low Energy, IEEE 802.15.4, Zigbee and 6LoWPAN
Energy models, duty cycling and sensor MAC protocols: S-MAC and B-MAC
Routing in sensor networks: RPL, LEACH and directed diffusion
Energy harvesting and precision-agriculture deployment design
Localisation and time synchronisation: RSSI, time of arrival and trilateration

syllabus.title: Satellite and non-terrestrial links
topics: Orbits: GEO, MEO and LEO; Kepler's laws, visibility windows and Doppler
Satellite link budget: EIRP, G/T and rain fade
LEO constellations: handover between satellites, inter-satellite links and latency
Satellite access: DVB-S2, VSAT and MF-TDMA; TCP over satellite paths
High-altitude platforms, drones and non-terrestrial networks in 5G
Connecting remote communities: satellite versus terrestrial options

syllabus.title: Research methods and project
topics: Reading wireless research: channel measurement and testbed papers
Simulation methodology: Monte Carlo of fading channels and confidence intervals
Project: design and evaluate a rural coverage or IoT network
Open problems: spectrum scarcity, energy efficiency and wireless security

courses.title: Algorithmic and Systematic Trading
topics: Market microstructure and order books
Signal research and backtesting
Execution algorithms and transaction costs
Portfolio construction for strategies
Machine learning for trading signals
Latency and system design for trading
Risk limits and controls
courses.description: The full life cycle of a systematic trading strategy: market microstructure, signal research, honest backtesting, execution and costs, portfolio construction, machine learning signals, trading system design and risk controls. Students simulate order books, code and backtest strategies on historical and synthetic data, and finish by presenting a strategy with a risk review.
modelledOn: Chan, Algorithmic Trading: Winning Strategies and Their Rationale
Lopez de Prado, Advances in Financial Machine Learning
Harris, Trading and Exchanges: Market Microstructure for Practitioners
outcomes: Simulate a limit order book with price-time priority and explain spread, depth and market impact from it.
Build and evaluate a trading signal with information coefficient, decay and turnover, and avoid look-ahead and survivorship bias.
Backtest a strategy with realistic costs and report Sharpe ratio, drawdown and a deflated measure that accounts for multiple testing.
Choose and compare execution algorithms (TWAP, VWAP, participation) by implementation shortfall.
Size positions and combine signals into a cost-aware portfolio under risk constraints.
Design pre-trade risk checks and a monitoring and kill-switch plan for an automated trading system, in line with market rules.

syllabus.title: Markets and microstructure
topics: Order types, the limit order book and the matching engine with price-time priority
Spread, depth, liquidity and market impact; reading a depth ladder
Market structure: exchanges, market makers, dark pools, and thin-liquidity African markets such as the Ghana Stock Exchange
Modelling order flow: Poisson arrivals, queue position and fill probability
Adverse selection, informed trading and the sources of the spread

syllabus.title: Data and signal research
topics: Market data: ticks, bars, corporate-action adjustment and survivorship bias
Returns, stationarity and classic signals: momentum, mean reversion, carry and value
Evaluating a signal: information coefficient, decay, turnover and breadth
Pairs trading and statistical arbitrage: cointegration, spread z-scores and half-life
Trend following and volatility signals, and the role of regimes

syllabus.title: Backtesting
topics: Vectorised versus event-driven backtesters and their trade-offs
Biases: look-ahead, survivorship, data snooping and overfitting; multiple-testing correction and the deflated Sharpe ratio
Walk-forward analysis and purged cross-validation
Performance measures: Sharpe, Sortino, maximum drawdown, Calmar ratio and turnover
Including fees, slippage and capacity limits in a backtest

syllabus.title: Execution and transaction costs
topics: Components of cost: spread, market impact, fees and delay; implementation shortfall
Market impact models: the square-root law and Almgren-Chriss
Execution algorithms: TWAP, VWAP and percentage-of-volume
Optimal liquidation trajectories and the risk-impact trade-off
Smart order routing, venue choice and order slicing
Transaction cost analysis against arrival price and VWAP benchmarks

syllabus.title: Portfolio construction for strategies
topics: Mean-variance, risk parity and volatility targeting
The Kelly criterion and fractional Kelly position sizing
Combining signals and diversifying across strategies; correlation of returns
Factor exposures and risk models for a strategy book
Cost-aware optimisation with turnover and position constraints

syllabus.title: Machine learning for trading signals
topics: Feature engineering for financial time series and the triple-barrier labelling method
Regularised linear models, random forests and gradient boosting for return prediction
Leakage and time-series cross-validation with embargo
Low signal-to-noise, overfitting, feature importance and interpretability
Reinforcement learning for execution and market making: setup and pitfalls
Regime detection with hidden Markov models and change-point methods

syllabus.title: Trading system design and latency
topics: Architecture: market data handler, strategy engine, order management, risk and exchange gateway
Latency budget, co-location, kernel bypass and efficient order book data structures
Exchange connectivity: the FIX protocol, market data feeds and sequence handling
Testing: deterministic replay, simulation, paper trading and staged roll-out
Monitoring, logging, failover and recovery for unattended systems

syllabus.title: Risk controls, regulation and project
topics: Pre-trade risk checks: fat-finger limits, position and loss limits, and order-rate throttles
Kill switches, circuit breakers, and lessons from an automated trading failure
Regulation of algorithmic trading: market abuse, spoofing and layering, and Ghana securities rules
Ethics, market fairness and systemic risk: flash crashes and herding
Project: research, backtest and risk-review a strategy, with a written model-validation report

courses.title: Applied Analytics Practicum
topics: Scoping an analytics problem with a client
Data access, governance and ethics approval
Exploratory analysis and baseline models
Iterative modelling and validation
Communicating findings to decision makers
Deployment hand-over and monitoring plan
Final report and stakeholder presentation
courses.description: A capstone practicum in which teams carry an analytics problem for a real or realistic client from scoping to deployment hand-over. Students rehearse every stage in the lab with client scenarios, data pipelines and models, then deliver a final report and a stakeholder presentation.
modelledOn: CRISP-DM 1.0: Step-by-step data mining guide
Provost and Fawcett, Data Science for Business
Sculley et al., Hidden Technical Debt in Machine Learning Systems
Data Protection Act, 2012 (Act 843) of Ghana and the guidance of the Data Protection Commission
outcomes: Translate a client's business need into a scoped analytics question with success metrics, risks and a project plan.
Assess data access, quality, privacy and ethics requirements and build a documented, lawful data pipeline.
Develop baseline and improved models with leakage-free evaluation designed around the client's costs.
Audit models for subgroup performance, uncertainty and interpretability before recommending action.
Communicate findings to technical and non-technical decision makers in writing and in a live presentation.
Plan deployment hand-over, monitoring and retraining so the client can operate the solution.

syllabus.title: Scoping an analytics problem with a client
topics: Eliciting needs: turning a business question into an analytics question and agreeing what a decision will look like
Success metrics, baselines, feasibility and cost-benefit of the proposed analysis
Project charter, scope boundaries, assumptions, risks and the stakeholder map
Team roles, working agreements and a reproducible repository with version control
Planning the term: work breakdown, Gantt chart, milestones and sprint cadence

syllabus.title: Data access, governance and ethics
topics: Data inventory, data sharing agreements and negotiating access with the data owner
Ghana Data Protection Act principles, lawful basis and consent; anonymisation, pseudonymisation and k-anonymity
Ethics review: risk-benefit assessment, vulnerable groups and community consent
Data quality audit: missingness, collection bias, provenance and a data dictionary
Building the data pipeline in SQL: staging, cleaning, joining and lineage documentation
Secure handling: encryption, access control, audit logs and retention policy

syllabus.title: Exploratory analysis and baseline models
topics: Profiling and exploratory analysis: distributions, segments and sanity checks against domain knowledge
Feature engineering and avoiding target leakage
Baseline models: client heuristics, regression and shallow trees, and the benchmark they set
Evaluation design: temporal and spatial splits and metrics aligned to the client's costs
Mid-project review: presenting early findings and re-scoping with the client

syllabus.title: Iterative modelling and validation
topics: Model iteration: feature sets, tuning, ensembles and a disciplined experiment log
Validation: cross-validation, temporal backtesting and calibration of predicted probabilities
Fairness and subgroup performance audits across region, gender and income group
Error analysis, uncertainty quantification and sensitivity to assumptions
Interpretability for stakeholders: feature importance, partial dependence and case-level explanations
Decision-focused evaluation: cost matrices, expected value and planning an A/B pilot

syllabus.title: Communicating findings to decision makers
topics: Narrative structure for different audiences: board, programme officers and field staff
Visual design for decisions: dashboards, uncertainty displays and avoiding misleading charts
Writing the executive summary and the technical appendix
Handling disagreement and stating limitations without losing credibility

syllabus.title: Deployment hand-over and monitoring
topics: Deployment options: batch scoring, API and dashboard, and fitting into workflows with weak connectivity
Packaging for hand-over: environment capture, containers, documentation and a model card
Monitoring: data drift, performance decay, alerts and retraining triggers
Operating cost, support, runbooks and training of client staff
Post-deployment evaluation and tracking benefits against the original success metrics

syllabus.title: Final report and stakeholder presentation
topics: Structure of the final report: problem, data, methods, results, recommendations and limitations
The reproducibility package: code, data access notes, environment and a one-command rebuild
Presentation rehearsal, anticipating questions and handling live Q&A
Reflection, peer assessment and lessons learned for the next team
Professional practice: reporting negative or inconclusive results honestly

courses.title: Applied Cryptography
topics: Block and stream ciphers
Hash functions and MACs
Public-key encryption and signatures
Key exchange and PKI
Authenticated encryption
Cryptographic protocol design
Common implementation failures
courses.description: How modern cryptographic primitives are built, combined into protocols, and broken when used badly. In the lab students implement ciphers, hashes, signatures and key exchanges at toy scale, mount real attacks on flawed designs, and review the cryptography of a mobile-money style system.
modelledOn: Boneh and Shoup, A Graduate Course in Applied Cryptography
Ferguson, Schneier and Kohno, Cryptography Engineering
Katz and Lindell, Introduction to Modern Cryptography
NIST Special Publications 800-57 and 800-131A (key management and algorithm transitions)
outcomes: State and use security definitions such as IND-CPA, IND-CCA and unforgeability, and reason about concrete security levels.
Implement and attack block-cipher modes, MACs, hashes and public-key schemes at toy parameters.
Select authenticated encryption, key exchange and signature schemes and justify their parameters.
Analyse an authentication or key-exchange protocol and find replay, reflection and man-in-the-middle attacks.
Identify and exploit common implementation failures such as nonce reuse, weak randomness and timing leaks.
Produce a cryptographic design review that maps controls to a threat model and to applicable standards and law.

syllabus.title: Security definitions and mathematical toolkit
topics: Threat models, Kerckhoffs's principle, computational security and negligible functions
Security games: IND-CPA, IND-CCA2, EUF-CMA and PRF/PRP distinguishing advantage
Randomness: CSPRNGs, entropy sources, nonces versus IVs and the birthday bound
Number theory toolkit: modular arithmetic, extended Euclid, CRT, Fermat and Euler, Miller-Rabin primality testing
Reductions, concrete security and security levels in bits

syllabus.title: Block and stream ciphers
topics: Feistel and substitution-permutation designs; AES rounds, GF(2^8) arithmetic and key schedule
Modes of operation: ECB, CBC, CTR and XTS; padding and why ECB leaks
Stream ciphers: LFSRs, RC4 biases, ChaCha20 and keystream reuse
Cryptanalysis: differential and linear cryptanalysis, meet-in-the-middle and double encryption
CBC malleability and padding-oracle attacks

syllabus.title: Hash functions and MACs
topics: Preimage, second-preimage and collision resistance; birthday attacks; Merkle-Damgard and length extension
SHA-2 and the SHA-3 sponge construction
HMAC, CMAC and Poly1305; forgeries and constant-time tag comparison
Password hashing and key derivation: PBKDF2, bcrypt, scrypt, Argon2 and HKDF
Merkle trees, hash chains and commitments, with a mobile-money ledger as example

syllabus.title: Public-key encryption and signatures
topics: RSA: key generation, textbook weaknesses, OAEP and PSS padding, small-exponent and common-modulus attacks
Discrete logarithm groups: Diffie-Hellman, ElGamal and generic attacks such as baby-step giant-step
Elliptic curves: group law, ECDH, X25519, ECDSA, EdDSA and the danger of nonce reuse
Digital signatures: security notions, hash-then-sign and Schnorr signatures
Post-quantum cryptography: the effect of Shor's algorithm, lattice-based key encapsulation and hash-based signatures
Hybrid encryption and the KEM/DEM paradigm

syllabus.title: Key exchange and public-key infrastructure
topics: Authenticated key exchange, forward secrecy and ratcheting ideas
X.509 certificates, chains of trust, revocation (CRL, OCSP) and certificate transparency
Trust models and key management: trust on first use, HSMs, rotation and threshold secret sharing
The TLS 1.3 handshake and key schedule
Password-authenticated key exchange: SRP and the idea of OPAQUE

syllabus.title: Authenticated encryption
topics: Composition: encrypt-then-MAC, MAC-then-encrypt and encrypt-and-MAC
AEAD interfaces and schemes: AES-GCM, ChaCha20-Poly1305 and CCM; associated data
Nonce misuse and misuse-resistant modes (SIV)
Encrypting stored data: disk and database encryption, format-preserving encryption and tokenisation of card numbers
Envelope encryption, key wrapping and cloud key management services

syllabus.title: Cryptographic protocol design
topics: Building blocks: nonces, timestamps, challenge-response and replay protection
Classic protocol attacks: reflection, man-in-the-middle and the Needham-Schroeder public-key flaw
Formal analysis: symbolic models, attack traces and computational proofs
Zero-knowledge proofs: Schnorr identification, the Fiat-Shamir transform and commitments
Authentication in practice: HOTP and TOTP, end-to-end messaging, and PIN protection in USSD and SMS mobile-money flows
Secret sharing, threshold schemes and homomorphic tallying for e-voting

syllabus.title: Common implementation failures
topics: Side channels: timing, cache and power; constant-time programming
Randomness failures: weak generators, repeated nonces and RSA keys sharing a prime (batch GCD)
API and design misuse: ECB, static IVs, hard-coded keys, homemade ciphers, downgrade attacks and compression oracles
Using high-level libraries and misuse-resistant APIs; crypto agility
Case studies of real failures: root cause through design, code and process
Auditing cryptographic code: known-answer tests, negative tests and fuzzing

syllabus.title: Standards, review and project
topics: Threat model and primitive selection for a complete system
Parameter choice and the key lifecycle: generation, storage, rotation, revocation and destruction
Standards and law: NIST guidance, FIPS 140, PCI DSS and the Ghana Data Protection Act
Writing and presenting a cryptographic design review

courses.title: Asset Pricing and Derivatives
topics: State prices and arbitrage
Risk-neutral pricing and replication
Equilibrium asset pricing models
Forwards, futures and swaps
Option pricing in discrete and continuous time
Interest-rate and credit derivatives
Numerical pricing methods
courses.description: The theory and numerics of pricing financial claims: no-arbitrage and state prices, equilibrium models, forwards and swaps, options in discrete and continuous time, interest-rate and credit derivatives, and numerical methods. Students derive prices analytically, then verify and extend them with simulation, trees and finite-difference code in the lab.
modelledOn: Hull, Options, Futures and Other Derivatives
Shreve, Stochastic Calculus for Finance I and II
Cochrane, Asset Pricing
Glasserman, Monte Carlo Methods in Financial Engineering
outcomes: Derive prices from the no-arbitrage principle using state prices, replication and risk-neutral measures.
Explain and test equilibrium pricing models, from the CAPM to multi-factor models, against data.
Price and hedge forwards, futures, swaps and options in binomial and Black-Scholes frameworks and compute the Greeks.
Build and compare interest-rate and credit models and use them to value caps, swaptions and credit default swaps.
Implement Monte Carlo, finite-difference and Fourier pricing methods and quantify their numerical error.
Assess model risk by calibrating models to market quotes and testing hedging performance.

syllabus.title: One-period markets and state prices
topics: Securities, payoffs and portfolios; complete and incomplete markets
No-arbitrage and the law of one price; detecting arbitrage with linear programming
State prices and the fundamental theorem of asset pricing in one period
The stochastic discount factor and the pricing kernel
Risk-neutral probabilities, replication, uniqueness and market completeness

syllabus.title: Portfolio theory and equilibrium asset pricing
topics: Mean-variance portfolio choice, the efficient frontier and the two-fund theorem
The CAPM: derivation, the security market line and beta estimation
Expected utility, risk aversion and consumption-based pricing; the equity premium puzzle
Multi-factor models: APT, Fama-French factors and cross-sectional tests
Market efficiency and behavioural critiques; evidence from frontier markets such as the Ghana Stock Exchange

syllabus.title: Forwards, futures, bonds and swaps
topics: Cost-of-carry forward pricing with storage costs and convenience yield; cocoa and gold forwards
Futures versus forwards: margining, marking to market, basis risk and the minimum-variance hedge ratio
Bonds and the yield curve: bootstrapping, forward rates, duration and convexity
Interest-rate and currency swaps priced as bond portfolios; hedging cedi exposure
Foreign exchange forwards and covered interest parity

syllabus.title: Options in discrete time
topics: Option payoffs and strategies, put-call parity and no-arbitrage bounds
One-period binomial replication and risk-neutral valuation
Multi-period Cox-Ross-Rubinstein trees and American options with early exercise
Convergence of the binomial model to Black-Scholes and discrete delta hedging
Trinomial trees and implied trees

syllabus.title: Option pricing in continuous time
topics: Brownian motion, geometric Brownian motion, the Ito integral and Ito's lemma
The Black-Scholes PDE by delta hedging and the Black-Scholes formula
Risk-neutral measure, Girsanov's theorem, Feynman-Kac and change of numeraire
The Greeks: delta, gamma, vega, theta and rho; delta-gamma hedging and hedging error
Implied volatility, the smile and skew; local volatility and the Heston stochastic volatility model
Exotic options: barrier, Asian and lookback payoffs

syllabus.title: Interest-rate and credit derivatives
topics: Short-rate models: Vasicek, CIR and Hull-White; affine bond pricing
The HJM framework and market models; caps, floors and swaptions priced with Black's formula
Credit risk: the Merton structural model and reduced-form intensity models
Credit default swap pricing and bootstrapping hazard rates from spreads
Counterparty risk: credit valuation adjustment and collateral; pricing sovereign Eurobonds

syllabus.title: Numerical pricing methods
topics: Monte Carlo pricing and variance reduction: antithetic and control variates; standard errors
Pathwise and likelihood-ratio Greeks; the Longstaff-Schwartz method for American options
Finite-difference schemes: explicit, implicit and Crank-Nicolson; stability and boundary conditions
Fourier methods: characteristic functions, the Carr-Madan formula and FFT pricing
Calibration and model risk: least-squares fitting to quotes and hedging performance backtests

syllabus.title: Project and market practice
topics: Comparing pricing frameworks: when each model fails and what it assumes
Project: price and hedge a structured product, such as a cocoa-linked note with a protective floor
Critical reading of a derivatives pricing paper and its model risk discussion
Market structure and regulation: central clearing, margin rules, Basel treatment and derivative market development in Africa

courses.title: Character Animation and Crowd Simulation
topics: Skeletal animation and skinning
Inverse kinematics
Motion capture data and retargeting
Animation blending and state machines
Physics-based character control
Crowd steering and flocking models
Evaluating believability
courses.description: The mathematics and algorithms behind moving characters and crowds in games and film: skeletal animation, inverse kinematics, captured motion, blending, physics-based control and large-scale crowd models. Students implement each method in the lab, plot the results and judge how believable the motion looks.
modelledOn: Parent, Computer Animation: Algorithms and Techniques
Lengyel, Mathematics for 3D Game Programming and Computer Graphics
Thalmann and Musse, Crowd Simulation
Millington, Artificial Intelligence for Games (movement chapters)
outcomes: Represent poses with quaternions and transform hierarchies, and skin a mesh to a skeleton with linear blend and dual quaternion methods.
Solve inverse kinematics problems with analytic, CCD, FABRIK and Jacobian methods and compare convergence and quality.
Clean, retarget and blend captured motion and combine clips with state machines and blend spaces.
Build a simple physics-based character controller with proportional-derivative joint control and balance reasoning.
Simulate crowds with flocking, velocity obstacles and social force models and relate them to measured pedestrian flow.
Design and run an evaluation of the believability of generated motion using objective metrics and a small perceptual study.

syllabus.title: Skeletal animation and skinning
topics: Rotations in animation: Euler angles, gimbal lock, quaternions and spherical linear interpolation
Skeleton hierarchies, bind pose and forward kinematics with local and world transforms
Linear blend skinning, skinning weights and the candy-wrapper artefact
Dual quaternion skinning and corrective blend shapes
Keyframes and curves: linear, Catmull-Rom and Bezier interpolation, easing and curve editing

syllabus.title: Inverse kinematics
topics: Analytic two-bone IK for arms and legs using the law of cosines
Cyclic coordinate descent and its convergence behaviour
FABRIK: forward and backward reaching for chains
Jacobian methods: pseudo-inverse, damped least squares and singularities
Joint limits, constraints, foot placement on uneven ground and look-at IK

syllabus.title: Motion capture data and retargeting
topics: Capture technologies: marker-based optical, inertial suits and single-camera pose estimation from phone video
BVH and similar file formats; cleaning noise, filtering and gap filling
Retargeting motion between skeletons of different proportions
Time alignment and dynamic time warping of clips; motion editing
Root motion extraction and removing foot-skate

syllabus.title: Animation blending and state machines
topics: Linear blending, additive animation and masks for upper and lower body
Blend trees and two-dimensional blend spaces for locomotion
Animation state machines, transitions, layers and cross-fades
Motion graphs and motion matching for responsive locomotion
Inertialisation and transition smoothing without cross-fade cost

syllabus.title: Physics-based character control
topics: Rigid body dynamics for articulated figures; ragdolls and joint constraints
Proportional-derivative control of joints; gain tuning and stability
Balance: inverted pendulum models, centre of pressure and zero-moment point
Active ragdolls, hit reactions and blending between kinematic and simulated motion
Learning controllers: trajectory optimisation and reinforcement learning to imitate motion clips

syllabus.title: Crowd steering and flocking models
topics: Boids: separation, alignment and cohesion; emergent flocking
Steering behaviours: seek, arrive, pursue, wander, obstacle avoidance and path following
Velocity obstacles, reciprocal velocity obstacles and ORCA collision avoidance
Social force model and its parameters
Navigation for crowds: navigation meshes, flow fields and potential fields

syllabus.title: Crowd scale, density and behaviour
topics: Pedestrian dynamics: fundamental diagram, lane formation, bottlenecks and stop-and-go waves
Spatial hashing and parallel update for tens of thousands of agents
Rendering crowds: GPU skinning, instancing, level of detail and impostors
Group behaviour, roles and goals; emergency evacuation of a market or stadium
Calibrating a crowd model against video-derived trajectories

syllabus.title: Evaluating believability and project
topics: Perceptual factors in motion: the uncanny valley, foot-skate visibility and timing thresholds
Objective motion metrics: pose error, jerk, smoothness, energy and collision counts
Designing a perceptual user study: stimuli, controls, rating scales and significance tests
Ablation and comparison of methods; reporting results with confidence intervals
Project: a character locomotion system plus a crowd scene, with an evaluation report

courses.title: Clinical Research Informatics and Real-World Data
topics: Clinical trial data management
Observational databases and common data models
Cohort discovery and phenotyping
Electronic health record data re-use
Data warehouses and data lakes for health
Registries, biobanks and linkage
Privacy-preserving analysis and data governance
courses.description: The information systems, data models and governance that turn clinical trials, health records, registries and biobanks into evidence. Students design trial databases, map routine data into a common data model, define patient cohorts in SQL, link records, and weigh privacy decisions in realistic cases.
modelledOn: Richesson and Andrews, Clinical Research Informatics
Observational Health Data Sciences and Informatics, The Book of OHDSI
ICH E6 Good Clinical Practice guideline and CDISC standards documentation
Hernan and Robins, Causal Inference: What If
outcomes: Design the data capture, validation and standards pipeline for a clinical trial.
Transform routine health data into a common data model and assess its quality and fitness for a research question.
Define and validate computable phenotypes and cohorts from structured data and clinical text.
Build warehouse and lake structures for health data, and link records across sources while measuring linkage error.
Apply de-identification, differential privacy and federated analysis, and judge consent and governance arrangements.
Plan an observational study from question to analysis plan, naming its main biases.

syllabus.title: Clinical trial data management
topics: Trial phases and designs: parallel, cluster and stepped-wedge randomised trials
Protocols, eligibility criteria and case report form design
Electronic data capture, data dictionaries and edit checks
CDISC standards: CDASH, SDTM and ADaM datasets
Data cleaning, query management, audit trails and Good Clinical Practice
Randomisation, blinding and safety reporting systems

syllabus.title: Observational databases and common data models
topics: Observational designs: cohort, case-control and self-controlled studies
Bias and confounding: selection, information bias and confounding by indication
The OMOP common data model: person, visit, condition, drug and measurement tables
Extract-transform-load into a common data model; vocabulary mapping (ICD-10, SNOMED CT, LOINC, RxNorm)
Data quality assessment: completeness, plausibility and conformance checks
Distributed research networks and federated queries

syllabus.title: Cohort discovery and phenotyping
topics: Cohort definitions: inclusion, exclusion, index date and observation windows
Rule-based computable phenotypes from diagnoses, labs and drugs
Machine-learning phenotyping and weak labels
Clinical text mining: concept extraction, negation and temporality
Phenotype validation: chart review, sensitivity and positive predictive value
Temporal and sequence phenotypes; disease progression patterns

syllabus.title: Electronic health record data re-use
topics: What a record contains and what it omits: coverage, coding practice and workflow effects
Missing data and informative observation
Longitudinal events, time series and irregular sampling
Linking diagnoses, laboratory results and medicines across tables
Secondary use and the learning health system
Routine facility data in low-resource settings: completeness and timeliness

syllabus.title: Data warehouses and data lakes for health
topics: Star schema design for clinical data: facts, dimensions and slowly changing attributes
Warehouse, data lake and lakehouse compared
ETL and ELT pipelines, lineage and provenance
Query performance: indexes, partitions and materialised views
FHIR bulk export and bridging between standards and analytic tables
Data catalogues, metadata and the FAIR principles

syllabus.title: Registries, biobanks and linkage
topics: Disease registries: design, case ascertainment and completeness
Biobanks: consent, sample metadata and access
Record linkage: deterministic matching and probabilistic match weights
Linkage error and its effect on bias
Linking clinical and genomic data

syllabus.title: Privacy-preserving analysis and data governance
topics: De-identification: identifiers, safe-harbour style removal, expert determination and k-anonymity
Differential privacy: sensitivity, the Laplace mechanism and the privacy budget
Federated learning and secure multiparty computation for health data
Consent models: broad, dynamic and opt-out; data sharing agreements
Ghana Data Protection Act and cross-border transfer of health data
Trusted research environments and data access committees

syllabus.title: From question to study
topics: Turning a clinical question into an analysis plan on real-world data
Target trial emulation
Reporting standards for observational studies
Capstone: design and critique a real-world data study

courses.title: Computational Intelligence
topics: Evolutionary algorithms
Genetic programming
Swarm intelligence
Fuzzy systems
Artificial immune systems
Neuro-evolution
Multi-objective optimisation
courses.description: Nature-inspired and soft-computing methods for search, optimisation and learning: evolutionary algorithms, genetic programming, swarm intelligence, fuzzy systems, artificial immune systems, neuro-evolution and multi-objective optimisation. Students implement each method, visualise its search behaviour and compare algorithms with sound statistics on benchmark and African application problems.
modelledOn: Engelbrecht, Computational Intelligence: An Introduction
Eiben and Smith, Introduction to Evolutionary Computing
Poli, Langdon and McPhee, A Field Guide to Genetic Programming

courses.description: A graduate course on systems where computation, networks and physical processes are tightly coupled: hybrid models, real-time scheduling, sensing and control networks, safety, formal verification, security and edge-to-cloud deployment. courses.description: How organisations make data trustworthy, lawful and useful: governance structures, master data, quality, privacy law, records, metadata and the oversight of analytics models.
